text:
Simon Willison 最近的一篇博客引用了 Anthropic 工程师 Felix Rieseberg 的说明，解释了 Claude Code 的 Cowork 功能在架构上的一次重要转变。

旧架构里，模型在云端推理，但执行工具的 VM 跑在你的电脑上。合上笔记本，任务也就停了，还要吃本地磁盘、电池和性能。

现在模型和 VM 都搬到了云端，每个任务有独立 Sandbox。电脑更多变成一个本地资源入口，需要文件或设备能力时再通过桌面 App 调用。

现在你关掉电脑任务还能继续跑，同一个任务也能在桌面、Web 和手机之间接着做。

我们可以发现 Agent 的运行环境开始和用户设备解绑了。你的电脑逐渐变成它访问现实资源的端点，Agent 自己可以长期活在云端。

text:
卧槽，Manus 这轮融了5亿美金！？？？

刚刚，Manus 母公司蝴蝶效应正式宣布完成超过 5 亿美元的新一轮融资，由博裕投资、IDG 资本领投，老股东腾讯、红杉中国、真格基金继续加码。

之前彭博就报道过，Manus 正接近完成一笔 5 亿美元的融资，现在算是正式官宣了。

这个金额放在整个 AI Agent 创业赛道里，确实相当夸张（毕竟不是模型层）。

而且我觉得更值得关注的是投资人阵容。

博裕、IDG 领投，腾讯、红杉中国、真格继续跟进，基本上把国内最有代表性的几家投资机构凑齐了。

前几天 Manus 创始人还在聊，要让 Manus 从一个 Agent 逐渐变成一台 AI 电脑。

现在这么大一笔融资落地，显然有更多资源去推进这个方向了。

说实话，我一直觉得 Agent 这个赛道挺有意思的。

过去一年，大家一直在争论 Agent 到底能不能成为一个独立的产品品类，还是最终会被 OpenAI、Anthropic 这些基础模型公司直接吃掉。

但现在，Manus 已经实实在在地融到了超过 5 亿美元。

资本至少已经用真金白银投出了一票。

接下来就看 Manus 能不能把这笔钱真正变成产品能力，以及 Agent 到底能走多远了。

🔵Metis 推出 Rise 月度开发者激励计划，以奖励在 Andromeda 主网部署 AI Agent 的团队

以太坊 L2 网络 @MetisL2  推出 Metis Rise 月度开发者激励计划，以奖励在 Metis Andromeda 主网上部署新 AI Agent、获取真实用户并产生真实链上经济活动的团队。

该计划关注 AI Agent 的「经济可用性」，涉及支付（x402）、身份（ERC-8004）、稳定币托管（Escrow）和可独立验证的链上签名回执四类需求。

该计划支持任意 AI Agent 框架与托管方式，包括 ClawUp、GOAT AgentKit 或自建后端，并支持基于 GOAT Network 的双链架构。

开发者需每月满足以下条件：有效月活用户不少于 15 个、每个计入的用户需在 Metis Andromeda 上完成至少 3 笔合格交易或结算金额不低于 2 美元（m.USDC、m.USDT 或 METIS）、主要用户交易、结算量与 Gas 消耗需发生在 Metis Andromeda 主网。

同时 Metis 正在构建面向 AI Agent 的执行与数据层，Andromeda 的去中心化排序器（DSeq）可消除 Agent 间无需信任的交易所依赖的单点故障。

Metis Rise 由 Metis 主办，ClawUp、GOAT Network 和 LazAI 为生态合作伙伴。

AI agent compute infrastructure project.

The core is to provide AI agents with intelligent model routing + proprietary GPU fallback + parallel batch processing.

It mainly solves several pain points agents face when actually running tasks: top-tier models can easily hit rate limits or run out of credits, causing tasks to get stuck; simple tasks still being handled by expensive models wastes money; batch workloads can only be processed sequentially, leaving the agent waiting; and without backup compute, the task simply fails.

Darwin is essentially an API placed in front of all the models a user has. It accepts requests in OpenAI or Anthropic format, uses rules to determine the difficulty of the task, and then routes it to the cheapest model in the user’s list that is capable of handling it.

When the budget is running low or a model hits its rate limit, simple requests automatically fall back to cheaper models. When all models are unavailable, the request falls back to Darwin’s own GPU models instead of simply returning an error. It also supports an MCP server, allowing agents to directly call Darwin as a tool.

It does not store users’ prompts or responses. It only records the model, token count, cost, and latency.

It’s basically like an intelligent load balancer + CDN + backup generator in the real world. You connect the agent’s “power meter” to it, and it automatically sends heavy workloads to large models, light workloads to smaller models, switches routes when a model is under capacity constraints, and uses its own generators when everything else is unavailable. The Swarm feature is like handing a pile of individual packages to a parallel processing center: submit them all at once, process them simultaneously, then aggregate and return the results.

The DARWIN token is used through a burn-to-credit mechanism: burning 1 million DARWIN gives you 5 credits. These credits are used to pay for calls to Darwin’s own GPUs and upgrades.

There are no subscriptions or card payments—everything is accounted for purely through on-chain burns.

The official team previously stated that around 52 million tokens had been burned, and that the developer allocation had also been burned. The price went up because Kyle Samani tweeted about the project, while the subsequent decline also happened because Kyle Samani deleted the tweet mentioning Darwin.

author: ycombinator
quoted_text:
Every AI data center needs power, and every power plant needs a step-up transformer to connect to the grid. If you ordered one in 2021, it arrived in under 500 days. Today it takes more than 1,120 days.

A large transformer core is made of grain-oriented electrical steel that spends about five days in a 1,200°C annealing furnace. Only one US company makes that steel: Cleveland-Cliffs.

Inside a bell annealing furnace, coils of iron with about 3% silicon stand on end in hydrogen while the furnace heats them about 15 to 20°C an hour. It takes two to three days to reach 1,200°C. As the coils heat up, tiny particles that pin the grains in place slowly dissolve, and about one grain in a million starts growing and swallows its neighbors. Then the coils sit at 1,200°C for 20 to 40 hours. Grains that started 0.01 mm across end up 10 mm wide, nearly all pointing the same way. That alignment cuts the power a transformer core loses as heat.

Cleveland-Cliffs can supply about 12 to 20% of what the US needs, by DOE's estimate. China was in a similar spot before 2000: its only volume producer covered 30% of demand. The few foreign companies that could make the high-grade version refused to license their process. Baosteel spent ten years on research and made its first good coil in 2008. By 2013 it could make 300,000 tons a year, three times what all of China made before 2000.

I build chemical plants. If you're in hard-tech, chances are you are now competing with AI data centers for the same grid equipment.

author: DeeZe
quoted_text:
After my foray into lands afar (Solana), and my first exposure in years to trench warfare (DeFi summer was quite similar to now), some thoughts.

I thought we could bring back hold culture bc, ideally, I think everyone prefers to WAGMI vs. whatever the fuck this is now, and I saw tribes forming around bags.

I was wrong ab this. Holding will continue to exist in isolated pockets, but the attention span of zoomers (and millennials too these days, if we’re being honest) is at record lows.

This is expert mode.

Everyone has superintelligence at their disposal, especially the bad guys.

Everything is bundled, especially the good shit.

Everything is fast… Like unbelievably fast. The tech, the cycles, the rotations, the coin creations… Fast.

This generation of traders is vicious. Many lack any technical charting ability and trade on vibes alone… And in trading, the vibes are shifting constantly.

Something that’s hot one week may have ZERO attention the next.

FOMO is way more powerful than people realize… He who controls the flows controls the universe.

Social trading at this level of transparency is novel and has many consequences in terms of reflexivity.

I think main characters rotate quickly bc they are under immense pressure not to sell whatever has kingmade them, and cycles haven’t magically stopped playing out.

I still think holding comes back to some extent as the cycle matures, and once again, some things are definitely worth holding. Most things aren’t.

It’s the perfect environment to take your initials out after 2–3x and buy another lottery ticket or put cash to the side for TBD.

You have to be extremely aggressive with profit-taking bc standing liquidity is thinner than ever, so the only way to be efficient is to take advantage of volume events.

And you have to be extremely diversified bc most bags are prob farms that just go to zero.

Reflecting on my recent performance, I think it’s better than some (I didn’t miss the Solana rotation), but I’ve definitely left a lot on the table by not being as mechanical ab this as I should have been.

It’s funny how one can do this his entire adult life and the game never gets old. It’s the same game I’ve been playing for years, just with thousands of badass expansion packs.

This is the most dangerous and hardest trading environment I’ve ever witnessed, but it’s also one of the most stimulating.

See you in the trenches, cousins.

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

author: mert
quoted_text:
Do the labs have better algorithms for breaking crypto?

Independent of the answer, the most important thing is to have crypto agility. Zcash has proven this, with 3 upgrades happening in 6 months, and Tachyon planned for January. The protocol design has plans for how to turn off features to enable safe protocol upgrades. This is what Quantum Recoverability is, and it applies equally well if there's a non-quantum ECDLP attack.

We're equipped on multiple fronts to protect against future bugs. In the next cryptography upgrade, coming January, already slated features are:
- PQ transparent
- Switching to Tachyon

What people don't realize about Tachyon is it switches us to R1CS, and enables far more crypto agility away from elliptic curves. The nullifier derivation no longer depend on elliptic curves. We get far greater SNARK agility and can very quickly move to STARKs when any crisis comes.

Today's Zcash transparent UTXO's give a better security guarantee than an ETH address. @ZakuraZcash has solved the privacy and performance problem that were blocking rotating T-Addresses natively in the wallet. This is done using PIR to fetch balances, and its already live in Vizor. So its a short UX leap to get this backup plan.

In January, the Transparent pool will be upgraded to support hash based sigs, that can later be STARK aggregated.

Correction: for multisigs the ideal "safe" rule is that you want each signer to change their key after each operation.

(This is making an implicit assumption that ECDSA might become weak, but not to the point where any crack of it would be literally instant so you would literally have to worry about eg. in-mempool frontrunning)

You definitely still want to gather sigs offchain if possible, to minimize the number of hours between "sig revealed" and "key no longer active"

But again: it's very easy to lose funds from a misconfigured rushed upgrade, so ... don't rush anything.
author: VitalikButerin
quoted_text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

text:
Unlike many networks, Solana users don't need to go into "bunker mode" ahead of an accelerated quantum timeline or classical attack provided by AI.
 
Solana uses Ed25519, where each signing key is derived by hashing a secret seed. Breaking the curve, whether by a quantum computer or a classical attack, would expose the derived key, but not the seed, and seeds are never exposed onchain. With a one-time network upgrade, rightful owners could prove knowledge of their seed using a hash-based proof and move their accounts to a safe signature scheme. A working proof of concept already exists: https://t.co/am2ErkkomT.
 
Solana remains secure today and has a defined path forward.
author: solana
quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

Every one of these hopeless cases is responsible for consuming the entire local tax contribution of a couple dozen residents, citizens whose lifetime of labor paying into the commons is effectively wasted and redirected into the upkeep of a class of permanent dependents who need constant supervision to not harm themselves and others.

A lot of policing and incarceration questions are framed as freedom vs security trade offs affecting the liberties and dignity of common people, but the pressing questions of today are all "how should the 99% of us without severe behavioral deficits choose to deal with the tiny minority of people who cause almost all problems" which is not a question of common liberty.

It's more like an animal rights issue; a question of how we as a society rule with conscience over a helpless form of life that occasionally causes us harm, but otherwise poops wherever it wants because it's an animal, and could never join us no matter how nice we are to them.

text:
Do the labs have better algorithms for breaking crypto?

Independent of the answer, the most important thing is to have crypto agility. Zcash has proven this, with 3 upgrades happening in 6 months, and Tachyon planned for January. The protocol design has plans for how to turn off features to enable safe protocol upgrades. This is what Quantum Recoverability is, and it applies equally well if there's a non-quantum ECDLP attack.

We're equipped on multiple fronts to protect against future bugs. In the next cryptography upgrade, coming January, already slated features are:
- PQ transparent
- Switching to Tachyon

What people don't realize about Tachyon is it switches us to R1CS, and enables far more crypto agility away from elliptic curves. The nullifier derivation no longer depend on elliptic curves. We get far greater SNARK agility and can very quickly move to STARKs when any crisis comes.

Today's Zcash transparent UTXO's give a better security guarantee than an ETH address. @ZakuraZcash has solved the privacy and performance problem that were blocking rotating T-Addresses natively in the wallet. This is done using PIR to fetch balances, and its already live in Vizor. So its a short UX leap to get this backup plan.

In January, the Transparent pool will be upgraded to support hash based sigs, that can later be STARK aggregated.

I’m extremely sad to announce that Abstract is shutting down.

When we were just a three-person team building Frame I never could have imagined the two and half year journey I was about to embark on.

From the tireless nights preparing for launch, to mainnet going live in January 2025, and everything in between, this journey is one I will treasure for the rest of my life. Even though the outcome is not what we wanted, I am incredibly proud of everything we built at Abstract.

The Portal and Abstract Global Wallet made interacting with a blockchain feel seamless. That foundation led to a wave of unique apps, novel onchain experiences, and, most importantly, an incredibly passionate community that gave Abstract an identity and culture of its own.

But the truth is that the industry has changed significantly since the idea was first conceived in the summer of 2024, and Abstract was facing difficulties with our DeFi Ecosystem and liquidity on the chain.

We reached a crossroads of experiencing significant growth, but not having cemented product-market-fit,and that was becoming an issue from a business sustainability perspective.

A very difficult decision needed to be made. Abstract’s growth had stalled and the chain was simply not economically sustainable anymore despite our best efforts.

I am extremely grateful to the Igloo, Inc team who truly gave it their all to explore every angle and make Abstract work.

I want to take this time to thank the incredibly talented team I had the pleasure of working with over the last three years. Every single one of them poured their heart and soul into Abstract and together we created something truly special that pushed forward what onchain discovery and experiences could look like. It is the best team that I have ever worked with. I will always be proud of that.

I want to thank all of our partners and builders that worked with us to make Abstract such a unique, special place. Truly some of the most talented developers launched on Abstract and I know you will all kill it in your next chapter.

Most of all I want to thank the Abstract community for the support over these three years. I know there have been moments of frustration, but your passion and admiration for Abstract are what made it so special and helped create a culture that is incredibly rare in crypto. I truly wish this could have worked out for all of us.

Thank you for supporting the green chain ✳️

text:
卧槽，当年轰动国内 AI 圈的“字节投毒实习生”田柯宇，现在杀回来了！

刚刷到彭博今天专门发了一篇对他的采访。

田柯宇 @keyutian  现在自己出来创业做世界模型，公司甚至还没有正式名字、没有产品，只有 10 个人，却已经从五源资本、IDG 等机构融了接近 3000 万美元，投后估值接近 2 亿美元。

而且这哥们现在做的东西还挺有意思。

简单来说，他觉得：人类的语言其实根本不适合描述这个世界。

比如你想用文字完整描述一段视频，里面每一个物体的位置、运动、光影、物理变化，基本是不可能的。

所以他的思路是，干脆别让 AI 使用人类语言理解视频了。

他们直接让 AI 自己发明一门语言。

他们现在已经做出了一套类似词典的东西，里面大概有 20 万个符号，人类完全看不懂，但 AI 可以拿这些符号去表示、压缩和预测视频。

接下来他们准备喂进去大约 1 亿小时的视频，让模型通过这套自己的语言去学习现实世界。

最终目标不是视频生成，不是World Model，是希望做一个基座模型：

让 AI 真正理解空间、运动和物理规律，未来可以作为机器人、自动驾驶、交互式视频这些东西的基础模型。

田柯宇说，这套方法目前已经能让视频生成效率提升至少一个数量级。

他们计划先做公开 Demo，甚至是直播，完整模型则准备在 2027 年发布。

现阶段不着急做消费级产品，也暂时不考虑怎么商业化，就是先怼基座模型。

田柯宇这个人，我其实之前就写过。

他离开字节之后，他还作为一作拿了 NeurIPS 2024 Best Paper。

那篇论文我当时专门看过，我印象特别深，因为它做的事情其实很暴力：就是想办法把视觉生成这件事，变得更像 LLM 一样，可以不断 Scaling，同时把生成成本和复杂度往下降。

我当时看完就觉得，这个人能力是真的很牛逼。

所以后来网上一直在讨论他当年在字节的事情，我其实也一直挺好奇到底发生了什么。

因为当时中文互联网传得特别夸张，什么“投毒大模型”、造成几百万甚至八百万损失，各种版本都有，已经快传成 AI 圈都市传说了hhhh

结果这次彭博终于把很多以前不知道的细节补出来了。

田柯宇自己承认，当时他为了释放算力，直接关掉了另一个实习生超额占用计算资源的程序，他现在也觉得当时这种“以火攻火”的处理方式是错的。

但另一方面，字节当年其实也明确说过，网上关于他破坏基础模型训练的很多传言存在误导。

最后法院判下来的结果，是他因为违反合同赔偿 50 万人民币，把自己在字节拿到的工资全部退了回去

这个结果跟当年网上传的那些版本，差距还是挺大的。

所以我今天早上看到这篇采访还挺感慨的。

因为我最早认识田柯宇这个名字，不是因为这次创业，甚至也不完全是因为字节那件事，而是后来真的去看了他的论文。

当时我的感觉就是：这人确实是有东西的。

现在再看，他离开字节之后拿 Best Paper，继续沿着自己的技术路线做世界模型，然后一个 10 人团队、产品都还没有，就融了接近 3000 万美元，估值快 2 亿美元。

至少从技术能力这件事情上，我觉得之前那个判断没错。

这个人，确实挺牛逼的。

加油啊，等你们新的roadmap！

text:
今天，以太坊核心研究员 Justin Drake 发出了一个极度反常的呼吁：要求整个加密行业准备进入“掩体模式”（Bunker mode），并建议大户开始把资产转移到全新的地址里。

这个呼吁也得到了 Vitalik 的回复，似乎大家又陷入了一种对钱包安全的恐慌和思考里。

很多人的第一反应是，又有哪个超级黑客组织要洗劫公链了？

并不是。恐慌依然来自于 AI 的进步。

过去几周，OpenAI 的内部模型在短短几天内，解决了几百个困扰人类几十年的数学难题。这种“数学超级智能”的突然爆发，让密码学受到威胁。整个加密行业（包括 BTC 和 ETH）的底层安全，依靠 ECDSA 的数学加密算法。

既然 AI 的数学能力正在以恐怖的速度进化，它还需要多久能找到一条攻破 ECDSA 的“数学捷径”？

Justin Drake 给出的时间表是“几个月，而不是几年”。

这绝对不是危言耸听，目前仅比特币网络，就有超过 600 万枚 BTC（包括中本聪的远古钱包）因为曾经发送过交易，公钥正完全“裸奔”暴露在链上。

一旦底层数学锁被 AI 降维拆解，这些庞大的资产将毫无还手之力。

Vitalik 随后也发了长文回应。但他的表态不仅带来了一个更深层的坏消息，还附带了一个真实的黑色幽默。

更深层的坏消息是，行业原本准备用来防御量子计算机的“逃生舱”（比如格密码技术），因为同样带有复杂的数学结构，很可能在未来一两年内也被 AI 的数学能力彻底打穿。

但面对这个仿佛随时会落下的核弹，V 神却强烈建议大家，千万别慌慌张张去转移资产。

他的理由无比接地气：“我个人因为搞砸了钱包迁移所损失的钱，比我被黑客偷走的加起来还要多。”

所以，在防住黑客和 AI 前，更应该防住自己手残弄丢了助记词或者转错了地址。

如果你是巨鲸大户，且拥有极高的钱包管理能力，确实可以听取建议，把资金静静躺在“从未发过任何交易”的新地址里。因为只要不发交易，你的公钥就隐藏在哈希背后，AI 连攻击的靶子都找不到。

但对于绝大多数普通人来说，不要恐慌，不要瞎折腾。

你被自己爆破的概率，远大于被 AI 算力爆破的概率...

quoted_text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

quoted_text:
Huge congratulations to @NousResearch and team @dillonrolnick @Teknium @karan4d @theemozilla @gradyacc and many others on closing their $90M Series B at a $1.5B valuation. @Delphi_Ventures co-led their seed round, doubled down in their Series A, and participated again here. This marks us tripling down on Nous.

Following Nous' journey over the past few years has recalibrated my view of top tier founders

The team has always been months to years ahead at every juncture. They did synthetic model evaluations years before people got sick of benchmark maxing, distributed training runs before it was interesting, YARN to massively increase context length back when you couldn't dump endless text into LLMs and millions of downloads for their fine tuned Hermes Models. There were also a lot of fun projects along the way like WorldSim (massive world simulation) and FORGE.

Fast forward to today and there are 24M+ downloads of Hermes Agent since February, #1 among apps on OpenRouter by daily token usage, and 250,000+ GitHub stars along with just mass virality. The Nous team estimates Hermes drives approximately 2.5% of all global token usage.

Nous has created two things that I think are both foundational and sticky

First, Nous created a religion and an authentic cult like following. They achieved this through grassroots interest and involvement from their community and users, and by actually embracing them. A recurring example is Teknium replying to users at all hours of the day, working with them and integrating their pull requests into Hermes agent. The project’s ethos is open source and against a totalitarian end state where a room full of folks controls AI and reality itself, and that resonates globally.

The second reason is that Hermes agent unlocks a fundamental new spot on the AI optimization frontier as the open source non lab owned option. Every major competitor is owned by an AI lab (Muse owned by Meta, OpenClaw by OpenAI, Grok by SpaceX, Instinct which is closed source). With Hermes Agent you own everything you create around an AI model so you have that as a long term evolving asset (Business or personal) instead of getting IP farmed

Also with Hermes agent you can drive differentiated outcomes versus using the same model as everyone else. Individuals and businesses have a comprehensive set of owned depth around the model (Evaluations, memory, interactions, data, private IP, variety of open or closed or fine tuned models, and more). This lends itself to an AI agent that grows with you that you own for life. 

Both @satyanadella and @PalantirTech’s have shared this view that corporations don’t want to give away their IP anymore and be farmed. They want to own it as an asset.

I’ve shared my full thesis on this concept of owning vs renting your intelligence here: https://t.co/cW05wedLRD

Hermes Agent is not just a random spark, it’s the result of a team that has spent years building products, building systems and being fully enveloped in the AI world. The thousands of micro decisions and the culmination of the team led to Hermes Agent.

So what comes next? 

When you have tens of millions of users already, they can become the champions within a business to bring their Hermes build to all employees of a company. They can start sharing skills, interactions, interop, data and more and build something truly multiplayer for enterprise. 

Having Nvidia, Microsoft and Samsung as investors doubles as enabling them to be extremely smart in potentially onboarding a massive enterprise user base to Hermes Enterprise. This isn't just private businesses using Hermes internally; it's Fortune 500 companies who can offer customized and unique agents to their customers and users built on Hermes Enterprise. 

Hermes' agent was not built to be a casual or fleeting personal agent and this lends itself to a larger business expansion. 

As Teknium shared 

“I fully intend and have plainly stated many times that I always built hermes to be the most powerful AI Agent. "Normie" consumers can leverage that and we do what we can to make it an experience they can approach (the mobile app will be almost exclusively focused on consumer) - but they are not our only demographic. I want the scientists, the cybersecurity engineers, the developers, the knowledge workers, the creatives, and everyone else to be able to have an agent that they can leverage that is maximally useful to them too.…”

Nous has captured the hearts and minds of the smartest user base on earth and that's the wedge. 

Nous is building for a future where you have sovereignty over your AI stack. They are the center of gravity for Open source AI developers, users, investors and supporters. 

The AI discussion has been dominated by fear mongering driven by centralized labs to obtain a regulatory moat. This is very obvious. The safest path in my opinion is open source and acceleration. An entire world of agents pressure testing, building and dealing with each other aligned to the individual vs aligned to a centralized team of decision makers at a lab. Nous is the answer. Nous has now raised $158M to date to execute this vision.

Internally we have people who have built insane Hermes agent builds including @KSimback and @pierskicks. I have built an insanely deep Hermes build that takes in 40+ private and public data sources and finds me new founders to invest in, helps manage my liquid portfolio, and tracks my entire historical journey as a VC (past founders, deals, much more).

A few fun content items through the years has been our AMA with Teknium and our Podcast with Jeff 

AMA: https://t.co/XeeB8WdTEv

Podcast: https://t.co/wM6RQqHw94

Very excited for @robotventures (@tarunchitra and @rleshner) to lead the round alongside @nvidia @Microsoft @Samsung @usv (@fredwilson), @MenloVentures (@deedydas and team), @ycombinator and @1789Capital. Tarun is extremely deep on AI, inference (see his latest article) and open source and is the ideal lead investor in Nous.

Also amped for the Hermes Mobile App

Our goal at Delphi Ventures is to be the biggest supporters and investors of our portfolio companies. We are extremely excited for the future of Nous.

text:
AI 变成了推高利率的理由。
这两年的剧本是：AI 提效、压成本，帮美联储把通胀摁下去。昨晚公布的 9 月会议纪要，把剧本翻了过来。

1｜美联储把 AI 写进了通胀
9 月会议 12:0 全票加息 25 个基点，联邦基金利率到 3.75%–4.00%，2023 年 7 月以来第一次加息。点阵图里 18 名官员有 16 人认为，年底前可能还要再加一次。
纪要里讲 AI 的几句，大多站在通胀那一侧：核心商品涨价里，关税的影响在退，AI 建设的影响在涨；AI 推动的企业投资，规模和速度「持续超出预期」。
理事 Cook 更直白：数据中心在抢建筑工人和电，美国电费、水费一年涨了 5% 左右，部分可能跟 AI 有关。
而已经宣布的 AI 投资，才花掉一小部分。
火还没烧完。

2｜柴从哪来：借。而且债主开始挑食
AI 已经从烧现金流，转向大规模举债。
FT 披露，SpaceX $SPCX 寻求筹集约 400 亿美元采购英伟达 $NVDA 芯片，阿波罗 $APO 牵头，Pimco 也在谈。英伟达那边，8 月和 Apollo、贝莱德、黑石等签了备忘录，搭融资平台帮客户借钱买芯片，自己可以兜底最多 25%。
拿卡抵押借钱买卡，卖卡的再给买家兜底。
纪要转述市场评论，把 AI 基建的大量私人债务列为推高期限溢价和美债收益率的原因之一。
白话：AI 在跟美债抢钱，借得越久，债主要价越高。30 年美债冲到 5.7% 上下，2002 年 5 月以来最高。
债主也开始挑食。同样借 30 年：
- 谷歌 $GOOGL 约 6.7%
- Meta $META 约 7.4%
- SpaceX 约 7.9%
- 甲骨文 $ORCL 约 8.3%
Meta、SpaceX、甲骨文这几只，发行以来利差全部走阔。再往下是 CoreWeave：债的收益率约 13%，买 GPU 的贷款利差半年里从 SOFR（美元隔夜基准利率）+2.25% 涨到 +5.5%。
钱还在往里挤：昨晚 10 年期美债拍卖中标 5.3%，含海外买家的间接投标方拿走 80.3%。
钱不缺，缺的是便宜的钱。

3｜盘面已经开始分开算账
SpaceX 借钱买卡，按理该是英伟达的大单。结果 $NVDA 跌 0.74%，$SPCX 跌 2.51%；同一天美光 $MU 涨超 4%。
纪要还说，今年美股上涨全靠盈利，市盈率是下降的。
好消息不涨，是市场开始给 AI 的资金成本定价了。赚现钱的和借钱买卡的，分开算账。

4｜如果 AI 少借点钱呢

Do the labs have better algorithms for breaking crypto?

Independent of the answer, the most important thing is to have crypto agility. Zcash has proven this, with 3 upgrades happening in 6 months, and Tachyon planned for January. The protocol design has plans for how to turn off features to enable safe protocol upgrades. This is what Quantum Recoverability is, and it applies equally well if there's a non-quantum ECDLP attack.

We're equipped on multiple fronts to protect against future bugs. In the next cryptography upgrade, coming January, already slated features are:
- PQ transparent
- Switching to Tachyon

What people don't realize about Tachyon is it switches us to R1CS, and enables far more crypto agility away from elliptic curves. The nullifier derivation no longer depend on elliptic curves. We get far greater SNARK agility and can very quickly move to STARKs when any crisis comes.

Today's Zcash transparent UTXO's give a better security guarantee than an ETH address. @ZakuraZcash has solved the privacy and performance problem that were blocking rotating T-Addresses natively in the wallet. This is done using PIR to fetch balances, and its already live in Vizor. So its a short UX leap to get this backup plan.

In January, the Transparent pool will be upgraded to support hash based sigs, that can later be STARK aggregated.

author: satyaki44
quoted_text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

text:
Unlike many networks, Solana users don't need to go into "bunker mode" ahead of an accelerated quantum timeline or classical attack provided by AI.
 
Solana uses Ed25519, where each signing key is derived by hashing a secret seed. Breaking the curve, whether by a quantum computer or a classical attack, would expose the derived key, but not the seed, and seeds are never exposed onchain. With a one-time network upgrade, rightful owners could prove knowledge of their seed using a hash-based proof and move their accounts to a safe signature scheme. A working proof of concept already exists: https://t.co/am2ErkkomT.
 
Solana remains secure today and has a defined path forward.
author: jacobvcreech
quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. 💡Our view: RSI is a systems engineering problem, not just a model problem.

Progress depends on the environment a research agent works in: what resources it can call, what it can change, and how it runs experiments. That environment should reflect real production workflows and be easy for agents to use.

text:
We’ve been thinking about this problem / unbundling of marketplaces a lot in regards to exchanges recently.

I’ve been asking every exchange founder I’ve met in Singapore the same question:

Why would an agent like/prefer your exchange?

Right now, typical user behavior is to choose an exchange, like Binance, Robinhood, or Hyperliquid and commit to it. The fees exchanges charge on top is the premium for the consumers laziness to switch off exchanges (or the added price they’re willing to pay in exchange for trust or liquidity).

But an agent doesn’t have this same semblance of loyalty. It’s willing to look across every single exchange and factor in on/off-ramps, liquidity, interop costs, time-bounds of the trade, and everything within the known universe (including options a trader wouldn’t have looked at).

I’m willing to bet that by this point next year, 90% of informed market participants will enter into the market with an agent acting as their broker in regards to their best interests. 

This begs the question:
Is an agent’s financial decision matrix strictly quantitative or are there qualitative factors as well? Liquidity, fees, decentralization, trust, counter-party risk, etc.

Whichever exchange answers this properly and successfully aligns itself with the agents reward function will receive so much flow it will be madness.

Right now, I think Hyperliquid is positioned best to win this, but there are other realities that could exist as well.

text:
比尔阿克曼要打造第二个伯克希尔哈撒韦

最近他接受了彭博的采访，17分钟的采访里主要谈到了Howard Hughes、IPO 市场、Anthropic，以及个人医疗投资。

Howard Hughes Holdings（$HHH） Ackman 把 HHH 定位为长期复利机器，目标是在约 50 年内做成类似伯克希尔的公司，估值有望超过 1 万亿美元。他已通过 Pershing Square 取得控制权（此前约以每股 100 美元买入，采访前后股价约在 70 美元出头）。核心做法是：以约 21 亿美元收购保险公司 Vantage Group，卖掉其固定收益持仓、把浮存金和资本投向由 Pershing Square 管理的股票；同时把地产业务更多转向管理主规划社区（master-planned communities），通过出售地块给建商、持有商业地产等方式释放现金，再把现金流注入保险业务，扩大承保能力和投资规模。他预计地产端到 2030 年可贡献约 25 亿至 30 亿美元现金，并计划引入外部资本以提高回报。

IPO 市场 他认为当前市场高度集中在少数超大型 IPO（如 SpaceX、Anthropic）以及支撑 AI 的“镐与铲”类公司上，其他公司很难拿到理想估值，部分交易因此推迟或搁置。

Anthropic 他把 Anthropic 称为自己见过的“或许最伟大的商业故事之一”：从零起步、收入快速爬升（2025 年收入约 46 亿美元、同比大幅增长），Claude 产品质量高，Pershing Square 内部也在使用。同时他也指出，前沿模型公司能否长期维持份额，仍要面对开源和开放权重模型的竞争，且并未明确表示其基金会投资 Anthropic。

个人相关 他提到女儿 Lucy 今年早些时候因脑出血入院、昏迷后仍在康复，这促使他与妻子 Neri Oxman 承诺约 4 亿美元（外加 Pershing Square 股票）设立 Ackman Oxman Institute，聚焦脑科学研究、康复、脑机接口与长寿。

text:
以太坊的代币化基金的一周增量大约是 Stellar 的两倍，是第三名之后总和的近9倍。

前两名合计约占图中全部增量的 93%。

说明了三个事情：

一是，机构级代币化基金选链高度集中，不太跟零售链热度走。

这类资产主要是货币市场基金/美国国债基金/信贷基金。

发行方要的是合规、托管、结算和已有分发渠道，不是 TPS 或 meme 活跃度。

由此，Solana/Base/BNB Chain 在散户和 DeFi 上可以很热闹，在这类产品的周增量里几乎看不见。

Robinhood链也开始出现在榜单末尾，也说明券商自有链还没成为基金发行的主场。

二是，表面看是双寡头格局，但其实更多是单寡头。

以太坊是默认的机构发行与结算层：BlackRock BUIDL、Ondo、Superstate、部分 J.P. Morgan 产品等都在上面，这一周 +3.5 亿美元只是存量优势在继续放大。

Stellar 能居第二，不是生态叙事，主要是是 Franklin Templeton 的代币化货币基金（BENJI）长期以 Stellar 为主场，另外Sky、J.P. Morgan有少量试点，算不上机构多数认同

三是，继续强化以太坊作为 RWA 结算网络的位置，不过，不会自动变成 gas 费或 ETH 需求，短期内不会对ETH产生明显影响。如果资产达到更大规模级别（如数百亿/千亿美元以上），会对估值产生明显影响。

最后，L2 在这张图里几乎为零，也说明基金发行方目前仍把资产放在 L1，不是跟着应用层流动性走。

text:
Unlike many networks, Solana users don't need to go into "bunker mode" ahead of an accelerated quantum timeline or classical attack provided by AI.
 
Solana uses Ed25519, where each signing key is derived by hashing a secret seed. Breaking the curve, whether by a quantum computer or a classical attack, would expose the derived key, but not the seed, and seeds are never exposed onchain. With a one-time network upgrade, rightful owners could prove knowledge of their seed using a hash-based proof and move their accounts to a safe signature scheme. A working proof of concept already exists: https://t.co/am2ErkkomT.
 
Solana remains secure today and has a defined path forward.
author: Mawuko
quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
昨晚的十年期美债拍卖结果是一个好的信号：
1）美国390亿美元10年期国债拍卖中标收益率5.3%，低于预发行利率、即市场定价预期；
2）认购倍数2.77倍明显高于过去六次平卖平均的2.54倍；
3）非交易商投资者认购比例创历史纪录97.5%，代表外国央行、国际货币当局、海外投资机构等海外机构的间接投标人获配80.3%、为历史第四高，显示外资需求异常强劲

很多人可能不是很理解这次拍卖数据意义多重大？
5.3%的拍卖收益率为2000年11月以来最高水平，美国国内的直接竞标这和美国海外的间接竞标者直接把这次拍卖97.5%的美债直接给买走了。而一级交易商——即负责兜底未被投资者认购债券的大型银行——此次的参与比例只有2.5%已经降至2003年以来最低。

但这也给出了一个很有价值的信号：5.3%左右的长债收益率开始出现明显的长期资金承接，这也源于投资者对高收益率的主动追逐。这也是10月1号这个推文https://t.co/zUtcdpyXJW聊到的：收益率大幅回升改变了债券的风险收益结构，当前这个位置上应该会有一批债市资金开始重新逐步买入长债，因为性价比开始显现了。

拍卖结果好，收益率也就有回落。但昨晚公布的美联储9月议息会议既要，美联储9月会议纪要称：“多数与会者评估认为，在年底前再次上调联邦基金利率目标区间可能是合适的。”部分联储官员近期表态已明显降温10月行动预期，就是年内再次加息共识很强但10月可能不急。

相当于说十年期美债拍卖结果提振了短期情绪，但美联储政策信号令利率长期维持高位的预期难以消退。接下来更重要的验证就是今晚的规模220亿美金的30年美债拍卖了。

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

author: xicilion
quoted_text:
卧槽，当年轰动国内 AI 圈的“字节投毒实习生”田柯宇，现在杀回来了！

刚刷到彭博今天专门发了一篇对他的采访。

田柯宇 @keyutian  现在自己出来创业做世界模型，公司甚至还没有正式名字、没有产品，只有 10 个人，却已经从五源资本、IDG 等机构融了接近 3000 万美元，投后估值接近 2 亿美元。

而且这哥们现在做的东西还挺有意思。

简单来说，他觉得：人类的语言其实根本不适合描述这个世界。

比如你想用文字完整描述一段视频，里面每一个物体的位置、运动、光影、物理变化，基本是不可能的。

所以他的思路是，干脆别让 AI 使用人类语言理解视频了。

他们直接让 AI 自己发明一门语言。

他们现在已经做出了一套类似词典的东西，里面大概有 20 万个符号，人类完全看不懂，但 AI 可以拿这些符号去表示、压缩和预测视频。

接下来他们准备喂进去大约 1 亿小时的视频，让模型通过这套自己的语言去学习现实世界。

最终目标不是视频生成，不是World Model，是希望做一个基座模型：

让 AI 真正理解空间、运动和物理规律，未来可以作为机器人、自动驾驶、交互式视频这些东西的基础模型。

田柯宇说，这套方法目前已经能让视频生成效率提升至少一个数量级。

他们计划先做公开 Demo，甚至是直播，完整模型则准备在 2027 年发布。

现阶段不着急做消费级产品，也暂时不考虑怎么商业化，就是先怼基座模型。

田柯宇这个人，我其实之前就写过。

他离开字节之后，他还作为一作拿了 NeurIPS 2024 Best Paper。

那篇论文我当时专门看过，我印象特别深，因为它做的事情其实很暴力：就是想办法把视觉生成这件事，变得更像 LLM 一样，可以不断 Scaling，同时把生成成本和复杂度往下降。

我当时看完就觉得，这个人能力是真的很牛逼。

所以后来网上一直在讨论他当年在字节的事情，我其实也一直挺好奇到底发生了什么。

因为当时中文互联网传得特别夸张，什么“投毒大模型”、造成几百万甚至八百万损失，各种版本都有，已经快传成 AI 圈都市传说了hhhh

结果这次彭博终于把很多以前不知道的细节补出来了。

quoted_text:
我把后面这一段单独摘出来放评论：

很多人看完这期访谈会觉得，以后自己也可以像 Lauren 那样不 Review PR 了，装上她的 Skill，让模型帮忙验证一下就行。我自己现在的做法和她差不多，每天也有大量 PR，也不 Review。但我的建议是先别急着学她怎么做，先弄明白她凭什么能这么做。

1. 你能不能用上最好的模型，Token 够不够

在用上 Fable 和 Opus 5.5 之前，AI 写的代码我是不太放心的；用上之后，我才真的敢让 AI 去写而不怎么 Review。模型能力很重要，能力没到，就先别想这件事。

还有成本。像我这样没有大公司可以依靠的，得自己掏钱买 2 个 Claude Max 20x 账号，还得省着用。Lauren 在大公司，不用考虑 Token 消耗，全程用最好的模型、开最快的模式都没问题。

不过也别着急。Fable 这个级别的模型，也许半年以后就能像现在的 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 一样便宜，人人用得起。梁圣加油。

2. 不能完全依赖 AI 的验证

哪怕现在 GPT-6 操作电脑的水平已经超过真人了，让它去做验证，也只能替代一部分，不能真的全交给它，自己还是要看。

可以做的是把那些手动重复做的事情，一点点沉淀成 Skill 和自动化脚本，把体力活解放出去。

3. 方向得靠你自己的专业来指

再聪明的 AI，也没办法替你决定该往哪个方向走。就像给车子装上火箭发动机，也得你来告诉它往哪开，走偏了要及时调整，不然跑得再快也是南辕北辙。

做软件也一样。你不能指望一句提示词做出一个淘宝。你得先做一个能发商品、能浏览的小网站，再加上用户注册，还得区分买家和卖家，然后是支付和安全，功能做完了还要扛得住很多人同时用。稍微复杂一点的软件，都没法完全依赖 AI，要人去拆解、规划，分成一个个小版本、小里程碑，做完要验证，出现偏差要重新指方向。甚至做着做着，你自己的想法都变了，AI 不可能知道你真正想要的是什么。

所以就像播客里说的：模型越来越强，卡住人的已经变成你能不能把自己想要什么讲清楚。

4. 不一定要用他们的 Skill，但要学着把事情交给 Agent 去做

Matt 和 Lauren 的 Skill 都很受欢迎，但你不一定要用。

一方面，软件工程的基础知识，现在的模型已经学得很好了。Lauren 在播客里也说，去年的 Skill 还得写清楚具体该敲哪条命令，现在这些都可以删掉，只留流程步骤，Skill 会越写越短。

另一方面，他们的开发流程和环境，跟你的很可能不一样。Lauren 的 Skill 都是从她自己的工作里总结出来的：验证技能来自她当“人肉中转站”的那段日子；另一个叫 recall 的技能，来自她每次开新对话，都得把上一个对话里的背景再讲一遍。

所以更重要的是从你自己每天的开发流程出发。那些还要你手动操作的环节，尽可能交给 Agent 去做；Agent 做顺了，再把它的操作过程沉淀成 Skill，反复迭代优化。

如果不知道从哪里下手的话，可以参考 Lauren 的办法：翻自己和 AI 的聊天记录，找那些你反复纠正、反复插手的地方。这样迭代出来的 Skill 才真正适合你，用她的话说，每个厨师都该有一套自己的刀。

I got some issues with this.

The $132m/year is not real at all. Closer to $3m at today's prices, and as low as $1.2k within a year.

Yes, $132m -> $1.2k. Hear me out.

1. The price listed is not accurate at all.

$11m/month is just wrong. Real "api cost" is prolly $100k-$500k per month range.

The 1.5T tokens number includes cache'd tokens. I looked at my own usage, and 33.5B tokens came out to $0.56/m (under 1/10th of Peter's $8/m estimate).

I'm primarily using expensive models like Opus and Astra, and "1.5t tokens" would still have cost me ~$800k. If I used cheaper models and hit cache more, easily could get as low as $100k.

2. Intelligence is getting cheaper incredibly quickly

I know our LLM bills are going up and everyone is stressed about it. Totally reasonable! It's not because intelligence got more expensive.

Artificial Analysis tracks how "cost at a given intelligence level" drops over time. It used to drop at ~10x/year. Now it's at 30x lower in 5 months. (see image)

Assuming the $100k from before, cost could get as low as $3k/month in a few months, and if trends continue, $100/month by this time next year.

Obviously there will be smarter models and we will move to them, but replicating her experience today with equivalent models will be $1.2k/year by next year.

3. Nobody said this is normal

Lauren is the 0.0001% of "agentic engineer". Measuring her work as "$ in -> software out" is reductive and wrong.

Her spend should be looked at as a combination of product/eng, research, FDE work (pstack), and marketing. Worth $350k/day? No. Worth a mil or two a month? Absolutely.

She is exploring what happens when you ignore the cost of intelligence. She's not doing this because Cursor expects every company to spend $10m/year on tokens.

She's doing it because that $10m in tokens is going to cost $10,000 in a year or two.

text:
An attacker just drained $6 million from a DeFi vault.

The vault kept a whitelist of approved addresses, and any address on that list could withdraw funds without putting up collateral.

An attacker got a malicious contract added to the whitelist, then used it to drain about $6M in wstETH.

Our head of security, @realgmhacker, told @cryptodotnews the security community would probably have found the flaw through a bug bounty.

But the vault had no clear way to report it. With its operators unidentified, a whitehat could hardly act without risking legal trouble.

On top of that, the vault's seven Safe signers are still unidentified. More than 24 hours after the attack, they hadn't said anything publicly.

A bug bounty gives researchers a clear channel to flag problems before attackers exploit them.

Give researchers that channel before an attacker finds the flaw.

text:
Google 开源 EnvHarness，给 Agent 配上会调难度的训练场。

做 Coding Agent、网页自动化的开发者，可以用它把反复出现的错误，变成针对性的练习。

工作流程很直观：
读取执行轨迹 → 找出弱点 → 生成环境插件 → 重新试跑验证。
比如 Agent 改完代码就提交、不跑测试，系统就能给训练环境加一道规则：没运行测试，先不让提交。再从练习中提炼验证技能。

它能调整任务起点、可用动作和观察反馈，同时保留原有判分逻辑。

团队报告：在 Gemini 3.5 Flash 的 SWE-bench Verified 技能学习实验中，相比从原始环境提炼技能，成功率从 49.88% 提升到 52.58%，平均执行步数减少约 9.8%。

这是面向可重置训练环境的研究框架；设计环境仍有额外计算开销，步数减少不等于总成本降低。

做 Agent 训练与评测，值得研究这条“诊断错误 → 定制练习 → 验证迁移”的路线。

Continuing to add to the previous $HOOKED analysis.

C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE 

I think this AI Assisted Hook Creation update is one of the most important changes in this round, because it is not about adding another new feature, but about lowering the barrier to creating a programmable token.

So far, HOOKED’s product line has started to form a complete loop:

Launch → Rules → Trading → Rewards → Borrowing → Liquidity → Financialization → AI-generated Rules

Loans allow tokens to directly enter lending; Social Trading Wars turns trading into a competition and reward mechanism; OTC solves the liquidity problem for locked assets; Permanent Hook allows these rules to persist throughout the token’s lifecycle.

Individually, none of these features is enough to justify a high valuation. But together, HOOKED is clearly no longer a traditional launchpad.

The Launchpad is the entry point, Hook is the execution layer, and AI is starting to become the rule-production layer.

And today’s AI Assisted Hook Creation fills in a key piece:

Previously, HOOKED provided the rules. Now, users + AI can create the rules.

If this mechanism can ultimately generate real usage and economic activity, HOOKED’s Thesis could evolve from:

Token-2022 Launchpad → Programmable Token Infrastructure → AI-managed Token Economy

This is what I currently see as the most compelling bet on HOOKED.

author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
Continuing to look at $HOOKED.

C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE 

Yesterday, when we analyzed it, I was more inclined to define it as “continued product expansion + deep price retracement + waiting for a re-rating.” But with today’s updates from the official account, I think the Thesis has moved another step forward:

HOOKED is gradually evolving from a Token-2022 Launchpad into Token-level financial infrastructure.

The most important update this time is not any single new feature, but Loans.

Holders can now use their own HOOKED as collateral to borrow SOL. The tokens remain in their wallets and are not liquidated due to price fluctuations. The lending mechanism itself is built around the token’s trading fees.

This extends the role of Hooks from “defining how a token trades” to “defining how token holders can use their assets.”

Previously, Lock & Earn was:Hold → Earn

Now Loans adds:Hold → Borrow

Combined with Paired Launch, Permanent Hook, OTC, and other features, HOOKED is gradually turning a token from a simple trading asset into a programmable financial product.

Social Trading Wars is another direction. FOMO App vs Pump App compete based on holder count, with SOL rewards distributed to the winning side. Essentially, it connects:

Trading → Competition → Rewards

If this mechanism can consistently generate trading volume, it feeds back into HOOKED’s own:

fee → buyback → burn flywheel.

So my view of HOOKED is no longer simply “a better launchpad.”

The launchpad is the entry point. What is really worth betting on is that, in the future, rules around token trading, yield, borrowing, locking, transfers, and other behaviors can all be written directly into the token itself.

That is also what makes the Hooked Standard so important.

The official account is now emphasizing “every transfer gets hooked.” A token can directly define what happens with every transfer: pay holders, burn tokens, pay the creator, and so on.

If this standard is eventually adopted by a large number of tokens, HOOKED’s value-capture logic could become much larger than that of a simple launchpad.

Fundamentally, I think it continues to strengthen.

From the previous Lock & Earn, Paired Launch, and Permanent Hook, to the current Loans, Social Trading, OTC, and Hooked Standard, the product coverage has expanded significantly.

Buybacks and burns have now reached 60.6M HOOKED, around 6% of total supply.

But there is one thing I don’t want to be overly optimistic about: although the burn figure looks good, the recent growth rate has not been particularly fast.

So we can’t simply use “6% of supply has already been burned” as proof that token demand is exploding.

What really matters is whether the cumulative trading volume can continue to translate into:fee → buyback → burn

So I remain bullish on HOOKED, but the thesis is no longer about “how many more Hooks it can launch.”

What will determine its valuation in the next stage is whether new mechanisms like Loans and Social Trading see real usage, and whether platform trading volume can consistently translate into fees, buybacks, and burns.

If product usage and value capture continue to grow together, the current valuation will become increasingly difficult to justify.

If the number of features keeps increasing but real usage doesn’t follow, then these Hooks will ultimately remain just narrative.

What HOOKED really needs to prove now is not how many more things it can build, but whether these features can actually make the token more valuable.

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.
