text:
泰达最近疯狂冻U，惹了不少官司。

9 月两名泰国商人起诉，指控泰达非法冻结约 4240 万U；昨日，跨境支付公司 Conduit 也起诉泰达，称其冻结了约 276 万U，却始终没有给出充分解释。

其实，促成泰达冻结一个地址的情形，一般可以分为三类：

1. 泰达应执法或司法要求进行冻结。

执法机关提出请求，或者法院发出相关命令，泰达审核后配合冻结。

这是最常见的。一个美国三线城市的警探，可以直接请求泰达冻结一个数十万甚至百万美金的地址，而这个地址的背后，可能是一个远在迪拜的某位大哥。
美国的长臂执法，在这里如此的具象化😂。

2. 泰达依据制裁名单或政策进行冻结。

最典型的是美国财政部 OFAC 的 SDN 名单，泰达的条款还涉及联合国、英国等适用的制裁框架，也与以色列国家反恐融资局 NBCTF 有过冻结合作。这类一旦涉及正式制裁，后续处理往往比较麻烦，尤其在国际政治紧张的时期。

3. 泰达自主调查、判断后发起冻结。

这类来自泰达自己的合规风控体系。Conduit 案目前更接近这一类。按原告的说法，巴西警方确实提供过一批可疑地址，但 Conduit 的钱包不在其中，是 T3 根据自身未披露的标准，额外纳入了冻结范围。这个 T3 到底是什么组织，稍后我会在评论区补充。

前两类原因都属于泰达被动参与的冻结流程，本质上还是外部的执法/司法请求发起的冻结，只有第三类原因是泰达主动发起的冻结，这也是最容易被遭到质疑的。

凭什么泰达你可以在没有针对我的司法命令/执法请求的情况下，就把我的U冻了？

但有时候泰达也挺无奈的。

因为执法和司法都有程序成本。从发现问题、追踪资金、取证核实，到形成请求、完成跨境协作，每一步都需要时间。链上资金却可能几分钟就转走好几轮。等正式程序走到冻结这一步，钱可能早就散了。

这就是执法、司法的滞后性。

在我看来，泰达对链上 USDT 的流向其实相当门清。主动把冻结动作抢在正式执法流程落地之前，既能拦住可疑资金，也能拿着这份合规成绩单，到监管面前邀一份功。

近期其他稳定币发行商也在不断扩张合规市场，近日币安入股 Circle、Circle 早在 2024 年就逐步退出 TRON 链的营运、泰达联合 Anchorage（美联邦特许加密银行，也有稳定币发行的业务）推出面向美国市场的 USA₮ ，这些都是信号，全球 U 市场要守，合规市场也想吃，泰达的动作已经很明确了。

另外，关于泰达的冻结流程，还有一个冷门小知识：在 Ethereum 和 TRON 上观察到的泰达多签冻结流程中，冻结提案可能先公开上链，满足签名条件后才真正执行。

简单说就是，泰达不是突然冻结你的地址，而是会先广播自己要冻结哪个地址，这个窗口在过去一年中的中位数是 20 分钟，也是有部分的地址，通过这个窗口将 USDT 进行转移、混币、兑换，这就是冻结逃逸，而过去一年的逃逸资金数额高达 8800 万 USDT。(https://t.co/9z5mYS9Dgt 数据)

但如果你的地址真的被冻了，那该怎么办？

不少 U 大户被冻后，第一反应都是：为什么冻我？这确实是一个值得问的问题。

我们也经常遇到，希望通过现有渠道了解冻结触发原因的客户。其实知道自己为什么被冻，不管是后续的解冻协调，还是业务合规优化，都是很有帮助的。

但同时，我们也不得不承认，冻结也是链上合规必要的一环。我们也与执法合作，成功帮助多位被盗客户冻结了部分资产。以我们处理案件的经验，链上资金一旦被冻结，追回的可能性提升的就是几个量级。

FlashRescue 也自研了一个 USDT Freeze Tracker，把泰达在 Ethereum 和 TRON 上的冻结、解冻、销毁记录，以及待执行的多签提案放在一起，供大家学习、查询和研究：https://t.co/cfLtixjn4o

text:
A few things: 

"DoorDash typically builds whereas Uber usually buys" - The facts don't support this opinion. Uber didn't deploy any capital on M&A between 2022 to 2024, while organically establishing category leading positions across Mobility and Delivery globally. Meanwhile, nearly the entirety of Doordash's international business is built on fairly expensive acquisitions (Wolt, Deliveroo), and it has acquired substantials assets to expand into new verticals as well (Sevenrooms, Grub Campus etc). If you add up the deployments, you'll find that Uber has deployed a significantly smaller portion of its FCF on acquisitions than DD has, while delivering steady ~20% growth off a much larger base.  

"Uber doesn’t seem to be buying cheaply either"
Every dollar of Gross Bookings is not created equal. We have successfully executed on a barbell strategy where products with high ticket size and margins allow us to invest behind affordable products that drive acquisition and frequency for the platform. Additionally, our Uber for Business offering has delivered sustained, strong traction. ezCater has a nearly 10X order size relative to a typical delivery order in the US, and is accretive to Delivery margins outright. We expect more upside post synergies (and potentially more as it's plugged into U4B distribution and goes global). Beyond the strategic merits, financially, it delivers a better return than buying back our own stock, which is a bar we continue to hold for any evaluation. 

Build vs. buy. 
Catering is an operationally complex business. When an office admin orders lunch for their hungry team, you better deliver! That means a distinct product experience, work on merchant ops, as well as a specialized effort with couriers and set up specialists. That doesn't mean it can't be built, but this acquisition leapfrogs Uber well ahead. Combined with our distribution and global footprint, an acquisition allows us to scale this category much faster.

Uber vs. Expedia. 
I guess it needs to be said - Uber is not Expedia! Post COVID, Uber has compounded topline at over 20% and bottomline at over 70% (CAGR 2022-2025).

text:
如果经常出国，我觉得 Gate Card 这种产品还是挺实用的

以前出国想办 Visa 卡，通常要跑银行、提交资料、等审核，临时要用的时候确实麻烦

现在 Gate 这套产品，直接把「账户 + 入金 + 换汇 + 消费」串起来了

先说我觉得比较实用的几个点：

① Gate Card：手机直接当 Visa 卡用

线下消费不一定非要带实体卡，支持手机碰一碰支付，出国吃饭、购物这些场景会方便很多

② Gate Money：可以开同名 USD 账户

重点是“同名账户”

不是借别人账户收钱，而是开通属于自己的账户信息，用来进行跨境资金收付，日常使用会更顺手

③ 入金方式比较多

银行转账、链上充值、Gate 账户内部转入都可以，根据自己的资金来源选择就行

④ 资金进来之后还能继续管理

可以在 Gate Money 里进行法币和数字资产之间的兑换，后续还能配置股票、ETF、黄金等资产

怎么开？

先把 Gate App 更新到 v8.39.0

首页 → Money → 充值 → 银行转账 → 选择法币 → 开通专属 USD 账户

按照页面填写资料，完成后就能看到自己的同名账户信息

怎么入金？

有三种方式：

银行转账
复制页面提供的收款人、账号/IBAN、SWIFT/BIC 等信息，用自己的银行账户转账，完成后回到页面确认

链上充值
选择对应币种和网络，把资产直接充到 Gate Money 支付账户

Gate 转入
如果资产本来就在 Gate，直接从现货账户转到支付账户，选择币种和数量即可

资金到账后，需要消费的时候再接入 Gate Card

简单理解就是：

银行账户负责收付款 → Gate Money 负责资金管理 → Gate Card 负责消费

对于经常跨境、出国消费或者需要管理多种资产的人来说，这种一体化体验确实比以前到处切换平台方便不少

Continuing to look at $HOOKED.

C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE 

Yesterday, when we analyzed it, I was more inclined to define it as “continued product expansion + deep price retracement + waiting for a re-rating.” But with today’s updates from the official account, I think the Thesis has moved another step forward:

HOOKED is gradually evolving from a Token-2022 Launchpad into Token-level financial infrastructure.

The most important update this time is not any single new feature, but Loans.

Holders can now use their own HOOKED as collateral to borrow SOL. The tokens remain in their wallets and are not liquidated due to price fluctuations. The lending mechanism itself is built around the token’s trading fees.

This extends the role of Hooks from “defining how a token trades” to “defining how token holders can use their assets.”

Previously, Lock & Earn was:Hold → Earn

Now Loans adds:Hold → Borrow

Combined with Paired Launch, Permanent Hook, OTC, and other features, HOOKED is gradually turning a token from a simple trading asset into a programmable financial product.

Social Trading Wars is another direction. FOMO App vs Pump App compete based on holder count, with SOL rewards distributed to the winning side. Essentially, it connects:

Trading → Competition → Rewards

If this mechanism can consistently generate trading volume, it feeds back into HOOKED’s own:

fee → buyback → burn flywheel.

So my view of HOOKED is no longer simply “a better launchpad.”

The launchpad is the entry point. What is really worth betting on is that, in the future, rules around token trading, yield, borrowing, locking, transfers, and other behaviors can all be written directly into the token itself.

That is also what makes the Hooked Standard so important.

The official account is now emphasizing “every transfer gets hooked.” A token can directly define what happens with every transfer: pay holders, burn tokens, pay the creator, and so on.

If this standard is eventually adopted by a large number of tokens, HOOKED’s value-capture logic could become much larger than that of a simple launchpad.

Fundamentally, I think it continues to strengthen.

From the previous Lock & Earn, Paired Launch, and Permanent Hook, to the current Loans, Social Trading, OTC, and Hooked Standard, the product coverage has expanded significantly.

Buybacks and burns have now reached 60.6M HOOKED, around 6% of total supply.

But there is one thing I don’t want to be overly optimistic about: although the burn figure looks good, the recent growth rate has not been particularly fast.

So we can’t simply use “6% of supply has already been burned” as proof that token demand is exploding.

What really matters is whether the cumulative trading volume can continue to translate into:fee → buyback → burn

So I remain bullish on HOOKED, but the thesis is no longer about “how many more Hooks it can launch.”

What will determine its valuation in the next stage is whether new mechanisms like Loans and Social Trading see real usage, and whether platform trading volume can consistently translate into fees, buybacks, and burns.

If product usage and value capture continue to grow together, the current valuation will become increasingly difficult to justify.

If the number of features keeps increasing but real usage doesn’t follow, then these Hooks will ultimately remain just narrative.

What HOOKED really needs to prove now is not how many more things it can build, but whether these features can actually make the token more valuable.

text:
The Next Step for HertzFlow Isn’t Just More Leverage, It’s More Reach

The more I study HertzFlow, the more interesting its “World Leverage Engine” positioning becomes.

Seeing HertzFlow represented at BNB SG in Singapore made me think about a part of the project I don't see discussed enough:

Who is this infrastructure actually being built for?
Not only traders.
Not only DeFi users.

But potentially humans + autonomous agents interacting with financial markets.

That distinction matters.

1. HertzFlow is building around a broader market model

HertzFlow is a self-custodial perpetual protocol on BNB Chain, with trading built around liquidity pools and oracle-based pricing rather than a traditional order-book matching model.

That architecture creates an interesting foundation:

Trader
↓
HertzFlow
↓
Liquidity
↓
Market exposure

The important part for me is that this structure doesn't inherently depend on a trader sitting in front of a screen clicking buttons.

And that's where the agent angle becomes interesting.

2. Humans and agents have very different trading habits

A human trader might think:
“I see an opportunity → I open a position.”

An agent can operate differently:
Observe
→ Evaluate
→ Execute
→ Monitor
→ Adjust
→ Repeat

That means an infrastructure layer for agents needs more than a nice trading interface.
It needs programmable access to markets.

HertzFlow is already exposing developer infrastructure around its protocol, including an SDK and APIs, while its public GitHub organization also includes agent-oriented work such as Goo, an autonomous onchain life engine.

That makes the Singapore positioning more interesting to me than simply another ecosystem appearance.

3. The real opportunity is programmability

This is the part I personally find most interesting.

Imagine an autonomous trading system with a simple objective:

Market data
↓
Strategy
↓
Risk check
↓
HertzFlow execution
↓
Position monitoring

A human still defines the strategy and risk boundaries.
But the machine can handle the repetitive execution layer.

HertzFlow's developer tooling already points in this direction: its CLI supports programmatic market data, positions, orders and trading commands, with JSON output specifically usable for scripts and agents.

That's a much more concrete way to think about the human + agent narrative.

4. But I don't think “agents” should just mean bots with leverage

This is where I think the conversation needs to mature.

Giving an agent access to leveraged markets isn't automatically useful.

The important questions become:
Can it read reliable market data?
Can it understand position state?
Can it respect risk limits?
Can it manage open positions?
Can it react consistently?
Can humans remain in control of the strategy?

That is why I see HertzFlow's infrastructure layer as potentially more important than simply advertising a bigger leverage number.

The protocol needs to become usable infrastructure, not just a place where someone manually opens a long or short.

5. Singapore is a fitting place to have this conversation

BNB SG brings together builders and projects around the BNB ecosystem.

So seeing HertzFlow represented there by Hero Yang isn't just another event appearance to me.

It's an opportunity to put a very specific thesis in front of the ecosystem:
What happens when leveraged markets become infrastructure that both humans and autonomous software can interact with?

That's a much bigger question than “how much leverage can I get?”

My takeaway

I've written about HertzFlow from the trader side, LP side, risk side and product side.

This angle feels different.

The interesting evolution isn't simply:
More leverage → more traders

It could be:
Markets → programmable infrastructure → humans + agents

And if that transition actually happens, the protocols underneath those interactions become increasingly important.

That's why I'll be watching how HertzFlow develops its agent + developer layer alongside its trading product.

The World Leverage Engine may ultimately be less about giving people bigger positions and more about making market access programmable.

text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

3 things Blend Baskets do that are easy to miss:

• Stock dividends stay in the Basket. Robinhood reinvests them into the stock tokens, and those tokens remain part of the Basket.

• One trade buys every underlying asset. Each stock is purchased through its own pool and the Basket share is minted in the same transaction. There’s no separate Basket pool.

• Owner fees can go back into the Basket. They can be added to holder backing, increasing the amount of stock behind each share, with Blend’s keeper handling it automatically.

WHEN INTELLIGENCE REFUSES TO FORCE AN ANSWER

October 7, 2026

WHAT IF THE MOST POWERFUL MARKET INTELLIGENCE IS NOT THE SYSTEM THAT TELLS YOU WHAT TO TRADE, BUT THE SYSTEM THAT UNDERSTANDS WHY YOU SHOULDN’T?

This is the fundamental distinction behind two independently developed TradingView systems: AAIS — Autonomous AI Strategies and AISLS — AI Self-Learning Strategy.

Markets are not simple. They are living environments of changing relationships, where direction, momentum, structure, timing, volatility, participation, risk, and confidence continuously interact.

Most importantly, those conditions do not always agree.

AAIS was developed to diagnose that complexity.

Operating through a multi-engine diagnostic architecture, AAIS examines market conditions across interconnected analytical mechanisms, organizing their relationships into an intelligible representation of the current environment.

Rather than reducing every observation to BUY or SELL, AAIS can identify WAIT, NO EDGE, CONFLICT, RESTRICTED, and NO TRADE.

These are not empty answers. They are meaningful diagnostic distinctions.

AISLS introduces another dimension: independent adaptive examination and qualification of developing market setups.

Where AAIS asks, “What is the market showing?”, AISLS examines whether the developing conditions actually justify qualification.

Both systems operate independently. Both can be examined together.

When they agree, their convergence becomes information. When they disagree, their divergence becomes information.

Neither system must manufacture an opportunity to justify its existence.

That is the architecture.

MARKET DATA → AAIS DIAGNOSIS → AISLS QUALIFICATION → HUMAN DECISION.

The purpose is not to eliminate market uncertainty or promise extraordinary returns. It is to organize complex evidence, expose developing conditions, preserve contradictions, and make the reasoning environment more visible.

Because intelligence should not be measured merely by its ability to produce an answer.

It should be measured by whether the evidence justifies that answer.

This is what I have developed, publicly released, and made available for independent examination.

TWO SYSTEMS. DISTINCT RESPONSIBILITIES. ONE DEEPER EXAMINATION OF MARKET CONDITIONS.

NOT PREDICTING THE MARKET. DIAGNOSING IT.

text:
Unlike many networks, Solana users don't need to go into "bunker mode" ahead of an accelerated quantum timeline or classical attack provided by AI.
 
Solana uses Ed25519, where each signing key is derived by hashing a secret seed. Breaking the curve, whether by a quantum computer or a classical attack, would expose the derived key, but not the seed, and seeds are never exposed onchain. With a one-time network upgrade, rightful owners could prove knowledge of their seed using a hash-based proof and move their accounts to a safe signature scheme. A working proof of concept already exists: https://t.co/am2ErkkomT.
 
Solana remains secure today and has a defined path forward.
author: therealchaseeb
quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
ok it's official... AI-written unit tests and integration tests are empirically proven to be unhelpful. you should tell your agents to stop writing tests by themselves

on the deepswe eval set, banning sonnet 5.5 high from writing any tests actually resulted in slightly higher success rate (non stat-sig), with less time and token spent (stat-sig). this is pretty hard empirical evidence

across the tests that were written by the "tests allowed" baseline arm, 65% of them were unit tests, 35% were integration tests, neither bucket resulted in any improvement compared to not writing any tests at all

i also picked a random sample of 44 tasks subset where i completely disabled executing even existing tests - it also did not affect success rate at all

i spot checked many tests written in the baseline arm, and my intuition is that most tests are simply a repetition of the implementation

agent-written tests do not add any value because both the implementation and the tests were simply the agent's interpretation of our intent. the tests aren't any more accurate than the implementation itself

i suspect we can still extract some value from unit tests and integration tests if we describe them ourselves when we believe we can articulate our intent better through test cases than through requirements. but i have not proven this yet

also worth noting, during deepswe eval the agent wrote almost no e2e tests (only 17, compared to 3000+ unit/integration tests written). so this analysis does not prove nor disprove the value of e2e tests - i will do another eval specifically for that
author: kunchenguid

text:
Crypto was built for a world where, if assumptions changed, they changed slowly. But that comfortable "end of history" era is now over. 

But that doesn't mean cryptography is over. It's easy to forget, but for most of history, cryptography was a constant arms race between offense & defense. 

Justin's right to highlight the changing paradigm, and the urgent need to do something about it. It's a safe bet that cryptography will keep changing and the next decade of crypto will be defined by a shift to crypto-agility. 

That agility not only enables us to keep up with increasing capabilities the attackers, but also integrate the *new and better* forms of cryptography that both quantum and AI will ultimately enable. 

Cryptography, blockchains, and digital assets will continue to exist after quantum computers and AI. But there will be a reshuffling: protocols unable or unwilling to adapt (most likely due to ignorance or inaction) will not survive. The distribution of value in the future will almost certainly look very different than it does today. 

We're not waiting around. @projecteleven we're working with @drakefjustin and @ethereumfndn, @solanafndn, @zcashfoundation, @ripple, @quantusnetwork, and other teams across the space to build for this future today.

author: elonmusk
quoted_text:
@bot has completely changed my life. 

Confession: I have crippling existential dread when it comes to the mundane tasks required to be a fully functional adult in Western society. 

Mailing things, paying bills, gathering tax documents, scheduling appointments. I will procrastinate until the thing becomes too painful to ignore. Often that means I’m about to face criminal or civil penalties. 😂

You may be thinking to yourself, “It can’t be that bad, you seem like a fairly successful, high-achieving dude.”

It is that bad. All of my success is either in spite of or directly because of this kryptonite. 

I have done therapy, coaching, medicine journeys, read hundreds of books trying to overcome this affliction. Nothing has worked. I understand the root, I’ve read the science on behavior change. 

And Grokbot just fixed the glitch. 

I’ve been using and testing various AI assistants for the better part of two years. I’ve been desperately trying to build a system that solves this problem once and for all. 

Grokbot is so good and easy to use that it removes any friction to the point that it now feels too expensive psychologically to procrastinate. 

It just… does things. 

Example:

I have a stack of 100 advance copies of my book sitting in my office. I’ve been promising to mail them for a month. (You know who you are.) 

But gathering addresses, outreach, not to mention figuring out the best way to ship all seemed better left to tomorrow. 

Finally I got tired of looking at them so I voice noted my lovely anthropomorphic assistant, Rose, to go through my messages on every social platform, texts, and email, compile the list, reach out to confirm addresses, find the best way to ship, and hand it all to my house manager.

One prompt. And she did it. No getting stuck, no random ass approval messages. It’s just handled. 

Some of you might say this has been possible for a while. You’re partially right, but it’s the frictionless experience that is the real game changer. If I have to keep pausing and explaining, or correcting mistakes, I’ll get frustrated and revert to procrastination. 

Yes, I’ve tested tons of solutions including OpenClaw and more recently Muse and Dot. 

@bot is undefeated. My friend @danmartell has been saying to never bet against @elonmusk. 

I won’t make that mistake again. 

Bravo. It’s a wild time to be alive.

text:
为什么 meme 币的天花板不断下跌：持续的抽取

Shiba Inu 达到 500 亿美元的峰值。Pepe 达到 120 亿美元。2024 年的动物币达到 20 到 50 亿美元。2025 年的队列大多低于 5 亿美元。2026 年推出的任何项目都没有突破 10 亿美元。人们责怪 meme。meme 本身没问题。问题是每张图表上都坐着四个中间商，每个人都抽走一点。

三明治机器人从每笔买入中抽成。交易量机器人伪造图表来吸引下一个买家，然后卖给他们。做市商玩弄情绪。从一开始，捆绑者就坐在隐藏的供应上。他们每个人都抽走一点，合起来在持有者基础形成之前就把每个推出项目榨干。

$HAMSTER 对大多数抽取免疫。它只能在社交交易平台内交易。代币拒绝终端、机器人和直接池调用。没有三明治，没有交易量机器人，没有捆绑者，没有做市商。

每一美元本该流向三明治机器人的钱都留在了买家手中。每根本该诱使某人成为退出流动性的假交易量蜡烛都不会出现。每笔本该被抛售的捆绑都没有机会被买入。

一个不被抽干的代币可以复合增长。持有者保留了他们本该损失的东西，图表反映真实需求，想持有的那些人有机会做到。这就是每个大 meme 币在其周期早期所具备的条件，而每个 2026 年的推出项目都缺少的。

移除抽取，天花板就不会再下跌。这就是为什么在 70 万美元时这是一个不对称赌注。
author: imsongshu
quoted_text:
Why memecoin ceilings keep falling: constant extraction

Shiba Inu peaked at $50B. Pepe at $12B. The 2024 animals at $2 to $5B. The 2025 cohort mostly under $500M. Nothing launched in 2026 has cleared $1B. People blame the memes. The memes are fine. The problem is that every chart has four middlemen sitting on it, and each one skims a little.

Sandwich bots take a cut of every buy. Volume bots fake the chart to pull in the next buyer and sell into them. Market makers play with emotions. Bundlers sit on hidden supply from the start. Each one skims a little, and together they bleed every launch into the ground before a holder base can form.

$HAMSTER is immune to most of the extraction. It can only trade inside social trading platforms. The token refuses terminals, bots and direct pool calls. No sandwiches, no volume bots, no bundlers, no MM.

Every dollar that would have leaked to a sandwich bot stays with the buyer. Every fake volume candle that would have baited someone into being exit liquidity never prints. Every bundle that would have been dumped didn't have the chance to be bought.

A token that isn't being drained can compound. The holders keep what they would have lost, the chart reflects real demand, and the people who want to hold get the chance to. That is the condition every big memecoin had early in its cycle and every 2026 launch has lacked.

Remove the extraction and the ceiling stops falling. That is what makes this an asymmetric bet at $700k.

text:
When I first posted about $DARK, the market cap was only $1.82M. This round, it reached as high as $10M, nearly a 5.5x move. 

7KEPApdbBMByrmqihz3bht2uMhFQcatjfSFQCKq66kH3 

I don’t think this rally is simply an emotional pump. The market is starting to reprice the combination of NEAR Intents + Privacy + Solana.

Initially, the market saw it as a Solana privacy swap.

But as the product continues to develop, the market is starting to see:Solana liquidity + NEAR Intents + Privacy + NEAR-native dev background

This significantly raises DARK’s narrative ceiling.

DarkSwap now has a live Privacy Swap that is actually integrated with NEAR Intents, while Dark Pool and future ZK Pools are also being developed.

So the market is no longer simply betting on:“DARK is a privacy trading meme.”

It is betting on:“If NEAR Confidential Intents becomes the next Privacy infrastructure narrative, can DarkSwap become one of the earliest consumer-facing privacy terminals on the Solana side?”

This is what I think is the core repricing behind $1.82M → $10M.

More importantly, the product roadmap is evolving from Privacy Swap → Dark Pool → ZK Pools, moving toward a more complete privacy trading infrastructure.

The current Privacy Swap is more about making the routing process harder to trace, rather than providing full anonymity. The real thing to watch is the Dark Pool.

If it can eventually achieve:Deposit → Private Balance → Swap → Withdraw

then DarkSwap’s product positioning would change significantly, moving from a privacy swap UI toward actual privacy trading infrastructure.

Fundamentally, it is clearly stronger than when I first analyzed it.

The product has expanded from a simple privacy swap into NEAR Intents integration, confidential routing, holder rewards, a ZEC treasury, Dark Pool, and ZK Pools.

But we still need to distinguish:Product fundamentals strengthening ≠ Token economic value fully validated.

DARK itself currently has high trading volume, but what really matters is DarkSwap’s actual privacy volume, protocol fees, and user growth.

If product volume continues to grow and starts translating into real revenue, the current $10M valuation becomes much easier to justify.

The most important catalysts from here:

1. Dark Pool launch

This is currently the clearest product catalyst. If it officially launches and generates real volume, the market will likely reprice it again.

2. NEAR ecosystem integration

If the current attention from NEAR ecosystem accounts develops into official integration, traffic, or partnerships, that would be a much stronger attention catalyst.

3. ZK Pools

If they eventually complete the testnet, audit, and launch, DARK would move from using NEAR privacy infrastructure toward having its own privacy infrastructure.

4. Privacy narrative expansion

If ZEC, Privacy, and Confidential DeFi become major market narratives, DARK should have strong narrative beta.

But the risks are also clear.

$10M is no longer a $1.8M valuation. The market has already priced in part of the NEAR + Privacy + Dark Pool future optionality, so simply repeating the same narrative will become less effective as a catalyst.

Dark Pool has not been fully validated yet, and ZK Pools are even earlier. So a meaningful portion of the valuation above $10M is still pricing in the future.

There is also one very important distinction:

DARK token volume ≠ DarkSwap product usage.

If DARK itself remains highly traded while actual privacy swap volume fails to grow, the valuation will increasingly depend on narrative rather than fundamentals.

So I no longer view DARK as a $2M early experiment.

$10M is now entering the Thesis validation stage.

What ultimately determines whether it can move from $10M → $20M → $30M → $50M+ is not how many more Privacy narratives it can tell, but whether Dark Pool can launch, real privacy volume can grow, and that usage can ultimately translate into protocol revenue.

If these three metrics start growing together, $10M may only be the first round of repricing.

If they don’t, valuations above $10M will increasingly depend on market sentiment.

okx wallet:https://t.co/7FLUb4ejVS

DarkSwap is a privacy-focused cross-chain swap tool built from Solana, currently in an available beta.

It uses NEAR Intents for routing, with the core selling point being that users do not need to connect their wallets or sign authorization transactions on the website.

The project is trying to solve a basic problem: transfers and swaps on public blockchains leave fully traceable records by default. After users send a deposit from their own wallets, DarkSwap uses NEAR Intents’ confidential routing to increase the “distance” between the sender and recipient, reducing unnecessary direct-linkage exposure.

It’s similar to using cash or an intermediary for a transfer in the real world instead of leaving a complete bank-to-bank transaction trail, or like using a relay to make tracking more difficult, rather than providing true anonymity.

The main role of DARK is to reward holders. Half of the creator fees are distributed proportionally to eligible holders based on their holdings, paid out in wNEAR with no manual claiming required. The other half is used to purchase ZEC on Solana and add it to the protocol treasury.

The latest round of rewards distributed around 86.08 wNEAR to 407 holders and 1 ZEC to 92 holders. Cumulatively, the rewards have reached approximately 3,381 wNEAR + 3.14 million DARK + 1 ZEC, worth around $24,000 based on prices at the time.

Simply put, the project combines Solana liquidity, NEAR routing, and the ZEC narrative into one product, while the privacy theme currently has some attention in the market.

Its advantages are a simple user flow, funds never being custody-held by the project, and a relatively clear distinction between what is already live and what is still under development.

The limitations are also clear: limited privacy strength, small scale, and more advanced dark pool and ZK features have not yet been launched.

最近比特币进入了回调，跌破了 83000，大家都在关注后续走势

之前我们分析过，牛市每次回调会出现很多次假摔，也就是假跌破的情况

如图是 2023 年 3 月和 6 月 ETH 的假跌破
以及 2025 年6 月和 8 月的 ETH 假跌破

每次都会面临 5%-10% 的一根大阴线跌穿支撑区域
第二天收一个小 k 线，第三天大阳线涨回来

所以这两天是一个关键的观察，今天确保不再大跌，收一个小 k 线，明天再来一个大阳线，那就确定是一个假跌破了，后续继续大涨的希望很大

如果行情和我们预想的相反，继续下跌，那只能登一个新的震荡区间了

还有一点，我们之前聊过风险再平衡问题
前段时间我在 uni 价格 8 附近减掉了 15% 左右的仓位换成了 bnb 和 sol

减仓之后 uni 又继续大涨，都涨到了 10，当时觉得卖亏了，卖早了，没想到如今 uni 跌破了 8，而 bnb 和 sol 帮我扛住了大跌

这让我更加确信，只要山寨过热，就做风险再平衡，减掉一部分仓位换到主流币上，即使短期卖飞，但是长期表现上绝对正确

就像 2024 年质押挖矿热门的时候，我也质押了一部分 ETH 去撸毛，当时奖励的代币我分成了两部分，一部分直接换成比特币，不管比特币价格如何，直接换，另一部分留着看长期价格如何

结果很明确，那些撸毛的币如果一直拿着，只有归零这一个选择，同期换成比特币，反而利润翻倍

所以，下一个行情热潮来的时候，你手里的山寨肯定会大涨，大家都会很开心，但是要忍住，坚定减掉一部分换成主流币，不要怕主流币价格贵，因为未来会更贵，贵到你超乎想象而且很抗跌

如果一个好山寨，比如 uni aave 这种，仓位太重，你是拿不到牛市末期的，很容易被洗下去，越涨仓位越小反而会吃到最后的超额回报

My favorite type of founders I've helped fundraise are those who don't take no for an answer.

9 times out of 10, founders tend to just give up on a relationship if there's no fit for a deal, which shows their lack of sales skills and they start thinking the deal is dead.

I'm personally a huge proponent of closing a deal months or even years down the line.

Just because something isn't a fit today doesn't necessarily mean it won't be a fit tomorrow.

Keep the relationship warm. Share updates, invite them to events, send them company milestones, and keep showing them that you're building.

There are deals I've worked on at my audit security job 3 years ago that I'm now seeing get closed as I go through some of those groups.

Sharing basic updates, company launches, milestones, etc. can build a lot of trust over time.

I mean you're asking someone for millions of dollars. Do you really expect them to commit after a 30-minute conversation? It's possible, and it does work, but it shouldn't be the ideal scenario.

Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

@Alchemy is the @PalantirTech of crypto. Everyone knows it, but very few actually understand what it does.

Whenever you open an onchain app, check your balance, view your history, or send a tx, there’s infrastructure in the background connecting that app to the blockchain.

Nodes, APIs, blockchain data, and wallet tooling that apps would otherwise have to build and maintain themselves.

Alchemy is now packaging those pieces specifically for agents too:

→ AgentPay for programmatic payments
→ MCP server with 160+ blockchain tools
→ Agent Wallets for controlled onchain access

Invisible, but pretty essential infrastructure for the space.

quoted_text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

text: The Victorian elites who ran the British Empire did NOT sauna, or plunge, or work out, or use red lights. They didn't learn much at school. Instead, they partied all night, drank amounts that would make us wince, and worked a relaxed five- or six-hour day, sometimes from bed.
author: cremieuxrecueil
quoted_text:
The elites of Victorian Britain got up late, drank ceaselessly, worked short hours, partied through the night, and knew nothing about science, technology or engineering. And yet, by their own lights, they were hugely effective.

https://t.co/TvbuWtaPRJ

The Victorians are often held up as a model against the supposedly soft, feckless, humanities-educated elites of today. But I argue that the genius of their system may have been its drastic weighting towards soft skills, team-building and intra-elite networking:

- A Victorian’s gentleman’s office hours typically began about 11am and finished about 5pm, including a multi-course lunch with wine.

- Upper-class Victorians drank ceaselessly. Conduct guides recommended four or five glasses of wine at dinner *for married women*. Port was often served in pints.

- Party culture was intense and nocturnal. Balls started at about 10pm, peaked after 1am, and continued till dawn. During the social season, bankers, judges and politicians might go to several balls per week.

- Elite Victorians learnt almost no STEM at school or university. At least half of class time was given over to ancient languages, often as much as 80 percent. One leading educationalist remarked that it was not worth teaching science to gentlemen because it does not involve ‘continued reasoning’.

- Sports and character formation were valued far above transmitting facts. A top headmaster described his school’s priorities as ‘First – character, second – physique, third – intelligence, fourth – manners, fifth – information’.

This cannot have made elite Victorians more productive individually, but maybe the dense social and emotional network it created helped them to work as a sort of extended team. 

Perhaps we should think again about what makes groups of people effective.

text:
Saw this on Rednote and found it surprising (I am not able to verify it). It claims Baseten's gross margin was 17% in its most recent quarter, with the full-year guide cut from 30% to 20%. The stated reason: demand outran contracted capacity, so they're buying expensive short-term compute to keep customers served. It also says Cursor went from 57% of Baseten's annualized revenue in April to 28% in September, and that Baseten makes only ~4% gross margin on it.

I knew inference margins were well below SaaS, and way below data startups (I covered this in my earlier post on NVIDIA and open-weight models). But the public number reported for Fireworks is ~50%. Baseten doesn't disclose its own. 17% would be a very different business.

These numbers don't match what I'd learned about inference economics. But there's supporting evidence at another company: OpenAI reportedly told investors its adjusted gross margin fell from 40% to 33% in 2025, because it had to buy pricier compute at the last minute. I couldn't find a public source for the Baseten numbers. The closest thing: CEO Tuhin Srivastava said in June that a cloud provider quoted him $5.10/hr to renew a B200 cluster in October, up from $2.63. A 94% jump.

It's getting harder to tell which number to believe, and harder still to see where this is going.

至24年这种模式出来以后，发币变成了流水线，各条链也开始效仿，每天都有冲不完的新盘，玩家被反复收割以后，慢慢只学会一件事，先跑的人赚钱，留下的人买单，这种习惯一旦形成，即使碰到认真做事的项目，大家也会用同样的方式去对待它

最近用了一次 Claude Code 送的重置，加上现在 Fable 也比较耐用，所以我用 Fable 就多了一些，我的用法是这样的：

把任务发给 Fable 让它安排 SubAgent（Opus）去执行，它负责分析、编排和验收。

所以大部分时间它都在等 subagent 执行，也就意味着它还能能力接活。

这时候你甚至都不用等subagent任务完成，持续派活，它都能给你记着一起安排，空闲的时候就会去执行

所以我有几个会话就一直开着，想到啥就发一个指令过去。

有点像 Fable 就是个 Tech Lead 的角色，专门帮你派活，还帮你验收，安排的妥妥当当的。

我现在已经不限制用 1M 上下文了（删除CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT），设置了最大上下文是 300K

当然这样用比只用 Opus 5.5 还是费不少，希望早点价格降下来，真的省心。

最近摸索了一种新的节约 Token 但是效果不错的模式（都是被逼的，Token 太贵）：

Fable 写设计方案 -> 
（Loop 开始）
Opus 执行 -> Advisor（Fable） 验收
（Loop 结束）

步骤是这样的：

1. 先 Claude 里面设置一下 advisor 为 Fable
> /advisor fable

这样在使用 Opus，Sonnet 模型的时候，遇事不决它会请教 Fable，可能会有无谓的 Fable 消耗，但还是可以接受也值得

就好比请了个高级工程师当顾问

2. 复杂一点的问题先让 Fable 出方案，最大化利用 Fable 的能力。

就好比你让一个高级工程师写一个技术方案，让普通工程师去执行

3. 方案写好了确认了，让 Opus 去执行，但是执行的时候，加一句提示词：

> 完成后让你的 advisor 验收一下，如果验收有问题就按 advisor 的反馈修复，修复完成后再让 advisor 验收，直到通过 advisor 的验收为止

可以配合 /goal 使用效果更佳

这样 Opus 在实施完成后就会找 Advisor 验收，通过 Advisor 就会给出反馈，然后 Opus 继续修改。

这样的好处就是整个过程你不需要人工去用 Fable 确认—— 以前我就是这么干的，Opus 执行完，我得回到之前 Fable 的会话去让它验收，或者新开一个会话，把文档发给 Fable 验收。

现在 Agent 自己就能形成闭环，不用你自己参与。

就好比你请了个高级顾问，复杂问题找顾问出方案，执行让你的工程师去按照方案执行，每次工程师做完自己去找顾问验收，顾问不仅验收还会告诉工程师哪里不对，然后工程师自己改，不用说每次做完找你，你再找顾问。

text:
HYPE完全回购要108年？

有人算了一笔账：Hyperliquid每天拿出约200万美元回购HYPE，一个月也只有约6000万美元。面对数百亿美元的完全稀释估值，要把全部代币买回来，可能需要超过100年

所以，即使协议持续回购，HYPE现在的估值是不是也太贵了？

这个质疑值得讨论，但回购资金已经出现了一个新变化

10月3日，AQAv2机制产生的首笔约1458万美元USDC收益，已经转入Hyperliquid的Assistance Fund，用于购买HYPE

我们此前讨论过，USDC储备收益可能成为HYPE的新回购来源

现在，第一笔资金已经到账

过去，Hyperliquid主要靠用户交易赚钱。用户开仓、平仓，协议收取手续费，再把部分收入转化成HYPE买盘
AQAv2增加了另一条收入路径：沉淀在平台上的USDC储备，也能产生收益，并为Assistance Fund提供资金
也就是说，即使一笔资金暂时没有参与交易，它对应的储备仍可能贡献回购收入

这对HYPE有什么影响？

先看这笔1458万美元的规模，首笔付款覆盖30天。平均下来，相当于每天约48.6万美元。如果这一规模能够持续，简单年化约为1.77亿美元，这条新增收入相当于额外增加约24%的资金规模

这还不足以让数百亿美元的估值突然变便宜，但已经是一笔可以进入市场的新增买盘

更关键的是，回购资金的来源变多了

交易手续费取决于用户交易有多活跃；USDC储备收益则更多取决于平台沉淀了多少资金、适用收益率以及具体分配安排

用户频繁交易时，协议获得手续费。用户把USDC留在平台时，储备也可能产生收入

Hyperliquid未平仓合约从年初约77.2亿美元，增长到9月30日的约164亿美元；同期，平台保证金规模从约43.4亿美元增长到约72.2亿美元

更多资金留在平台，也支持了更大的持仓规模

今年前九个月，Hyperliquid永续合约成交量约2万亿美元，协议留存手续费约4.933亿美元。与此同时，按保证金规模计算的年化交易周转倍数，从1月约568倍下降到9月约440倍

这说明，平台上的资金变多了，但每一美元保证金对应的交易频率有所下降

如果只依赖手续费，用户把资金存进来却减少交易，收入增长就可能放缓

AQAv2恰好让这些沉淀资金也能贡献收入。它无法消除交易量下降的影响，但可以增加一部分与交易频率联系较弱的回购资金

再回头看“回购全部HYPE需要108年”的说法

按照每天200万美元计算，一年约7.3亿美元；用截图中的840亿美元FDV去除，确实会得到超过100年的数字

这笔计算揭示了一个事实：相对于目前的估值，现有回购规模并不算特别大

但它同时固定了几个条件：未来收入不增长、代币价格不变化，回购资金也始终维持今天的水平

第一笔1458万美元储备收益到账，已经说明其中一个条件开始变化

如果平台USDC规模继续扩大、交易手续费增长，回购资金就可能增加；反过来，如果资金流出、利率下降或者交易量萎缩，两条收入都可能承压

所以判断HYPE回购力度，既要看累计买了多少，也要看新增收入能否持续、实际买回多少枚代币，以及能否抵消解锁和其他新增流通供应

但不可否认的是，Hyperliquid 团队几乎所有的操作都是朝着通缩 HYPE 去的

未来的回购因素可能会更多，但不会更少

很多人还在担心团队把收入都收进了自己的囊中，但正如 Jeff 在 Token2049 上所说“我们并没有真的在优化收入，收入只是为用户创造价值的副产品”

text:
Scale Labs 发布了一个叫 Humanity's Sixth Sense（HSS）的新 Benchmark，专门测试人类习以为常的视觉直觉。

522 道涉及图片和视频的题目，人类正确率 93.1%，最强的 GPT-6-astra 只有 53.6%，25 个模型的中位数更是只有 30.9%。

有一道题，一位女士正在追赶公交车，司机停下来等她，于是她放慢脚步。人类一眼就能看懂这个因果关系，很多模型却解释不出来。另一道题问书架上还能不能塞进两本书，模型明明能看到空隙，却判断空间不足。

最离谱的是社交理解。25 个模型中有 21 个在这个维度表现最差，平均正确率只有 24.4%。

这些模型能处理复杂的数学证明，能写代码，能分析财报，却经常搞不清一个人为什么放慢脚步、谁在等谁、谁在一段互动中占据主导。

而且，研究团队发现，模型在这些题目上的失败，有 94% 来自视觉感知和隐含信息推断，真正归因于逻辑推理错误的只有约 5%。

模型平均每道题会消耗 4046 个推理 Token。提高推理强度，在部分测试中甚至会让正确率下降。

过去几年，我们对 AI 智力的理解，很大程度上是被考试塑造的。数学、编程、科学问题都能被明确描述，模型只要沿着给定的问题寻找答案。

但现实世界有一个很重要的区别，大多数时候，根本没有人替你把问题描述清楚。

一个人走进会议室，得先判断谁在说话、谁有决定权、谁虽然没开口却在影响讨论。司机看到行人犹豫，得理解对方究竟准备过马路，还是在等车。

这些判断涉及物理经验、社会关系、意图识别，以及对未发生事件的预测。人类的大量常识，恰恰建立在这些无法轻易用语言穷举的经验上。

现在流行的 Scaling 推理时间，主要解决的是给定信息之后如何推导答案。可如果最初就看错了人、漏掉了关键动作、误解了空间关系，增加 Token 可能只会让模型把错误解释得越来越完整。

更值得注意的是，研究团队给模型配上了裁剪、放大、搜索等 Agent 工具。结果在 388 道题的子集上，最佳系统也只达到了 59.3%。其中一类把二维遮挡误判为三维对齐的错误，几乎完全没有改善。

这说明工具调用可以弥补部分感知缺陷，但有些问题涉及模型对物理世界的内部理解，靠多看几眼也解决不了。

而我们现在正在做的事情，是把这些模型接入电脑、汽车、机器人，让它们拥有越来越大的行动权限。

这会带来一个很有意思的矛盾，AI 执行任务的能力越强，错误理解现实的成本反而越高。

过去 Chatbot 看错一张图，最多给你一段错误回答。未来 Agent 看错一个动作、误解一个人的意图，可能会直接执行接下来的一连串操作。

所以我越来越觉得，AI 下一阶段真正需要突破的能力，可能藏在那些我们从来没有认真考察过的普通人类经验里。

模型已经很擅长回答问题了。但在现实世界里，知道自己看到了什么、看漏了什么，以及什么时候应该停止行动，可能比继续提高答题分数更重要。

author: ebfull
quoted_text:
Do the labs have better algorithms for breaking crypto?

Independent of the answer, the most important thing is to have crypto agility. Zcash has proven this, with 3 upgrades happening in 6 months, and Tachyon planned for January. The protocol design has plans for how to turn off features to enable safe protocol upgrades. This is what Quantum Recoverability is, and it applies equally well if there's a non-quantum ECDLP attack.

We're equipped on multiple fronts to protect against future bugs. In the next cryptography upgrade, coming January, already slated features are:
- PQ transparent
- Switching to Tachyon

What people don't realize about Tachyon is it switches us to R1CS, and enables far more crypto agility away from elliptic curves. The nullifier derivation no longer depend on elliptic curves. We get far greater SNARK agility and can very quickly move to STARKs when any crisis comes.

Today's Zcash transparent UTXO's give a better security guarantee than an ETH address. @ZakuraZcash has solved the privacy and performance problem that were blocking rotating T-Addresses natively in the wallet. This is done using PIR to fetch balances, and its already live in Vizor. So its a short UX leap to get this backup plan.

In January, the Transparent pool will be upgraded to support hash based sigs, that can later be STARK aggregated.

text:
LPing is almost reaching saturation 🤔

In tradfi, fee reduction is the worst tactic to compete with others. Competitors fight each other by cutting fees to attract users and volume, but they also cut their own margin. Good for users, but at the end of the day, none of those exchanges win.

But in the on-chain LPing game, fee reduction seems like the only choice DEXs have right now to suck up volume.

Take a look at the swap fees of ETH/USDG from 3 different DEXs on Robinhood: 
▶️ @Uniswap : 0.01%
▶️ @giga_dex : 0.005%
▶️ @uponrh : 0.0087% 

All 3 are offering swap fees way lower than a CEX, which normally sits around 0.1%.

And according to ETH annualized volatility at 48% (Deribit stats), if you play a safe ±50% range strategy, you only get approx 10-15% APR. That's acceptable, and I believe this is the final backstop for the LPing game. We're almost at equilibrium.

If these platforms keep lowering fees below current rates, I'm afraid LPing just isn't worth it anymore. LPs will remove their positions, and no one wins.

author: punk6529
quoted_text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

text: 我操，今天这一波 AI 更新，真的让我有点震撼！  ChatGPT 新的智能输出形式、Grokbot 读取 X 内容能力的升级，再加上最近大模型能力的疯狂进化……  我突然有一种非常强烈的感觉：  对一个普通人来说，未来可能真的只需要一个 ChatGPT 对话框，就足以成为自己的整个数字工作入口。  网上经常有人说 ChatGPT 不行了，OpenAI 不行了，Opus 5.5 已经把它们按在地上摩擦。  但我自己的实际体验完全不一样。  这段时间，我几乎每天都在用 AI 做研究、写代码、部署产品、管理自动化任务、处理社交媒体、跟进各种项目。  坦白说，Opus 在一些任务上确实很强，我也愿意用。  但在 Computer Use、跨工具协作，以及把一件复杂的事情真正推进下去这方面，ChatGPT 依然是我目前体验最好的工作入口。  而且我越来越觉得：  最强的模型，和最好的 AI 工作入口，根本不是一回事。  我不在乎 GPT、Opus、Grok 到底谁在排行榜上第一。  我希望的是：  我只需要在一个对话框里说出我想做什么。  然后 AI 自己去调用最合适的模型、工具、Agent、云电脑，完成研究、执行、验证，再把结果交给我。  我不想每天管理十几个 AI 产品。  我只想管理自己的目标和结果。  当然，现在还远远谈不上完美。任务中断、上下文丢失、执行不可靠，这些坑我自己每天都在踩。  但今天这些更新叠加在一起，真的让我第一次如此强烈地感受到：  AI 正在从一个个独立的工具，变成个人数字世界的统一操作入口。  一个对话框，背后是无数个模型、Agent 和工具在替你工作。  这可能才是普通人真正能够享受到的 AI 革命。  不是 AI 又聪明了多少。  而是一个人，真的开始有能力调动过去只有一整个团队才能完成的工作。  太震撼了。

text:
Putting down some thoughts on what seems to be happening to the open-source harnesses, guys.

1. I found it weird that Hermes published an index showing the best models to use in their harness, and told their users, who according to OpenRouter largely use cheaper models, that they are doing it wrong. Barely any of these models make it to their index.

2. But then the index has Terminal-Bench Science and Terminal-Bench. I found this strange, because a general/personal agents harness is evaling itself on science and code benchmarks.

3. My back and forth with one of the cofounders made me realize where their heads are at. He has since written a post to break up with the personal agents positioning they fought hard to win from OpenClaw.

4. This sums it up: "Dumb Normies". OpenClaw launched the first agent harness. It's long forgotten because of how un-normie friendly it was. Hermes took over, but is largely being abandoned just like OpenClaw, because easier products with better UX showed up, i.e. Grok Bot, Instinct, Muse, Dots, etc.

5. It seems the open-source harnesses like OpenClaw and Hermes feel they have lost the consumer opportunity, or that they have no chance of winning it.

6. OpenClaw launched an Enterprise beta, clearly positioning itself as a technical agent layer for enterprise. I called this 4/5 months ago when I was in the community team, Hermes was beating our ass and Peter was making even weirder moves. I said to the team then that OpenClaw feels it has lost, so it's positioning for enterprise.

7. Now it's Hermes' turn to position away from general agent to specialized harness, in their case coding and science. Sad to see them give up on consumer, but I guess they have to make money somehow, so this makes sense.

8. But it's not obvious even that they will win those. @clairevo is a power user and she's since dumped OpenClaw/Hermes.

9. I still think open-source consumer/personal/general agent harnesses need to exist. I'm still a big fan of OpenClaw/Hermes, but I can see Grok Bot, Muse and Dot pulling me away, largely because of the UX.

10. @kunchenguid wrote some days back that we still need an open general agent harness. Seems we need new OSS companies, since the 2 flag bearers have given up. (https://t.co/WGw0IRrTBX)

Today we are releasing the new Injective Whitepaper.

It is the first full rewrite since our original paper in December 2018, which described a front-running-resistant exchange protocol on Ethereum.

Eight years later, Injective has evolved greatly into becoming a layer-1 blockchain for institutional-grade finance and tokenization. Every layer of the protocol exists to issue real-world assets and give them real utility across markets, applications, and AI agents.

Inside the paper

→ Asset issuance. Native RWA tokenization with role-based permissions over mint, send, receive, and burn, plus programmable receive hooks and sealable namespaces

→ RWA exposure. iAssets, stablecoin-margined, oracle-priced derivatives that track external assets with no wrapping or pre-funding

→ Trading. Tokenized assets trade on a fully onchain CLOB where each block runs a sealed frequent batch auction at a uniform clearing price, resisting front-running and ordering MEV

→ Settlement. BFT consensus with a greater-than-two-thirds commit threshold delivers deterministic finality with ~600ms blocks

→ Composability. Native EVM and WASM in one canonical state, with the MultiVM Token Standard keeping a single bank-module balance per asset, exposed to Solidity through precompiles

→ Derivatives. Perpetuals with time-weighted premium funding, initial and maintenance margin checks, reduce-only liquidations, and insurance funds

→ Agentic finance. AI agents operate on tokenized assets through MCP servers, policy-bounded signing, and x402 machine payments in USDC

→ Value accrual. Onchain protocol revenue flows to the recurring Community BuyBack for $INJ

The paper formalizes each mechanism, from the consensus threshold and block lifecycle to the batch clearing rule, oracle accounting, derivative risk checks, permission model, and dynamic issuance controller.

From issuance to settlement, one chain built for the full lifecycle of tokenized finance.

text:
$STOCKER, the launchpad behind $ZC, is worth keeping an eye on. It has already demonstrated strong fundamentals, and the platform is trying to turn a relatively straightforward token economic mechanism into a self-sustaining trading and burn flywheel.

0x75e2fc69ff2ac12af65ba7d321bbf4f878c535d2 

According to the data on its official website, Stockerum is no longer just a conceptual showcase. The platform has recorded approximately $99.83M in cumulative trading volume, generated around $558.01K in rewards, processed 267K trades, and launched 1,688 tokens. These figures at least indicate that the platform has real trading activity and a certain level of product adoption.

What deserves even more attention is its fee distribution mechanism.

Of the platform fees generated by each ETH trading pair, 60% is used to buy back and burn the corresponding token, while 10% goes to the Zcoin Foundation. Different tokens also have their own fee allocation ratios. According to the official website, STOCKER currently receives a 50% allocation, while ZC, VERIDIA, and SC receive 10%, 5%, and 5%, respectively.

This means STOCKER is not relying solely on market sentiment to attract attention. As long as the platform continues to generate trading activity, STOCKER has the opportunity to benefit from ongoing buybacks and burns through this fee distribution mechanism. According to the official website, approximately 38.69 million STOCKER tokens have been burned so far, with a corresponding value of around $251.56K. A total of 477 burns have been executed, using approximately 30.065 ETH.

Of course, a burn mechanism should not be directly equated with price appreciation. Burning reduces the circulating supply, but whether it can ultimately support the valuation still depends on new buying demand, platform trading volume, and the sustainability of fee revenue. If platform activity cools down, the burn rate may slow as well. Moreover, the platform's total trading volume does not translate entirely into actual buying pressure for STOCKER. Its fee allocation ratio and the execution of buybacks also need to be monitored and verified over time.

Another development that cannot be overlooked is that Stockereum is not positioning itself as just another ordinary Meme launchpad. Instead, it pairs newly launched tokens with tokenized stocks, bringing familiar symbols from traditional financial markets into on-chain trading. This direction has some narrative potential because it connects the familiarity of the stock market with the viral appeal of Meme culture and the speculative nature of on-chain trading. Whether the platform can consistently attract trading activity around different stock-related assets will directly affect its long-term growth.

So my interest in STOCKER is not primarily about betting on a single burn figure or exchange listing. What matters is whether it can turn its combination of stocks and Memes into a sustainable trading environment, then use platform revenue to generate ongoing token demand.

If Stockereum can continue expanding its trading volume, attract more projects and users, and maintain the execution of its buyback-and-burn mechanism, STOCKER's market narrative could evolve from that of a simple Meme launchpad token into an ecosystem asset supported by genuine platform activity.

However, at this stage, it remains a growth story that still needs to be validated. What I will be watching most closely is whether the platform can sustain its trading volume beyond periods of hype, and whether STOCKER's buybacks and burns can continue to produce meaningful changes in token supply.

금리와 유가가 조금 진정했지만 아직 그렇게 마음 편하진 않음

오늘 삼성전자 잠정실적 영업이익 107.4조원으로 컨센부합.
처음으로 분기 영업이익 100조 시대 열었으나 주가는 보합.
NXT 2% 오르던 주가도 정규장 열리면서 상승분을 다 토함.
107조가 뉘집 개이름도 아니지만 최근 컨센서스가 높아진탓.

SK하이닉스는 1.9% 상승하며 오랜만에 반등세가 나오는 중.
그럼에도 코스피는 -0.2%로 여전히 6,700대에서 빌빌 댐.
산업재와 금융섹터 동반 약세로 합심해서 코스피를 끌어내림.

코스닥은 장초반 -1.6%까지 밀렸다 약보합까지 반등한 상황.
바이오가 처맞아도 소부장과 2차전지가 지수를 캐리하는 중.
다만 양시장 모두 하락종목이 더 많다보니 시장체감은 험난함. 

주성엔지니어링 10%, 고영 7%, 대덕전자 4% 장비,기판 강세
삼성전기와 LG이노텍은 이 와중에 약세보이며 대형주는 소외.
국장은 최근들어 중소형주의 약진이 계속해서 돋보이고 있음.

LG에너지솔루션은 잠정실적 컨센상회 후 2차전지 끌어올림.
삼성SDI 4%, 에코프로비엠 3%대로 2차전지도 동반 반등.
보조금을 포함한 실적이지만 일단 주가 반응은 긍정적인 모습.
삼성전자는 실적 내고 제자리이지만 배터리는 동반강세 시현.

바이오는 펩트론 하한가, 알테오젠 -5%대로 급락나오는 중.
펩트론은 일라이릴리 기술평가 종료됐고 상업화 계약 없었음.
나중에 나올지 어떨지 모르겠으나 일단은 결실이 없기에 실망.
한미약품도 식약처 비만신약 허가 셀온 나오며 -7% 급락나옴.
비만 신약 가격에 대한 왈가왈부도 심한 상태로 보임. 

원전과 전력기기는 오늘도 약세를 이어가며 힘을 못쓰는 중.
두산에너빌리티 -5%, LS ELECTRIC -4%대로 동반하락.
방산과 조선 등 산업재도 철저히 소외되며 코스피 부진에 기여

이제 삼성전자 실적과 FOMC 의사록은 지나간 이슈가 되버림.
오후엔 옵션만기와 반도체 ETF 리밸런싱 남고, 내일은 휴장임.
오늘은 수급적인 이벤트까지 겹쳐서 눈치싸움이 치열해보임.

순환매가 나오는게 쏠림보다는 낫지만 코스피 추세는 애매함.
하루 단위로 급등과 급락이 반복하며 정신을 쏙 빼놓는 장임.
어설프게 매매하면 잔손실만 커질 수 밖에 없는 그런 장세.
시장은 아직도 시간이 더 필요하겠구나 싶은 그런 모습임. 

어제 의견 물어보니 대동단결로 삼성전자 하락을 봐서 놀랐음.
아직까진 약보합인데, 오후로가면 더 빠질거라고 보는지? 
오늘 ETF 리밸런싱 앞두고 다들 어떻게 대응하고있는지 궁금.

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

Embeddings are like a general vibe check. They turn text into number blobs that show overall similarity, but exact words can throw them off.

Decision models are like a scorecard. They rate specific things you pick (skills, interests) with clear scores and reasons.

Example: Matching friends for a hike.

Embedding might pair two people who both mention "outdoors" even if one hates walking.

Decision model checks "enjoys hiking? yes/no score" and "free Saturdays?" so matches stay accurate.

text:
根据近来的时间线和调查内容得出了一些分析

总结一下：
1.这个用户存了50BTC，三天后，Solv的合约部署者私钥泄漏了，所以这笔存款构成了这起安全事件的攻击路径所利用的重要条件。
2.有地址私钥，不代表你有这些资金和地址的控制权
3.证明控制权的时候，用户说错了一些交易的时间，所以这地址不是你的

目前来看，这个用户需要
1.部署者的地址泄漏，和用户存款50BTC没有关系
2.证明自己不是黑客
3.发动鬼脑记住这个地址上所有交易的具体时间和作用，错了一个字也不行

一些补充内容
事主 7 月 8 日 19:12 申购了 48.98 BTC+（交易）。这个钱包的下一笔交易要到 7 月 17 日。他的币安 Web3 钱包在攻击前后也一笔交易都没发过。

7 月 13 日 01:01:52，Solv 自己的部署者地址部署了一个恶意合约。11 秒后，同一地址把 BTC+ 的铸币合约升级成了这个恶意合约。

这个恶意合约：它只有一个铸币函数，不检查调用者，也不读任何存储，等于谁都能凭空铸币。

孟岩在文章中说到，在用户存入3天就发生了攻击，实际上是4天6小时，并非三天。

7 月 13 日 Solv 拉黑了 9 批可疑地址，因为部署者私钥泄漏后，期间铸造了38 张赎回凭证，合计约 195 BTC+。

7 月 31 日 15:42，事主被单独拉黑，那一批只有他一个地址。37 分钟后，Solv 发帖宣布恢复赎回。

根据Solv论坛的事后报告，他们称所有底层BTC资产均保持完全安全。https://t.co/H7anUEuYYR

根据查询结果，当时Solv在链上储备只有60.8BTC，其中包含事主存进去的50BTC，因此我们大概可以还原出来Solv的思路应该是。以下内容均为我根据公开内容和事实进行推测和推演的可能性产物。否则我很难想明白为什么要冻结50BTC

1. 他们认为黑客是个一个笨蛋，并不知道他们的赎回是手动的
2.他们认为，在私钥泄漏前忽然存入50BTC，是非常愚蠢的行为，是有目的，有组织的
3.他们认为，黑客存入这50BTC的目的，就是在赌，可以正常赎回非法铸造的BTC，然后再用这50BTC的合法证据去取回或者维权（但是我个人想法来说，如果黑客这么蠢，应该要被电死，而且我们知道，一般来说，项目被盗了，大概率是没有赔偿的）

个人认为，也有可能这些BTC有点点坏账，刚好平账了。
所谓的安全审查在这种关联上来说，我感觉，基本站不住脚，所以我更倾向是否有其他原因或者无法告人的理由。
