author: origin_trail
quoted_text:
Global supply chains, on TRAC(k)

The United States imported $3.4 trillion of goods in 2025. The @SCANAssociation helps secure the supply chains behind around 40% of US imports.

SCAN's members include @Costco, @Walmart, @Target, and @HomeDepot and many of them buy from the same factories. Instead of each importer auditing the same factory against the same US customs security criteria (CTPAT), they share the audit reports. 

In 2025 alone, SCAN members avoided 10,159 duplicate factory audits this way, across 93 countries.

The audits are secured on the @origin_trail Decentralized Knowledge Graph (DKG):
→ Each audit result and factory credential becomes a tamper-evident record that can be checked at the source
→ Members and US Customs and Border Protection can check a factory's audit history without one central database owning it
→ Access stays permissioned, so sensitive audit data reaches only those entitled to see it

One audit, verified once, trusted across the network. The same pattern fits any industry where the same compliance evidence is requested again and again.

Trust the source.

Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

author: EliBenSasson
quoted_text:
Do the labs have better algorithms for breaking crypto?

Independent of the answer, the most important thing is to have crypto agility. Zcash has proven this, with 3 upgrades happening in 6 months, and Tachyon planned for January. The protocol design has plans for how to turn off features to enable safe protocol upgrades. This is what Quantum Recoverability is, and it applies equally well if there's a non-quantum ECDLP attack.

We're equipped on multiple fronts to protect against future bugs. In the next cryptography upgrade, coming January, already slated features are:
- PQ transparent
- Switching to Tachyon

What people don't realize about Tachyon is it switches us to R1CS, and enables far more crypto agility away from elliptic curves. The nullifier derivation no longer depend on elliptic curves. We get far greater SNARK agility and can very quickly move to STARKs when any crisis comes.

Today's Zcash transparent UTXO's give a better security guarantee than an ETH address. @ZakuraZcash has solved the privacy and performance problem that were blocking rotating T-Addresses natively in the wallet. This is done using PIR to fetch balances, and its already live in Vizor. So its a short UX leap to get this backup plan.

In January, the Transparent pool will be upgraded to support hash based sigs, that can later be STARK aggregated.

text:
TL;DR for people who don't know cryptography:

Every Bitcoin wallet has a public key and a private key.

Your private key lets you spend your BTC, so it's known only to you.

Your public key is used for receiving btc. BTC relies on elliptic-curve cryptography to protect private keys. 

Public key can be visible when transacting, because with today's math, deriving private key from public key is effectively impossible.

Drake is worried AI could discover a mathematical shortcut that changes that.

If that happens, anyone whose public key is already exposed (early btc transactions exposed it) could have their coins stolen.

That's why he's telling people to move funds to fresh addresses whose public keys are still hidden, and rotate addresses after spending.

Interestingly, most of Satoshi's BTC already has its public keys exposed, so it will be the first target for the attack :)

text:
STRC 从入坑到盈利：入坑始末！

现在 STRC 的价格已经趋于稳定，基本回锚了。

早先持有STRC、sUSDat、apyUSD的小伙伴，只要没中途割肉，大多也已经实现盈利。

可就在几个月前，情况完全不是这样。

我按计划只动用高风险仓位的一部分，却在一轮轮下跌里把这部分几乎打光，浮亏一度超过 30%。

这不是简单的 "抄底被套"，更像一场突如其来的 DeFi 考试。

题目是：STRC 相关生息代币在除息与脱锚时会怎么走，实际答卷却比当时以为的复杂得多。

后来复盘才看清，关键不在于要不要碰 STRC，而在于这些代币之间的系数关系一旦错位，就会出现可操作的价差。

社区里不少朋友对套利路径感兴趣，所以我打算把这次从入坑、被套到自救盈利的过程拆成系列。

本篇先回顾我是怎么在价格还稳的时候，把高风险仓位全部打进去的。

如果没记错，STRC 和链上项目 Apyx 在 X 上被频繁讨论时，还是在 3、4月，那时市场低迷，CeFi 和 DeFi 频繁被盗！

我观望了很久，直到看到 Apyx的 "稳定币" apxUSD 上线 Kraken（这也是坑，后续还有 SpaceX 打新不给筹码的事儿） 的消息。

奔着要干就干票大的，我决定放弃 apxUSD 的低年化（当时也知道它其实有STRC敞口），转而把高风险仓位的 1/5 投入有 STRC 敞口的生息代币 apyUSD，追求当时大约 40% 的年化。

当时很多人也在看这类高息机会，我选择只动用限定仓位，是想把风险锁在自己能承受的范围内。

随后，另一个链上 STRC 项目 Saturn 进入视野。

它和 Apyx 有点类似，也有两个代币：稳定币 USDat，以及有 STRC 敞口的 sUSDat。

sUSDat比较特殊：它的净值会跟着STRC除息而下跌（大致是年化除以12个月的幅度），而按照除息规律，除息后价格通常会回归锚定。

于是我又分配了1/5的高风险仓位，用做 sUSDat 的除息跌幅与价格回归。

因为回归需要时间，除息后我通常还会再持有 15 天左右。

这样一来，sUSDat 的账面收入就包含除息跌幅和持有利息，前两个月大概能有 2-3% 的收益。

到这时，我以为情况会是这样：直到 10 月 Apyx 和 Saturn TGE 之前，我可以在 STRC 相关资产上收获大约半年、40% 左右的年化。

时间往前走，5 月底刚进入 6 月初，STRC 除息后并没有马上企稳，而是继续下跌。

6 月 4 日晚，跌幅接近 8%，链上与 STRC 强相关的 sUSDat 同步下跌。

我按照脱锚逻辑继续抄底，等待回归。

如果只是 sUSDat 下跌，一切还算在预料之中。

可 Apyx 那边的情况完全出乎意料。

作为稳定币的 apxUSD，之前从未与 STRC 同步下跌，这次居然跟跌。

更要命的是 apyUSD 跌得更加夸张，一度达到 30%！

万幸的是，我之前为了做 YT 波段，把 apyUSD 的循环拆了几层，才没有被清算。

面对这样的跌幅，认为 STRC 不会完蛋的我选择继续加仓，最终让 apyUSD 和 sUSDat 各占高风险仓位的一半。

其中跌的最惨的 apyUSD 仓位还包含着循环贷，导致浮亏 50% 以上，而当时 STRC 本身的跌幅只有约 7%。

当时群里也有不少人在讨论要不要继续加，有人选择观望，有人直接离场。

但没想到，噩梦和煎熬才刚刚开始。

6 月 6 日和 6 月 27 日，STRC 又迎来两次巨幅下跌，最低时只有锚定的 68% 左右。

而我的高风险仓位，还没等到后面这两次下跌，就已经打完了。

仓位规划救了我，让我没把全部资金都打进去。

但正因为只动用了有限的高风险仓位并要坚决执行，只能用现有仓位，想办法辗转腾挪，开始自救。

下一篇我会讲第一次最有效的套利路径。

来自对 apxUSD 和 apyUSD 系数关系的重新梳理！

text:
Seeing people celebrate the downfall of Abstract and throw fud at Luca Netz tells me they don't know anything 

Luca is one of the most ambitious, hardworking founders in crypto, and I think people are incredibly quick to forget what someone has accomplished.

He took Pudgy Penguins from a struggling NFT collection to one of the most recognizable consumer brands in crypto, expanded into mainstream retail, created enormous amounts of wealth and opportunity for people throughout the entire pengu ecosystem.

He's contributed more to bringing this industry forward than the vast majority (combined) of people criticizing him.

Now, Abstract didn't work out. After losing tens of millions of dollars, he chose to shut it down rather than launch a token which would go to zero, putting focus where it belongs.

You have to respect that decision.

People forget that building anything ambitious involves a lot of failure.

Elon Musk's SpaceX had three failed launches before reaching orbit in 2008, multiple failed booster landing attempts before successfully landing a rocket back on Earth in 2015. The company was on the verge of bankruptcy in its early years and look what happened.

Crypto is an incredibly fast moving industry. Narratives shift, business models become obsolete, and even the most talented founders will make bets that don't work out. It's natural.

How I measure founders isn't by whether every bet succeeds. It's what they build over time, how they handle failure, and whether they have the conviction to make difficult decisions when circumstances change.

You can criticize Abstract without discrediting everything Luca has built.

I'll continue backing him, and I have little doubt he'll go on to build more great things.

This industry needs more people willing to take ambitious risks, not fewer.

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
谷歌系 AI 药企 Isomorphic Labs 新一轮估值 400- 500 亿美元，差不多 3 个TEM+RXRX+SDGR

1｜这家公司现在有什么
- 英国公司 2025 年报：营业收入 0，药企合作给的钱记作其他收入 5523 万英镑，研发 1.9 亿英镑，净亏 1.59 亿英镑，平均 225 人。
- 手里的牌是药企合作：礼来 $LLY 里程碑最高 17 亿美元，诺华 $NVS 最高 12 亿，今年 1 月又签了强生 $JNJ。里程碑是药做到某个阶段、药企才付的分期款，写的是上限，不是收入。

2｜一级到底在买什么
买的是人加平台。
- 人是 Hassabis：2024 年诺贝尔化学奖。今年 8 月把 DeepMind CEO 交了出去，转任 DeepMind 董事长，出任 Alphabet 首位首席科学家，Isomorphic 的 CEO 继续兼着。
- 平台是 AlphaFold 3，和 DeepMind 一起做出来的。再往后是 Alphabet，年报写得明白，控股方就是它。
- 融资结构更说明问题。两轮都是 Thrive 领投，B 轮 Alphabet、GV 跟投，MGX、淡马锡、CapitalG、英国主权 AI 基金新进。同一家连续领投，谷歌自己的基金也在里面。

3｜二级怎么给同一个故事定价
- 莫德纳 $MRNA，有上市产品、有收入，8/19 三期结果出来前股价约 63 美元，现在 196，市值约 784 亿美元。400 到 500 亿，差不多 2/3 个莫德纳。
- 递归制药 $RXRX 市值约 22.9 亿美元。一个零收入的 Isomorphic，抵二十个左右的 RXRX。再加上薛定谔 $SDGR 约 20.4 亿、Tempus AI $TEM 约 126.9 亿，三家合计 170 亿，500 亿是它的 2.9 倍。

4｜一级热完，轮到二级
AIDD、AI4S 在一级已经热了大半年。
这轮要是按 400 亿以上关掉，等于给整条赛道立了个价锚。
一级热完，二级应该还有半年到一年的机会。

Genuine on-chain research differs significantly from engagement farming. Unfortunately, @bubblemaps seems increasingly interested in the latter.

The irony? Frank had already sold his $EDEL, exited other positions and opened leveraged shorts before this narrative resurfaced. 

Love or hate him, @frankdegods is one of, if not the best, realised PnL traders; he doesn't take backhand deals, so he can stay agile and unencumbered. This is factual. 

Bubblemaps, you failed again, the information was already outdated before the tweet went live.

Let's discuss some actual fundamentals.

• Nearly 40% of $EDEL supply remains outside circulation, including publicly disclosed allocations. The team voluntarily relocked its tokens in March for another 12 months, 10% locked to ensure 1:1 $EDEL:$EDELx on @CantonNetwork, nearly $4m in liquidity across @base, @RobinhoodCrypto, @Solana, and as mentioned Canton.

• Presale tokens are 100% vested, with most participants having already exited.

• Edel is generating $10K–$50K in daily revenue(public), supporting token buybacks(undefined for the minute) and building a sustainable runway without relying on treasury token sales.

• When the xStocks $GOOG pricing discrepancy occurred and there was an exploit, the affected Edel users were made whole.

• Edel continues building institutional-grade infrastructure across tokenisation, credit and derivatives on Canton and Base.

As someone who has engaged with the team on and off since before TGE, I've seen firsthand the maturity of the product, the depth of thought behind its usability and sustainability, and most importantly, the team's willingness to evolve and pivot towards genuine revenue generation.

That last point is something the industry doesn't give nearly enough credit to.

Web3 was supposed to be about democratising finance. Broader access, equal opportunity and financial infrastructure that doesn't exclusively benefit the institutions controlling it.

Edel is actually working towards that vision, while building a business capable of sustaining itself.

Catching up with the CEO in Singapore only reinforced my conviction. Being privy to some of the conversations and interactions with major institutional players and supporters across the Canton and Base ecosystem gave me an even greater appreciation for the scale of what they're building.

These are the conversations that matter. Not recycled wallet diagrams designed to generate impressions.

As @TraderSZ highlighted, context matters. Historical wallet activity without consideration for current supply dynamics, revenue, product development or institutional relationships is an incomplete picture at best.

What I find particularly interesting is the motivation.

In an industry overflowing with projects generating zero revenue, endless emissions and little more than promises, why repeatedly target one of the few sub-$100M Web3 companies actually generating meaningful revenue and reinvesting it into its ecosystem?

I'm all for accountability. Teams should be scrutinised, token movements questioned and claims independently verified.

But scrutiny without context isn't research. And recycling old narratives while ignoring material developments isn't protecting investors.

There's a difference between understanding a blockchain transaction and understanding the business behind it.

One takes a few clicks. The other requires actual due diligence.

author: bneiluj
quoted_text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

text:
硅谷的 VC 最近多了一种焦虑：创始人用了致幻剂之后，万一真的想通了，不想创业了怎么办？

David Senra 最新一期采访了好莱坞大亨 Ari Emanuel，就是那个一手打造 Endeavor、花 42 亿美元收购 UFC 的狠人。

这期播客里有两段特别有意思，一段关于马斯克与 AI，另一段关于致幻剂正在硅谷创业圈流行。

先说致幻剂。

Senra 今年 3 月采访 a16z 创始人 Marc Andreessen 时提到，他已经采访了十几位顶级创始人，几乎每期都会聊到 Psychedelics（致幻剂），甚至不断有人劝他也试试。

Marc 对此深恶痛绝。他说自己知道不少案例，一些创业者因为压力太大，尝试致幻剂后突然获得了内心的平静，随后辞掉工作、放弃公司，跑去印尼当冲浪教练。

他还专门跟神经科学家 Andrew Huberman 抱怨过这件事。

Huberman 反问他：「你怎么知道他们没有变得更幸福？」

Marc 的回答很绝：「可他们的公司垮了啊。」

这次采访 Ari Emanuel，Senra 又把这件事拿出来讨论，结果 Ari 直接骂了回去，认为 Marc 完全是在胡扯。

Ari 自己就是致幻剂的使用者。

2022 年，他和当时的伴侣去了新墨西哥州，尝试一种叫 5-MeO-DMT 的强效致幻剂。他回忆，自己经历了大约十分钟的意识断联和随后半小时的致幻体验，突然觉得人类在整个世界面前渺小得可笑。

他开始觉得，自己过去几十年拼命追求的所谓 Legacy（身后留下的伟大遗产），其实没那么重要。

但他并没有因此失去野心。现在依然每天早上五点起床、健身、工作，继续收购资产、建立新公司。

他的意思很简单，放下对名声和财富排名的执念，不妨碍自己继续享受做生意。

还有一个细节。Ari 从小患有阅读障碍，长期觉得自己没有兄弟聪明，几十年来一直被某种不安全感驱动。他后来逐渐意识到，自己过去引以为傲的愤怒与好胜心，也让婚姻、家庭和生活付出了相当大的代价。

所以我觉得 Marc 和 Ari 的分歧很值得玩味。

Marc 担心致幻剂会让创业者失去驱动力，Ari 则认为，一个人可以不再依赖焦虑和自我怀疑，也依然拥有野心。

某种程度上，在 Marc 的世界里，创始人的痛苦似乎也是商业系统的生产资料。你把痛苦解决了，投资人反而不高兴了。

另外一段关于马斯克的内容，也很精彩。

Ari 说，自己当年看到马斯克开始造车的新闻，就主动打电话联系他，两人由此成为朋友。

他回忆，马斯克早在 2007 年就开始跟他讨论 AI 的未来。后来，当他们聊到娱乐产业时，马斯克告诉他，AI 很难取代的一样东西是 Live Entertainment。

这句话对 Ari 的商业决策影响很大。

他现在除了经营 UFC、WWE 所在的 TKO，还建立了 MARI，持续布局网球公开赛、Frieze 艺术博览会、汽车拍卖、宝可梦收藏品活动等现场体验资产。

一个很有意思的判断是，AI 让数字内容的生产和复制越来越便宜，但一场真实发生的比赛、一场万人参与的演唱会、一次不可复刻的现场体验，其稀缺性可能反而在上升。

我觉得这两段放在一起，挺能反映当下美国科技精英的精神状态。

一方面，他们正在积极寻找 AI 时代新的稀缺资产；另一方面，一部分创业者已经开始重新审视那种永远不满足、永远要赢、永远不能停下来的生活。

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

关于@axisrobotics Hub 任务参与方式很明确

选择任务，完成机器人轨迹，提交结果，持续积累自己的任务记录，赚取未来奖励

看似抓杯子、移动方块、推拉物体等这些简单任务

但如果 Axis 后面真的把这些任务沉淀成可组合的Expert，这些早期轨迹就可能成为技能库里最基础的一层数据。

这也很多人比较关注 Axis 的地方。

我觉得 Axis 和很多机器人数据项目真正值得看的差异，核心是它在尝试把一次性的任务，沉淀成可以复用、可以衔接的 Expert。

抓取有自己的 Expert，放置有自己的 Expert，推拉也有自己的 Expert。

如果这些 Expert 可以组合起来，那训练一个任务的价值，就不再局限于这个任务本身。

它可能会成为机器人完成下一项任务的基础能力。

这就很关键。

因为机器人最终需要的不是一万个互不相干的演示。

它需要的是一套可以调用、组合、迁移的技能。

从 Task 到 Skill，再从 Skill 到 Skill Library。

值得注意的点！Axis 最近给出的实验数据也开始验证这条思路。

单任务 Expert 用 A100 训练大约 3 到 6 小时，纯算力成本约 5 到 10 美元，成功率接近 100%。

另一组实验里，仿真策略迁移到真机，再加入少量真实成功数据，成功率从约 22% 提升到 52%。

不过，别把 5 到 10 美元理解成训练一台机器人只要这么多钱，数据采集、工程开发、真机部署这些成本都还在。

但如果单项技能真的可以低成本规模化训练，再通过真机数据持续修正，最后形成可以复用的 Expert，那么整个机器人训练过程就有机会从一次次定制项目，变成不断扩充的技能库。

所以，Hub 里的任务意义也变了。

我们做任务是为了拿积分。

但从 Axis 的路线来看，在给某一个机器人技能补数据。
想参与的，直接去 Axis Hub 做任务就行。

进入 Axis Hub → 连接账号 → 浏览开放任务 → 选择不同类型任务 → 完成轨迹 → 提交 → 持续积累。

入口→https://t.co/50Box8ZzpX

撸积分的，建议别只刷一种任务。

有意识地覆盖抓取、移动、放置、推拉等不同能力，看看自己的任务记录最后能不能覆盖一条完整的技能链。

因为如果 Axis 后面真的把 Skill Library 和技能关系做出来，那现在积累的这些任务记录，会是你参与贡献过哪些机器人技能。

Tips: 本文无任何投资建议，仅自己参与项目记录，DYOR~

text:
Unlike many networks, Solana users don't need to go into "bunker mode" ahead of an accelerated quantum timeline or classical attack provided by AI.
 
Solana uses Ed25519, where each signing key is derived by hashing a secret seed. Breaking the curve, whether by a quantum computer or a classical attack, would expose the derived key, but not the seed, and seeds are never exposed onchain. With a one-time network upgrade, rightful owners could prove knowledge of their seed using a hash-based proof and move their accounts to a safe signature scheme. A working proof of concept already exists: https://t.co/am2ErkkomT.
 
Solana remains secure today and has a defined path forward.

We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

再看 NEAR。这个币更拧巴，很多人拿了几年没赚钱，骂它骂到麻木。但有件事被严重低估：NEAR Intents 已经跑了 300 多亿美元跨链成交，接了 35 条链。你在 Zashi 钱包里换 ZEC，背后走的就是 NEAR。

你手里那些拿了一年没动的币，别指望它们突然想起来补涨。

贪心和侥幸，是比踏空更贵的东西。

quoted_text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

Starknet is based on ZK-STARKs, it has crypto agility, and an active migration roadmap to PQS.

But as an L2, Starknet relies on the security of its L1, Ethereum.

We’ll need Ethereum to become quantum-safe and AI-safe, and we’ll need it to happen fast. Real fast. 

What happens if it doesn’t?
We’re considering multiple options, including becoming an L1.

The advantage would be control over the network’s security migrations, rather than having to wait for Ethereum or Bitcoin to move first.

For context, Ethereum is targeting full L1 quantum resistance by the end of 2029. Bitcoin has made no such commitment. Starknet could get there by 2027.

Starknet has the right architecture to be a future-proofed network, a place to trade, earn, pay, and HODL, publicly or privately, with quantum-resistant security and crypto agility.

text:
OpenAI 一夜放出了 722 篇数学论文，币圈关心的不是黎曼猜想这种数学话题，而是AI带来的风险，你的币该放在哪种地址上。

昨晚 Justin Drake @drakefjustin   呼吁行业提前规划“bunker mode”（地堡模式）：他担心 AI 加速的数学突破可能先于量子计算威胁到 ECDSA签名算法，建议从大户开始，有序地把资产迁到“公钥还藏在哈希后面”的新地址。

Vitalik 随后表示，不建议任何人立即就慌忙转移，但这个风险要认真对待；Adam Back @adam3us  则直接称之为“AI 恐慌”，并指向 Blockstream 基于哈希的签名方案 SHRINCS。

目前没有任何公开证据表明 ECDSA 已被攻破。但这场讨论里有一个细节，我看很多人都没有说：

“换个新地址”这招，对 bc1p 类型的地址不管用。

📍1… / 3… / bc1q…：链上只记录公钥（或脚本）的哈希，首次花费之前，公钥不公开
📍bc1p…（Taproot）：输出里直接就是一把 32 字节的公钥（tweak 过的），收到币的那一刻就暴露了
📍早期 P2PK 的币：公钥一直在链上
📍任何花费过的地址：公钥已经公开，重复使用的地址都属于这一类

严格来说，受威胁的是椭圆曲线离散对数这个底层难题，ECDSA 和 Taproot 用的 Schnorr 签名都建立在它之上。所以如果这个风险真的提前到来，bc1p 反而是最先“裸奔”的一类。

当然我们不必恐慌，可以做几件低成本的事做防御：

✅不要重复使用地址，这本来就是基本的安全习惯
✅长期冷存储，优先用从未花费过的 bc1q 等哈希类地址
✅关注 BIP-360（P2MR，原名 P2QRH，去掉了 Taproot 的密钥路径）和 SHRINCS 的进展，两者目前都还是草案

最后补充一点：花费时公钥会随交易广播出去，所以哈希地址只是缩小暴露面，不是根治，真正的解决还是要靠协议层的升级。

你的币主要放在哪种地址呢？

author: dapangdun
quoted_text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

text:
you're thinking too small. i don't need terabytes of random bits. i need a seed and a complete rejection of elliptic curves.

from this seed i grow an astronomical number of one-time secrets. each secret becomes a hash chain. you can walk forward through the chain but never backward. i arrange these chains into winternitz one-time signatures, and their public keys become leaves of merkle trees. those trees become leaves of larger trees. trees all the way up. a hypertree.

but first, at the bottom, i plant the FOREST OF RANDOM SUBSETS. FORS. the message is reduced to a string of ones and zeros. groups of bits select leaves from independent merkle trees. i reveal the corresponding secrets and the neighboring hashes, and you reconstruct the roots. the roots become a single hash. this is the message's signature, born from the forest.

now i sign that hash with a winternitz key. i prove the key belongs to a merkle tree by revealing its authentication path. i sign that tree's root with another key from the tree above. and again. and again. we ascend through layers of hash chains and sibling nodes until the entire structure collapses into ONE ROOT.

32 bytes. that's my public key. the entire forest is committed to those 256 bits.

i don't store the forest. i don't even remember which leaves i've used. the forest is deterministically regenerated from the seed whenever i need it. the message itself tells me where to go.

there are no elliptic curves here. no discrete logarithms. no hidden algebraic relationship waiting for a mathematician to invert. only preimages, hashes, and an unfathomable number of ones and zeros arranged into trees whose branches authenticate each other.

you can have my elliptic curves. you can have my RSA. but you cannot have the forest.

the forest is stateless. the forest remembers nothing. the forest verifies everything.

卧槽，当年轰动国内 AI 圈的“字节投毒实习生”田柯宇，现在杀回来了！

刚刷到彭博今天专门发了一篇对他的采访。

田柯宇 @keyutian  现在自己出来创业做世界模型，公司甚至还没有正式名字、没有产品，只有 10 个人，却已经从五源资本、IDG 等机构融了接近 3000 万美元，投后估值接近 2 亿美元。

而且这哥们现在做的东西还挺有意思。

简单来说，他觉得：人类的语言其实根本不适合描述这个世界。

比如你想用文字完整描述一段视频，里面每一个物体的位置、运动、光影、物理变化，基本是不可能的。

所以他的思路是，干脆别让 AI 使用人类语言理解视频了。

他们直接让 AI 自己发明一门语言。

他们现在已经做出了一套类似词典的东西，里面大概有 20 万个符号，人类完全看不懂，但 AI 可以拿这些符号去表示、压缩和预测视频。

接下来他们准备喂进去大约 1 亿小时的视频，让模型通过这套自己的语言去学习现实世界。

最终目标不是视频生成，不是World Model，是希望做一个基座模型：

让 AI 真正理解空间、运动和物理规律，未来可以作为机器人、自动驾驶、交互式视频这些东西的基础模型。

田柯宇说，这套方法目前已经能让视频生成效率提升至少一个数量级。

他们计划先做公开 Demo，甚至是直播，完整模型则准备在 2027 年发布。

现阶段不着急做消费级产品，也暂时不考虑怎么商业化，就是先怼基座模型。

田柯宇这个人，我其实之前就写过。

他离开字节之后，他还作为一作拿了 NeurIPS 2024 Best Paper。

那篇论文我当时专门看过，我印象特别深，因为它做的事情其实很暴力：就是想办法把视觉生成这件事，变得更像 LLM 一样，可以不断 Scaling，同时把生成成本和复杂度往下降。

我当时看完就觉得，这个人能力是真的很牛逼。

所以后来网上一直在讨论他当年在字节的事情，我其实也一直挺好奇到底发生了什么。

因为当时中文互联网传得特别夸张，什么“投毒大模型”、造成几百万甚至八百万损失，各种版本都有，已经快传成 AI 圈都市传说了hhhh

结果这次彭博终于把很多以前不知道的细节补出来了。

田柯宇自己承认，当时他为了释放算力，直接关掉了另一个实习生超额占用计算资源的程序，他现在也觉得当时这种“以火攻火”的处理方式是错的。

但另一方面，字节当年其实也明确说过，网上关于他破坏基础模型训练的很多传言存在误导。

最后法院判下来的结果，是他因为违反合同赔偿 50 万人民币，把自己在字节拿到的工资全部退了回去

这个结果跟当年网上传的那些版本，差距还是挺大的。

所以我今天早上看到这篇采访还挺感慨的。

因为我最早认识田柯宇这个名字，不是因为这次创业，甚至也不完全是因为字节那件事，而是后来真的去看了他的论文。

当时我的感觉就是：这人确实是有东西的。

现在再看，他离开字节之后拿 Best Paper，继续沿着自己的技术路线做世界模型，然后一个 10 人团队、产品都还没有，就融了接近 3000 万美元，估值快 2 亿美元。

至少从技术能力这件事情上，我觉得之前那个判断没错。

这个人，确实挺牛逼的。

加油啊，等你们新的roadmap！

text:
三个大事件和一个趋势，让X平台在政治、地缘、科技AI和金融这些高度重视时效的领域，越来越成为全球范围内的信息中心，也越来越成为全球最有影响力的社交媒体平台（没有之一）。三个大事件：24年美国总统大选、25年关税战、26年伊朗战争（伊朗最高领袖、总统、议长、外长都启用X账号发声）；
一个趋势就是AI公司和科技领袖越来越倾向在X上发布动态、营销，打口水仗。详细说说：

1、2024年美国总统大选：关键政治人物的发声，本身就能成为平台上的重大事件
2024年7月13日，川普遇刺，这个事件迅速在网络上发酵，X是最主要的传播和讨论平台。
2024年7月21日，拜登通过社交媒体发布退选信，X是主要发布渠道之一。24年8月12日，特朗普与马斯克直接在X Spaces进行访谈。
以及之后大选的民调、选情进展，还有大选投票日的实施进展，这类事件对X平台的影响，远远超过普通热点带来的一轮流量。
当公众发现重大决定可能由当事人直接发出来，记者、政治观察者、交易者就有动力持续监测相关账号。对新闻机构而言，守在现场的必要性也随之提高。

关键人物在这里发声，记者和分析者就会关注。记者和分析者持续关注，发声者就更容易获得平台之外的传播。这种传播效果被反复验证，其他关键人物也更愿意加入。对于我们这些普通投资人来说，自然也是获取相关资讯的最快渠道。

2、2025年关税战：持续监测政策消息，开始具有非常直接的经济价值
当时川普的声明首先发布在Truth Social，但被拿来快速传播和讨论几乎都是X平台，X 在这类事件中承担了迅速汇集、转播和解释的作用。

关税战强化了 X 的另一个属性：它成为市场参与者共同监测政策变化、讨论解释的重要场所。
对于投资者而言，消息的重要性取决于它能否改变盈利、通胀、利率或风险偏好。政策如果在交易时段发生变化，持续监测的价值就会上升。

3、2026年的伊朗战争：交战方直接进入全球舆论和市场预期的争夺
这一次伊朗最高领袖开始启用X账号对外发声，战争提高了既有高层账号的国际关注度，新任最高领袖也迅速启用了官方账号。

一条公开表态可能同时被外交人员、记者和投资者阅读。不同受众会分别判断它是否意味着谈判立场改变、航运风险变化，或能源价格需要重新评估。以至于大家都觉得伊朗高层也学会了川普利用社交媒体来影响舆论的套路。

4、而“AI公司和科技领袖商业大佬越来越倾向在X上发布动态、营销，打口水仗”的这个趋势影响则更为深远
黄仁勋最近都注册了X账号开始频繁发生、扎克伯格时隔三年重新启用X账号，苹果新人CEO于9月1日首次在X上公开发帖。

LVMH 的 Bernard Arnault 在今年7月开始使用个人 X 账号，回应关于其家族和接班安排的报道；
传媒业的 David Ellison 则于10月2日首次使用 X 发布重大公司消息。

AI 产品的一个特点是，发布者可以同时给出演示、链接或测试入口，专业用户随后就能提出问题。
一次传播有可能很快从“公司宣布了什么”，进入“实际表现怎样”“哪些条件下有效”“和另一家相比有什么差别”的讨论。
对企业来说，这种即时反馈有产品价值，也有营销价值。对用户来说，原作者与专业人士的来回回应，有时比单独阅读发布稿更有信息量。

你想想一下，一个普通X账户讨论grok bot、英伟达等新闻，引来的老马和老黄的点赞、评论甚至转发，对于普通人来说不仅是巨大的曝光量，还有巨大的成就感。

当然这种趋势已经不至于AI领域，加密领域更早，其他行业也越来越多。这给 X 带来了一种相对持续的内容供给，而且发布者、评价者、产品开发者和商业决策者之间高度重叠。

5、这背后的逻辑是啥？
1）X的信息内容传播机制：公开关注和引用帖，让内容能够跨越原有圈层
X 的公开帖子可以沿关注关系传播。转帖保留原作者的内容和身份；引用帖则允许用户附加自己的评论，形成一条新的传播入口。

这种结构很适合专业信息跨圈传播。
例如，假设一名工程师写了一段芯片技术分析，AI 研究人员引用并补充，投资者再讨论对产业链的含义，记者随后联系当事人核实。同一份原始材料就可能经过几次互动，进入多个不同圈子。

每一次专业回应，都有机会让原信息接触到新的受众。
争论同样具有这种作用。一个有影响力的人反驳另一方时，也可能把对方的观点介绍给自己的关注者。因此，企业之间的公开争论有时会同时增加双方的曝光。

2）X聚集了大量“会继续传播信息的人”
政治领导人、政治家、科技大佬、商业领袖、金融投资大佬、各行业资深人士以及越老越多涌现的不同类型的博主，这些人本身就有发声的需求，也愿意传播有价值信息，当然更想让自己的观点被更多人的看到。

假设一条消息被一万个人看到，其中有大量记者、研究人员和行业意见领袖，那么后续传播可能远远超过这一万次直接触达。
就产生了一个有趣的场景：
这些人还会在自己的文章、节目、邮件和其他社交平台上继续讨论。最终受众可能没有打开过 X，却仍然接触到了从 X 进入公共讨论的议题。

这回形成马太效应，越来越多的政治名人、科技商业大佬会把X当作首选发声平台。

3）不可忽视老马的示范作用
他本人持续给平台提供值得关注的议题，马斯克涉及科技、企业经营和政治讨论，使平台拥有一个频繁制造新闻、也频繁回应新闻的人物。
这会让一部分用户即使对平台其他内容兴趣有限，也有动力继续关注。他的回复和互动，可以把新加入者迅速带进既有圈子

马斯克在多个圈层的存在，也让一条原本只属于科技圈的话题，有机会进入投资或政治讨论。

他强化了企业负责人直接发声的风格，对企业负责人来说，价值除了曝光，还包括很快接触到同行、合作伙伴及相关受众。

4）当然还有X自己的机制变化
关注关系提供稳定入口，推荐系统提供额外扩散。特别是启用AI算法之后，排序会预测用户可能发生的点赞、回复、转帖、分享、停留，以及负面反馈等行为，再综合打分。由此可以推断，突发变化、具有争议的技术判断、重要人物之间的回应，都可能形成持续互动，并获得进一步传播。

还有一点，文字本身就是一个低成本生产和低成本获取的内容形态。

所以当：
1）一手信源在这里。记者、交易员、研究员、政客、监管者和公司发言人的默认公共时间线仍是X。当最高领袖、总统、芯片CEO自己发帖时，二次传播的起点就在平台内；

2）短文本、引用帖、回复串、列表和Spaces的摩擦远低于长视频或闭源社群；算法按互动把高争议、高时效内容顶上来，所以政治、地缘和行情类信息的“第一波”往往先在这里完成扩散，再被路透、彭博、CNN等转写。Community Notes和放开后的言论尺度也让原本被限流的政治内容重新聚集。

这就导致了X还不是最大社交网络，总用户也只超过10亿，活跃用户估计也只有五到六亿，但X已经成为精英和实时公共讨论的密度最高的地方。特别是在政治、地缘、财经和前沿科技这几条线上，最快的公共信息往往先发生在X，平台的议程影响力远超其他平台。

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

Had to explain it to a few folks, apparently it helps understanding the argument better.

- Elliptic cryptography (used in almost all blockchains) is built on clever tricks and fancy math assumptions, an engineering analogy would be self-stressed structures
- AI labs breaking math assumptions left and right lately, might break elliptic crypto too (maybe already did!)

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
IMF：代币化市场扩张面临四大障碍

国际货币基金组织（IMF）发文指出，代币化市场增长迅速，但整体规模仍小，不同平台之间相互割裂。法律权利不明确、监管规则不清晰、平台互操作性不足，以及缺乏安全的结算资产，是制约其发展的四大因素。

报告指出，超过一半的相关交易发生在传统市场交易时段之外，约 80% 的代币化股票交易单笔规模不足 1 股，显示投资者对延长交易时间和零股交易的需求。不过，代币化市场目前流动性较低、波动性较高，跨平台割裂也限制了网络效应。

IMF 警告，随着市场规模扩大，抛售、流动性争夺和风险传染可能加剧。政策制定者应明确代币化资产持有人的法律权利，对类似金融活动实施一致监管，推动平台与传统金融体系互联互通，并持续监测杠杆及流动性风险。

text:
在美读书实习打工的门槛更高了。美国国土安全部今早发布公告，计划对在美留学生的实习工作许可 OPT，加一笔手续费，首次申请校方要向美国政府缴纳 7 万美元，之后再申请需缴 3 万美元。

美国政府认为，OPT 本来只是跟专业相关的短期实习，现在被当成，外国人赴美留学后，留在当地工作的漏洞。

如果放任不管，会对本土毕业生有就业压力，增加费用就是为了让大学少推荐外国人，顺便给美国本地人腾出岗位。

因为当前很多赴美留学的，毕业后都是先用 12 个月短期实习 OPT 入职美国公司，公司那边同时帮你抽 H-1B 工作签证资格，而理工科还能再延 24 个月，等于毕业后在美国能靠这个呆 3 年。

按照该提案，交钱的不是学生，而是有资质的学校。学校必须先把钱交给美国政府，才能在系统里给学生推荐 OPT，而如果没交，移民局就不批工卡。

如果这项提案真落地，学校大概率今后，会把成本转给学生，比如纳入学费或周边费用，或者干脆少开实习推荐，让外国学生在美国毕业就回去。

text:
未暴露的比特币地址，是指对应公钥从未被写入区块链的地址。

在 P2PKH 与原生 SegWit（P2WPKH）等常见类型中，地址本身只是公钥的哈希；只要该地址仅有入账、从未作为交易输入完成过签名，公钥即保持隐藏。

一旦从该地址支出，公钥随签名脚本永久上链，地址即变为已暴露，且无法还原。

将已暴露地址中的资金转移到未暴露地址，不能改变原地址的暴露状态，但可使资产进入公钥仍受哈希保护的新地址。

具体做法是使用分层确定性钱包生成一个从未使用过的新地址，从已暴露地址发起交易，将余额直接支付至该新地址（或通过标准找零输出进入新派生的找零地址）。

交易确认后，新地址仅存在入账记录、尚无出账，因而属于未暴露地址。

此过程会在链上留下从旧地址到新地址的直接关联，但不导致新地址公钥暴露；原地址若已清空，则不再保有需保护的资金。

Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
Drake 的建议值得一听，我们的加密资产应该尽快全部进入“堡垒模式（Bunker）”。

所谓堡垒模式，说白了，就是更换地址。

现在我们用的老地址，大部分都做过签名了。而签名会暴露公钥（地址≠公钥，公开地址、接受转账都不会暴露公钥），他担心公钥被 AI 破解。

换个崭新的地址，且避免签名，自然就安全多了。

说说我的看法。

如今的公钥，依赖于椭圆曲线的难解，如果 AI 真的发现了椭圆曲线的漏洞，确实有被公钥反推导出私钥的可能性（当然，我个人认为概率极低）。

而如果你没暴露过公钥，就一个地址，从公钥到地址又多了一重哈希。哈希不太依赖于某些困难问题的解，安全性自然高一个档次。

另外，我倒是比 Drake 乐观一些，我依然相信 AI 的幻觉存在，要知道半年前，最聪明的 AI 还无法算出 9.11 和 9.9 哪个更大，一年前的 AI 数不清 strawberry 里有几个 r。

你说现在的 AI 会威胁到椭圆曲线么？我觉得重要但不紧急。

现在 A 社、O 社筹备上市，他们急需一些大新闻来论证他们的 AI 的强大，所以三天两头说破解数学问题，搞得大家都焦虑了。

再说了，天塌下来，还有高个子顶着，感谢中本聪，留下了 100w 个比特币，无论量子计算、AI 破解，大概率先瞄准中本聪遗产。

PS：因为当年中本聪用的 P2PK，公钥都已暴露。

宝贵的算力，不会第一时间，盯着咱们那三瓜两枣的。

感谢“中本聪之盾”吧。

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
I got a lot of thoughtful feedback after publishing the original post - thank you to everyone who took the time to read it, challenge the assumptions, and share data points. A few of the pushbacks changed how I think about the framework, so I wanted to write a short follow-up and lay out the main areas of disagreement.

Where the feedback roughly landed
Most clustered around ~0.2–0.3GW for standalone/agent CPU at 100M DAU, versus ~0.1GW in my original estimate.

Inference demand is all over the place.

---
1/ My CPU scope was too narrow.

My original CPU estimate focused mainly on the agent sandbox/VM. Separately, my inference estimate modeled GPUs, but did not include the head-node CPUs that support the GPU fleet.

One clarification: tool execution is not necessarily a separate CPU bucket. Browsers, code, and tools often run inside the sandbox itself; orchestration may run in a separate backend or share other CPU infrastructure.

So I now think about CPU demand as two main pieces:

Standalone / agent-execution CPU
Sandbox + the actual work happening inside it + some orchestration

Head-node CPU
CPU required alongside the GPU/XPU fleet ≈ GPU/XPU fleet × CPU attach rate

2/ The sandbox itself may need more CPU than I assumed.

The original estimate used the 2 vCPU environment exposed by Muse as a starting point. But provisioning a lightweight VM is different from the physical CPU consumed once agents are actively running browsers, code, tools, and multiple tasks.

The bigger long-term question is also whether one human request continues to map to one agent. A request could increasingly spawn 4–8 sub-agents, or eventually become agent → agent → agent. Usage will likely be highly skewed toward power users, and infrastructure also needs to be provisioned for peaks rather than averages.

A more complete framework is:

Standalone CPU demand
users
× tasks/user/day
× agents/task
× active time/agent
× physical CPU per active agent
× peak factor
There are a lot of moving pieces here, but I suspect agents per task is one of the biggest long-term swing factors.

3/ Inference may also be understated, but for a different reason.

The relevant unit probably isn’t simply “human messages per day.”

A consumer might only initiate 5–10 meaningful tasks per day, but one agent task could require dozens of model calls as the agent reasons, uses a tool, observes the result, reasons again, etc. So a better framework is:

GPU inference demand
users
× tasks/user/day
× agents/task
× model steps/agent
× tokens/step

This is also where the feedback was most dispersed. Some people think 50+ model steps for a meaningful agent task is completely reasonable; others think an assumption of 50 consumer-initiated events per day is far too high. Those aren’t necessarily contradictory - tasks/day and model steps/task are different assumptions.

---
How this compares with sell-side CPU math

The sell-side approach is generally much more top-down.
Using BofA as one example - they estimate total data-center systems TAM growing from roughly $506B in 2025 to $2.56T in 2030, while assuming CPUs remain around 7–8% of total system value. That gets them to roughly $211B of server CPU TAM in 2030.

Their CPU bull case is essentially:

AI infrastructure spending gets much larger
× AI becomes more CPU-intensive relative to GPUs
× agents create a new standalone CPU compute layer
× AI CPUs get more expensive / higher-spec

BofA splits the 2030 number into roughly $90B of GPU-attached/head-node CPUs, $90B of standalone agentic CPUs, and ~$30B of traditional server CPUs.

++
Better formatted version: https://t.co/qVwYKNr1ZA

++
Thank you again to everyone who challenged the assumptions and shared thoughtful feedback - I learned a lot from it!
author: FredaDuan
quoted_text:
A humble attempt to est. the infra required to serve 100M DAU @Muse 

Rough conclusion is:

1 GW of power to serve 100M DAU in the base case, of which only ~0.1 GW comes from the CPU/VM layer. Depending on the # of reasoning-equivalent model calls one Muse DAU generates per day, 3-4GW is entirely plausible. Maybe that’s why @Meta  is rumored to be adding 7-10GW of compute next year.

The sandbox layer = sub $1B of CPU content and ~$2B of DRAM content, which is much smaller than many expected.

Lot of moving assumptions. Welcome all feedbacks/ pushbacks.

------
Two very different pieces of infrastructure behind Muse.

1. Muse VM / sandbox infrastructure

2 vCPUs, ~8 GB of RAM and ~100 GB of persistent logical storage per user. https://t.co/7rP5vDKnT7

2. Muse Spark inference

Model inference goes out through Meta's external inference infrastructure. https://t.co/e203XUp6jq
------

1/ Sandbox infrastructure

A. CPU
The first mistake is assuming that 100M DAU means 100M VMs are actively consuming compute at the same time.

Suppose the average Muse DAU has an agent actively working for two hours per day.

100M users * 2 hours / 24 hours = ~8M average simultaneous active VMs

Meta obviously cannot provision only for the daily average. Usage will be concentrated during waking hours and bursty.

Assume a 2.5x peak-to-average ratio:

8M * 2.5 = ~20M peak active VMs

Then add roughly 20% capacity headroom: ~25M provisioned live VMs. So the base assumption is effectively that Meta needs enough infrastructure to support roughly 25% of DAU being live simultaneously.

The next important distinction is between virtual CPU allocation and physical CPU demand. Agent sandboxes are particularly well suited to CPU oversubscription. They spend a lot of time waiting. During those periods, the VM may still be alive, but it is barely using CPU.

DeepSeek’s recently published DSec infrastructure provides a useful benchmark. Its production agent sandbox platform runs approximately 30,000 physical CPU cores and 250TB of DRAM across ~160 nodes, with peak concurrency above 380,000 sandboxes. https://t.co/PFlgc6nnUs DSec also demonstrates stable operation at around: 800 microVMs per node. With roughly 188 physical cores per node: 188 physical cores / 800 microVMs = ~0.23 physical cores per live VM.

DeepSeek is obviously the King of efficiency. The number for Muse might be at 0.3-0.75 physical cores per live VM, or assume 0.5 physical cores per live VM as the base case. That is equivalent to roughly two simultaneously live Muse VMs per physical CPU core.

Using the base assumptions: 25M live VMs * 0.5 physical cores per VM = 12.5M physical CPU cores.

On a 256-core CPU: 12.5M cores / 256 cores per CPU = ~50K CPUs; Or on a 192-core CPU that would be 65K CPUs.

At the current public pricing, that is ~$800M.

B. DRAM
CPU can be aggressively oversubscribed because a VM that is waiting may consume almost no CPU. Memory is harder to oversubscribe because a live VM still needs to retain its working state.

Muse exposes roughly 8GB of RAM to the user environment, but one observed instance was actually using only around 3GB at the time of measurement.

25M live VMs * 3GB = 75PB of physical DRAM, call it ~75-100PB of physical DRAM feels like a reasonable base range.

At the current public pricing, that is ~$2B.

C. Sandbox power
~0.1 GW for the entire Muse sandbox / VM layer at 100M DAU.

------

2/ Inference
Muse’s personal computer executes tools and stores state locally, but the actual model runs on separate inference infrastructure. Meta’s Muse architecture

Energy per inference event
Microsoft’s 2026 study estimates that optimized frontier-scale inference consumes a median of approximately: 0.31Wh per normal query

But a long reasoning query with roughly 15x the token count consumes approximately 13x as much energy, or around: 4Wh per long reasoning query

The study specifically highlights reasoning and agentic workloads as significantly more energy intensive.
https://t.co/z1YEsvVeMo

Sensitivity analysis on # reasoning-equivalent events per DAU per day

Suppose each active @Muse user generates the equivalent of 50 heavy inference events per day.

At 5Wh each:

100M users * 50 events/day * 5Wh = 25GWh/day

25GWh/day / 24 hours = ~1.0GW average power

So inference alone could require: ~1-2GW of average power

A 3-4GW Muse is entirely plausible. Maybe that’s why @Meta  is rumored to be adding 7-10GW of compute next year.

------
The popular framing around Muse is that giving every user 2 vCPUs and 8GB of RAM creates an enormous CPU requirement. But the naive calculation materially exaggerates the CPU requirement because it treats logical VM allocation as dedicated physical infrastructure.

The more interesting conclusion is: Consumer agents may be a meaningful new demand driver for CPUs and conventional DRAM, but inference remains the real compute bottleneck. And as agents do more work, run longer trajectories and increasingly spawn other agents, inference demand can scale much faster than the number of users itself.
