text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

text:
Ethereum Is Killing the L2 Boom by Fixing Itself

Blast, Abstract, Polygon zkEVM, Loopring, Zero, Mint, Swellchain, Sophon and others are shutting down or winding down in 2026.

The common problem?

The economics no longer work.

As Ethereum becomes cheaper, faster and more scalable, many standalone L2s lose the main reason they existed: providing cheaper blockspace and reducing Ethereum’s limitations.

This is the part the market is missing.

Ethereum is fixing the weaknesses that created the L2 boom in the first place.

Cheaper data availability reduces L2 operating costs, while better throughput and infrastructure make it less necessary for every app, wallet, NFT ecosystem or payment product to launch its own chain.

So L2 shutdowns don't necessarily mean Ethereum is losing.

They can mean the opposite:
Ethereum is becoming strong enough that fewer L2s are needed to support it.

The next phase may not be a world of hundreds of Ethereum L2s.

It may be a smaller number of dominant networks, with Ethereum itself becoming increasingly capable of handling more of the activity.

text:
Sadly, I wasn't able to attend Sui Basecamp this year, but I managed to watch the livestream.

Here's a TL;DR of the biggest announcements ↓

1. Google Cloud + Sui

Mysten Labs and @googlecloud are building VAA, which lets companies verify what an AI agent did without exposing the private data underneath. Agents can act, and businesses still get a record they can audit later.

2. Alibaba Cloud + Sui Agent Payments

Agents will be able to use @alibaba_cloud services and pay for them automatically through Sui Agent Payments. No manual approvals needed.

3. New record TPS

Sui hit ~41M TPS in a live Basecamp test. A controlled test isn't the same as normal mainnet activity, but it shows how far they're pushing execution.

4. Sui Threat Intelligence

A new security system that detects suspicious activity, scores transactions, and helps contain threats in real time.

The first two are about giving agents more autonomy. The other two strengthen the infrastructure those agents will depend on.

Disclosure: I'm a $SUI holder.

author: apruden08
quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

We are sorry.

We know how much privacy matters to you, and how careful many of you are about who you share personal information with. You trusted us with yours. We should have held ourselves to a higher standard in protecting it. We understand and we are deeply sorry.

On 5 October 2026, a security alert led us to discover the incident, and we contained the attack immediately. By then, some user data had already been accessed by the attacker. We fixed the vulnerability and tightened our access controls.

The attacker tried to reach deposited funds but was unable to. Funds on the Based Visa Card remain safe and cards remain operational. Funds in the Based App wallet and Trading Terminal are also safe and were not affected.

After the attack, we reviewed our other systems and found no sign that they were compromised.

As soon as we made sure that all systems were thoroughly audited and extra security precautions were put in place, then we proceeded to disclose this incident to affected users. Cardholders who are affected have the right to know.

If you were affected, please be extra careful. Sophisticated actors may use this information to try to trick you. 

For account queries, use the in-app support chat. It is the most secure way to reach us, and it lets us verify that you own the account. No one from the Based team will contact you on X or Telegram about your account.

We are committed to strengthening the security of our systems.

Once again, we are very sorry.

quoted_text:
Based Visa Card: Security Incident Update

On 5 October 2026, we were alerted that an unauthorised party has gained access to an internal dashboard used to manage the Based Visa Card program. The attack was swiftly stopped and contained as soon as it was discovered.

KYC data collected by our card issuer for some cardholders, including name, ID or passport number, date of birth and address, may have been obtained by the attacker.

What was NOT affected:
- Card numbers, CVV and PIN
- Photographs of IDs and liveness check images
- Based Wallet, which was used for trading
- Funds on the Based Visa Card. Your funds are safe and Visa cards continue to work as normal.

Affected cardholders have been notified by email today, and relevant authorities have been informed.

What can you do next?

If you are one of the affected users, assume that the data is compromised. Be careful of impersonation attempts from anyone who possesses that information. Sophisticated attackers may use this information to perform social engineering attacks.

Also, support for Based Visa Card is only done on the in-app support chat, and no team members will DM you on Telegram or X for account servicing purposes. For security reasons, comments on this tweet is disabled on purpose.

We are sorry about this incident, and we are working closely with our card service provider to tighten access controls and enhance monitoring.

We are publishing an update to OpenAI problem #109 (integer multiplication) with further tightening. 

κ = 2⁻³⁴  (tightened from κ = 2⁻¹⁸²)

The exact witness is 8.3 × 10⁻¹¹, a roughly 48 million fold improvement over the previous result and a 2¹⁴⁸ fold improvement over original OAI result.

The improvement came from removing the spacing penalty behind the quadratic bottleneck. This was done by moving compact control bits instead of entire windows.

κ = 2⁻⁵⁹   (from OpenAI’s original κ = 2⁻¹⁸²)

Approximately 500 thousand fold improvement over our previous result and a 2¹²³ fold improvement over the original OAI result.

The latest redesigned the finite network to share intermediate computations and scratch space, then tightened the recursion and Gaussian estimates.

text:
一个去中心化的音乐平台终于上线了
声刻 SonicMint，作品刻进链上的唱片容器，听众买一次永久能听，钱当场按比例分给每个创作者

看到它，我想到了我关注的一位艺人陆虎，早年写的很多歌，版权并不在自己手里
邓紫棋也一样，14岁签约，六年没拿到版税，最后只能把整张专辑重录一遍
问题都是源于作品一出生，就先归了公司

声刻的意义，我觉得有五层

第一，作品从第一天起就在创作者名下
写好的歌，艺人自己刻进自己的唱片容器
在谁名下、什么时候刻上去的，链上清清楚楚，不用再靠一纸合同去证明

第二，钱怎么分，创作者自己定
一首歌背后有词作、曲作、编曲、制作人，以前大家各拿多少，是公司说了算
现在每个人的比例写进合约，听众一付钱，当场分好，合约里不留一分余额
平台只收3%，规则写死，所有人都看得见

第三，每一笔都能查
以前艺人拿多少、什么时候拿、拿没拿到，全看公司的账本
现在每一笔收入都在链上，自己随时能查
六年收不到版税这种事，在这里一眼就能看出来

第四，没人能把你的作品拿走
传统平台说下架就下架，账号说封就封
作品一旦刻上链，就永久留在那里，不依赖任何一家平台活着

第五，中间人从必须变成可选
经纪公司和唱片公司收钱，不全是白收，他们出钱做制作、做宣发、帮你被更多人听到
链上不是把这些人全部赶走，而是让你有得选
你可以自己做，也可以找人帮你推，但分多少，公开写在合约里，不再是一份只有一方看得懂的合同

当然
链上改变不了合同法，签出去的版权，法律上照样有效
链上也分不出上传的人是不是真正的作者，身份和版权的认定，还是要靠线下
付费解锁的钥匙，现在也还要靠平台发放，不是百分之百没有中心
它做不到让每个艺人都不被坑，但它把默认值换了过来
以前是作品先归公司，现在是作品先归自己

再往外想，同样的逻辑能用在很多地方
只要是创作者卖作品、多人分收益、怕平台下架的事，都能这样做
作家的书和专栏，读者买断，出版方不再拿大头
老师的课程，永久可看，不怕平台跑路
摄影和设计素材，授权范围写进合约
播客、有声书、游戏美术，参与的人按比例自动分钱

text:
This paper flips the “AI will replace software engineers” debate on its head.

Field studies (4,867 devs, +26% task completion; but -19% productivity for experienced devs) show that coding agents like Copilot only boost throughput for simple tasks. For anything complex, time saved in coding is lost to supervision and rework.

Why? LLMs have hard limits: they generate plausible code but can’t judge sufficiency, lack organizational context, and forget as soon as the session ends. No amount of pre-training fills that “structural vacuum.”

The fix: four explicit artifacts—methodological, domain, design, and process knowledge—must be baked into the workflow. AI agents execute, but software engineers become methodologists, mediators, and custodians of these artifacts. Get the SE structure right, and AI delivers; skip it, and you risk unverifiable, unmaintainable code.

This isn’t about AI replacing engineers—it’s about engineers and SE discipline becoming more essential than ever.

Hare is being built to assess those risks and make them legible to investors and issuers. https://t.co/DDHMZDKVUs
author: turtledotxyz
quoted_text:
A lot of the conversation about bringing real-world assets onchain focuses on the assets themselves.

I think the harder question is how we underwrite the risks behind them.

As more assets come onchain, the market needs people who can assess those risks, explain them clearly and help investors understand what they’re actually taking on. That’s why we’re building Hare.

DeFi has developed strong ways to assess smart-contract and oracle risk. But many real-world assets also depend on offchain credit and counterparties. To understand the risk, you have to look beyond the onchain structure: Where is the capital being deployed? What is the underlying credit? Who are the counterparties? How could problems move through the system?

A strong rating or familiar name doesn’t answer those questions.

You also have to ask what happens when everyone wants liquidity at once. How much can be returned immediately? What takes longer? Have those scenarios been stress-tested and explained clearly to investors?

Calling anything riskless would be a lie. The job is to understand the risks, model how they behave under stress and be honest about the results.

We’re launching with dollar- and gold-denominated earn products. Gold is an interesting place to start because people already understand it as a store of value. Bringing it onchain creates the opportunity to build new utility around a familiar asset.

Longer term, I want onchain markets to become a serious venue for capital formation in their own right. That will take more than putting assets onchain. It will take underwriting people can understand and trust.

I spoke with GSR about why we’re building Hare and what we’re working toward: https://t.co/yN3sz1hYcY

text:
昨天，美国拿出 390 亿美元的十年期国债拍卖，收到约 1080 亿美元的投标，投标倍数达到 2.77 倍，是 2016 年以来的高位。相当于美国想借 100 美元，市场提交了 277 美元的购买申请。

买家不仅申请得多，出的价格也不错。拍卖前，这批国债的收益率约为 5.317%，最后以 5.30% 成交。买家愿意少拿一点收益，也要买到这批国债，说明这次需求确实比较强。

最后，直接下单和通过中介下单的投资者，合计买走了约 97.5%，一级交易商只拿到约 2.5%。这批国债大部分都有投资者愿意接手。

收益率涨上去，也会把买家吸引过来。像养老金、保险公司这类需要把钱安排很多年的机构，会考虑买入国债，用之后收到的利息和到期拿回的本金，支付未来的开支。同样是买国债，现在能拿到更高的回报，自然更容易让它们动心。

美国政府这边，钱确实借到了，但要付的利息也更高。这次拍卖说明，给到 5.30% 左右的收益率，市场还是很愿意买单。以后旧债陆续到期，如果还要按较高的利率重新借钱，政府花在利息上的钱就会越来越多。

接下来就看，利息少给一点，大家还买不买。如果收益率降下来，买家仍然很多，美债价格就更容易稳住。如果必须不断提高收益率才能吸引资金，那美国虽然借得到钱，借钱也会越来越贵。

一个 @Gate ，交易更多市场
author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
十年期美债收益率盘中一度突破了5.3%，最高到5.306%，随后仍在5.3%附近。从PCE公布后约5.20%的低点算起，已经反弹了超过10个基点，通胀数据带来的缓解没有维持住。

这次核心PCE环比增长0.2%，低于预期的0.3%，确实是好消息。但同一份报告里，个人消费支出增长了0.9%，即便扣掉涨价的影响，实际消费仍增长了0.6%，说明美国人的消费需求还很强。

也就是说，通胀比市场担心的温和一些，但需求并没有明显冷下来。再加上能源价格的压力仍在，仅凭这一次PCE，还不足以让市场相信美联储很快就能结束加息，或者让利率降下来。

这轮收益率反弹，更像是市场重新考虑高利率还要维持多久。投资者如果担心未来利率更高、通胀迟迟压不下来，就会要求更高的回报才愿意买债，债券价格因此被抛售，收益率往上走。

目前十月加息的市场概率已经降到了 37% 左右，说明十年期突破5.3%，并不意味着十月一定会加息。长债还在反映未来几年的利率和持有期间的风险。说人话，就是市场越来越相信美联储会维持高利率的时间更长，甚至接下来加息的概率上升。

而对市场来说，如果十年期收益率持续处于这样的高位，即便美联储十月暂时不加息，企业融资和居民房贷的成本也很难明显降下来。借钱成本仍然很高，股票估值也会继续承受压力。尤其是九月通胀数据如果继续走高，那么对于市场的压力会更大。

text:
Without prior experience auditing manually, I don’t think AI auditing can be done properly.

In my final Quantus sweep, five of six parallel agents returned reasoned negatives.

The sixth produced passing PoCs, but they only rediscovered an existing finding.

None of those outputs could be accepted at face value.

I strongly question every finding the agents return. But I also question them when they return nothing.

A reasoned negative can help me decide where not to spend more resources. It does not mean an area has been completely checked, and it definitely does not mean the audit is done.

This is what makes leading AI audit agents difficult.

You need to stop them from inventing vulnerabilities to satisfy the prompt, while also stopping them from declaring completion because they exhausted one path.

I don’t see this as replacing one auditor with six agents.

It is about navigating and leading the resources LLMs give you: challenging findings, questioning negative results, noticing missing coverage and deciding where each agent should search next.

The agents can explore and test much more than I can alone. But my previous manual auditing experience is what lets me judge whether their work actually means anything.

author: jedifractal
quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
@templedao is voting to build fixed-price auctions for Spice Bazaar, its marketplace for trading directly with the Temple treasury, at a rate the treasury cannot change once posted.

In past auctions the price rose with every bid, bids couldn't be withdrawn and the amount for sale was fixed at the start. The proposal says locked bids "increased price risk for early Bidders and served to discourage bidding until large bids had come in," while the treasury couldn't enlarge an auction "even if the market demand was high."

Under the new format, bidders could add or withdraw deposits during a window of typically 3-7 days, since a bid no longer moves the price. Deposits then lock, and the treasury accepts all, part or none of them, refunding the rest.

"The Treasury can only choose how much of the order it wants to fill," the proposal says. Bidders get a known price but no guarantee of a trade.

The vote authorizes development only, with no budget or auction size set.

4 wallets have cast 5,060,223 $stTEMPLE so far: 100.0% For. No quorum is set.

Voting closes October 8th at 8:21pm UTC.

text:
神了，一名广东大学生居然靠AI把韩国好几家大银行都给黑了......

最近韩国的大新闻就是好几家大银行都被黑了，数万人的个人信息遭到泄露，甚至连韩国总统李在明都亲自要求彻查。

结果10月7号 CrowdStrike 公布的一份调查报告，居然发现幕后黑客可能是一个只有 26 岁的中国年轻人。

而且这哥们更是重量级，攻击了这么多金融机构，最后居然因为自己的 Claude Code 聊天记录，把身份线索都暴露了。

事情是这样的。

9 月底到 10 月初，韩国多家金融机构接连遭到网络攻击。CrowdStrike 在调查中发现，攻击者使用了中国开发的开源 AI 渗透测试工具 ARTEX，主要接入 DeepSeek V4.1-Flash，同时还使用了 GLM-5.3、Grok 4.6 和 Claude Code 辅助操作。

他还搭建了两套服务器，一套在香港负责控制，另一套运行 ARTEX。

结果这哥们干了一件特别抽象的事。

他居然在自己的服务器上开放了目录列表功能。

安全研究人员几乎没费什么力气，就找到了他的 CLAUDE.md 文件、Claude Code 历史会话、ARTEX 配置文件，甚至连 Claude 的记忆文件都被翻出来了。

相当于一个黑客把自己干活的全部过程，直接放到了公网上。

然后研究人员越看越离谱。

这哥们居然还问过 Claude，韩国泄露的数据通常在哪里卖？有没有专门交易这些数据的 Telegram 群组？

最逆天的是，他还让 Claude 帮自己写过一份网络安全研究员的简历。

在这段对话里，他提供了自己的年龄、姓名、电话号码、Telegram 账号、教育背景和所在地。

按照这些信息，他今年 26 岁，有华南理工大学的教育背景，住在广东茂名。

我看到这里真的没绷住。

一个人已经能熟练使用多个大模型、Agent 和各种网络攻击工具，对韩国金融机构实施攻击，甚至还知道用代理服务器隐藏自己的网络活动。

结果连自己服务器最基础的目录访问权限都没配置好。

最后，CrowdStrike 几乎是顺着他自己留下的 Claude Code Session，把整个攻击过程都还原出来了。

 AI 能力再强，也架不住人类自己留下这么离谱的安全漏洞。

更抽象的是，这哥们甚至还准备让 Claude 帮自己找一份网络安全研究员的工作😅。。。

好吧，这下建议招安了

author: mikebelshe
quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

Crypto is reaching a similar point. The engineering still matters, but faster alone is no longer enough to make people care. They need something worth using.

text:
存储的反身性，可能正在扼杀自己的股价🧐

每天都在看存储新闻，涨价和短缺一直是关键词，但这么好的基本面，并没有带来股价的上涨趋势。

所以觉得在 10年美债收益率走高，折现率压制市值之外，还有一个原因是，存储本身的反身性。

——————

“反身性”这个词来自索罗斯。

简单说，就是市场参与者的预期会改变现实，而改变后的现实，又会反过来强化，或者打破原来的预期。

放在存储上，就是：市场为了摆脱周期，开始追求确定性。可确定性越高，股价能交易的想象空间，反而越小。

——————

过去的存储，是最典型的周期行业。

芯片涨价，厂商扩产——产能上来，供给增加——价格又开始下跌。

然后打价格战、亏损、减产，直到市场出清，再进入下一轮周期。

这也是为什么，存储看起来进入门槛没有那么高，最后却形成了寡头垄断。

因为大量竞争者，早就在一轮又一轮周期里被淘汰了。

而周期性最大的问题，就是华尔街不愿意给高估值。

盈利越接近周期高点，市场越担心下一轮下行。

——————

所以这些年，存储厂商一直想改变这件事。

你能看到，美光 CEO 在财报电话会、投资者日等各种公开场合，不断强调 HBM 的长期需求。

背后的核心，其实就是希望降低市场对存储周期性的担忧。

——————

具体怎么做？

签长期协议，锁定采购量，锁定产能，甚至加入最低采购义务，把未来几年的收入变得更可见。

对公司来说，这当然是好事。但反身性，也恰恰从这里开始。

当未来一两年的产能已经被客户锁定，意味着未来的出货量，乃至大部分盈利，也越来越容易被算出来。

那么股价下一步想继续超预期，主要只剩两个来源：

继续涨价，或者出现分析师模型里还没有看到的新需求。

问题是，这两个空间其实都在变窄。

——————

新的需求必须足够大，才能在已经很高的基数上继续推动增长。

而涨价本身，也有极限。

存储价格越高，在服务器和数据中心 BOM 里的成本占比就越高，客户控制成本的动力也会越强。

能少配一点内存，就少配一点；

能延后采购，就延后采购；

能通过模型、架构和内存效率优化掉一部分需求，就会去优化。

AI 服务器对高端存储的需求，确实比消费电子刚性得多。但再刚性的需求，也有价格弹性。

更重要的是，高价格、高利润，本身也会刺激厂商扩产、技术升级，以及更多资本开支。

也就是说，涨价一边在创造这一轮的利润，一边也在孕育下一轮的供给增长和需求优化。

现在，厂商想用长期协议和收入确定性摆脱周期，却又让未来几年的盈利越来越容易被计算。

确定性解决了周期股的问题，也压缩了成长股最值钱的东西：预期差。

————

所以接下来对存储，我可能更多会把存储当成波段机会。

相比之下，把更多注意力放到推理端，包括 ASIC、CPU，以及随着推理规模扩大之后，绕不开的能源和电力，去寻找那些市场还没有充分定价的机会。

text:
从OKCoin到OKX，股东名单换了三拨人，控股的老大还是徐总

这轮Circle入股被聊成了「币安间接持股 OKX」。币安9月花1亿美元买了 Circle不到1%的股权；而Circle在OKX占多少没公布，所以这个梗听听就好

很多人更关心OKX背后到底站着哪些人。把公开披露翻了一遍，大致是三拨：

一、2013年，天使和A轮

·天使：Tim Draper和创业工场（麦刚），100万美元
· A 轮：约1000万美元，策源创投（冯波）领投，曼图资本、创业工场跟投，蔡文胜、黄劲、蒋涛等个人跟投

二、2015到2019年，OKCoin母公司 OKC Holdings

2019年OKC收购港股前进控股（就是后来的欧科云链）时，港交所公告披露了它的股东表：

· 徐明星合计约52.68%
· 史静（Kalyana Global）13%
· 策源9.86%，唐越7.89%，麦刚 5.08%，卓媛5.08%
· 王亚伟的千合系等2%，蔡文胜 1.82%

三、2026年，华尔街和Circle

· 3月：纽交所母公司ICE入场，估值250亿美元，投了约2亿美元，ICE拿到一个董事席位

· 10月：Circle、Ripple、渣打旗下 SC Ventures、量化基金QRT，同样是250亿美元投前估值，金额没披露

10月这轮更像商业结盟，钱倒在其次。四家投资方本来就是OKX的合作方：
USDC 的发行方、RLUSD的发行方、BUIDL的托管行、给OKX供流动性的量化机构

徐明星自己也说，不是因为缺钱才融的。估值7个月没动，换来的是股东名单上多了一排欧美金融机构。

你觉得OKX三年内会在美国上市吗？

Meta、OpenAI 和 Anthropic 这些今天看似在搞软件的大模型巨头，终局全都会变成生物技术公司。

很多人只把他们当程序员看，
但 Anthropic 创始人 Dario 本身就是神经科学博士出身，
Altman 和扎克伯格在神经生物学上的理解深度同样极深，
这群过去造编译器、写代码的工程师，正在集体把研究重心转向人类大脑。

他们私下里心照不宣的终极目标只有一个：
非侵入性地从人类大脑里直接读取和写入信息。

今天我们在键盘上打提示词、在屏幕上看几十行字，本质上是一种传输带宽极低、极其原始的机械过渡态。
休伯曼举了个极具操作感的具体场景：
人在做艰苦学习、攻克复杂代码时，最大的阻力往往不是智力不够，而是注意力涣散、驱动力不足。
未来的非侵入式设备，不需要开颅做手术，
可以直接通过外设刺激大脑里的伏隔核以及相关的多巴胺回路，
在你要干重活的这三个小时里，把你的动机水平和专注度直接拉满；
任务结束一键关闭，让你迅速恢复能量进入深度休息。

这就是为什么顶级 AI 巨头都在暗中布局神经科学。
大模型如果只停留在云端聊天框里，永远只是人类身外的一件工具；
把算法的算力，直接对接到碳基大脑的神经回路上，才是这场军备竞赛真正的终点线。

如果未来有一款不需要开颅的头戴设备，按一下就能让你保持三小时的顶级专注力，干完活一键关闭，你会愿意天天用它吗？ https://t.co/X8O9F60wkn

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

author: youyou5202
quoted_text:
bem是让“计算逻辑 的资产化”。这句话已背诵。
。任何计算逻辑、代码程序本身就是一个可以交易的数字资产。

比如pumpfun发明了发射曲线，这其实是一个“计算逻辑和数学函数”，然后这一个计算逻辑就做成了一个单品。

但是bem打造的是“计算逻辑资产”的发射台，也就是你做的“链上应用”平台，可以有很多人使用，但是这个“计算逻辑”的发射台，可以发射很多应用和创意。

发射出来在tapeout上为你提供几个“孵化服务”呢？

第一·给你deweb，不容易被封，永久储存。你直接deweb写明一个版权声明，我是26年10月8号敲定，我发明的这个“电路成品”。后续的人模仿，后来者也会向大小写“Neiro”一样自发去找之前最早的那个创意来源，降低“分流”对模仿电路的估值溢价，赋予“原创电路”时间最先永远的“溢价”。这其实可以和现实版权一起注册，双重保护。版权第三方保护不了的，市场散户自发定价保护，而是市场自发把价值从账面上表现出来。

第二·给你直接“资产化”，跳过版权，你直接可以把你的“电路资产”本身，以市场卖出的价格来取代估值中间环节。市场可以直接报价，作者可以选择最好的价格卖出。

第三· “这种资产化的链上电路”还会在未来数年后影响到一个事实：股权可以被拆分为发明权和发行权。

大部分用户拥有复制后的使用权——这交付了发行权（而盗版会在这里分流），而当时灵感创意的第一个“原创电路模型”却具有收藏权，溢价储存权——这交付了发明权（时间性唯一确定“高昂溢价”）

当发行权属于A，发明权属于B，但是虽然持有个体不属于同一个“公司”，即使A和B完全分裂也不影响，发行权和发明权两个“股票资产”的一荣俱荣，一损俱损。

当现金流很好，发行权持有人A获得更多的收益，而金融市场对“初始链上电路原创成本”的金融溢价也会上涨。

譬如photshop公司现在的价值是股价拥有权和发行给用户的使用权（正版复制软件）是一体的，但是第三方链上世界是这样的，真正的创造者譬如“爱迪生”发明了“灯泡”，未来即使再多的人发行“复制版灯泡”，但是史上第一个“灯泡”在链上它不会被氧化消失，它依然存在。所以未来创始的第一个“灯泡灵感”著作权永远在链上，具有最高的价格。而“复制品”都只是廉价的使用卖出价格。

这就使得公司把拥有权拆给了“作者”，把稳定业务拆给了“用户”的现金流。而无论未来行业复制多少次，作者不再靠第三方版权来获得权益，而是直接拥有“原创的链上电路”来直接获得收藏估值溢价，当然如果作者直接发行的是“原创的链上晶体管”基础模型，它的现金流会更加庞大，那可能仍然是“公司”性质的，既具有产权又具有源源不断地现金流权益。

第四，新的电路资产形式，会成为很多代码创作者有一个创造平台的选择。而且“代码就是资产”，在这里强化了程序员创作者的收益、版权。（当然未来盗版可能性依然会在tapeout链上平台内竞争）

以前是没有这样的通用规范的，相当于bem打造的就是新一套的规范，就像是各个发射台发币一样，tapeout发射台发射的是“程序员编程好的逻辑代码”，一键发射为“数字资产”，可以自由被人们交易。

其实这里的发币，就不只是文化模因和公司链上股权了。而是程序员，“创作即是财富”。不去申请版权，直接把自己的代码成品，创造作为一个“可以交易的代币形式”，一键发射，在市场上也可以自由流通、炒作，定价。这相当于，现在币圈炒的火热的资产，不仅仅是meme、nft，还有新的“计算逻辑资产化”的“链上电路”。

第五——我认为tapeout接下来一定会诞生、且必经之路：

任何“链上电路”的成品，它不仅可以是个体交易，导致创始人的原创作品被“一次性定价”交易掉。

它一定需要tapeout未来的开发者，开发一个“股权管理公司”，这是金融导向的，为旗下每一个支持的程序员，获得更高的“金融收益溢价权”。@Blonskr @BruceBlue @martin23_sen 

譬如现在有个：“链上支付宝”的网站，
它的所有权确实在一个“链上容器”中储存，而这个“链上容器”可以通过这个“股权管理平台”把所有权质押并分为10亿份，然后准许市场散户认购个股，形成了“一个链上支付宝”应用本身，就形成了一个股权市场。

允许市场的投资者，自由买入，持有。那么“链上电路”本身也不仅仅是一个创作者一次性卖出的权利，可以变成缓释权，可以慢慢稀释抛售小比例股份，逐渐让创作者吃到自己产品的完整生命周期的收益。

这是okx欧易暂时没有开辟的，“链上应用”资产也可以开出一个新的交易所，一个和币圈内的meme炒作不一样的，对外公开的“github+资产直接定价流通”的平台，

个人猜测其价格在百亿~千亿美金。那将直接让okx的参与从我们需要它，变成它需要我们。

而且这里激活了一群币圈从未没有的玩家的积极性：大部分推特上会写代码的程序员，都具有写一段代码在tapeout平台发射为“链上应用成品”，并立刻转化为财富的能力。既可以是自己的概念性产品直接发射在tapeout，获得“版权溢价”，又可以在市场反响很好，直接发行“官方正版、复制版”的应用，直接向用户收取现金流。

再往后想，一个tapeout的“apple store”，历史上第一个“Dewb store”就此打开。甚至未来很多ai代理或者个体的手机客户端，都愿意直接去“tapeout Dewbstore”下载各种传统世界，没有的链上应用。解决了隐私问题、中心化窥探的问题。更加守卫了web2世界传统用户渴求的隐私权。（先刺激b端程序员，给予很大的创作金钱激励，代码发行即是可交易资产、股权。不仅仅是今天的生产权，还要激励b端程序员的积极性。）

结尾：

之前看bem币价到200u顶天了，跨链之后，okx+bsc两条链之后，估值上限又打破了。但是如果又以最新的——
todd提出的，我觉得最契合题意的概念是：

“计算逻辑的资产化”、“计算逻辑的资产可编程化”，
完全不一样了。这是媲美“虚拟空间”、“虚拟物质”的又一种崭新的“数字资产”，“链上电路”，而tapeout开创了这条品类的第一个代币。

个人认为，先不说tapeout的区块时钟的限制，因为未来的仿品竞品自然可以像solana、eth一样丝滑，但是tapeout开创的“计算逻辑资产化”的“数字黄金”不需要实用性，因为未来真的其他竞品很实用，但是市场炒作公认的网，最贵的晶体管，还是tapeout。

所以，tapeout负责承载“链上电路资产化”整个未来市值的33%~50%的价值存储。

投资的是一个“新资产”的“储水的格子”，它是空的，等待传统世界的跳入，和市场再次选择这种“金融新资产标的”的格式。

我觉得okx未来一定和tapeout沟通，会开辟“链上应用”的资产交易股权平台。一种新的公司股权形式，直接以“链上电路”的应用，用应用发行股权，而非公司发行股权。这种“新资产发行”格式，缔造的数百亿美金的“代码即是金钱、代码即是权力”的去中心化主义的趋势延申，一定会从金融、到掌握代码的创作者、到使用“链上电路成品资产”的Deweb用户，这条趋势路上，一定会先后出现的。@zakk_okx    @star_okx

text:
wrt justin's fable (fable because claude) I think it's useful to warn people to take best measures against unknown unknowns. RN that is basically whether AI is, or will soon (months) be able to crack crypto keys. Because getting better at math than we are. So "can just do things". (I know this is simplistic, but well, not like anyone knows...)

Be that as it may. It is also useful to consider human behavior. Most crypto participants are not here for a long time. Certain whales and CEX treasuries are. But the vast majority are trading or doing grey market or remittances. And would just switch to another solution even centralized if regulations changed.

In the "fallout" scenario, where certain smart people 'bunker down' in the interim and survive and everyone else gets rekt. It does not seem to me anyone returns to crypto. They will not be imo, impressed or relieved to see such caution on display as something to imitate, now wizened by the carnage ("well crypto can work if you just keep ahead of the curve...").

The bunker dwellers might squint and see, well, not much to return to ('I have my ETH.... but no buyers'). This is not to layer on the doom, though. In fact the opposite.

The game here says to me, we will not reasonably expect most people in crypto to secure themselves. Many are correct that the mere suggestion to migrate under the threat of 'lose it all' will now inevitably lead to phishing and mistakes that could amount to same fallout.

When speaking from a position of authority, you are not simply relaying information. You are setting up epochs and pushing dominoes.

In this epoch, I think we must strive to solve crypto and cyber threats at the root layer: consensus. There will undoubtedly be clever maths and so on. But my gut is that we are playing with fire against a fire bender, in terms of AI. What can humans do? They can govern. The resolution against fallout scenarios is not going to be by the preppers, but by the enclaves. Don't trust people to protect themselves if you want to help them. The DAO hardfork might not have been the biggest blemish on Ethereum. But a dress rehearsal for something that will keep us on our toes: the unknown unknown of securing our property rights and networks against alien powers. 

Social recovery, at network level, can be communicated in a way right now to help people not panic and see around the corner (if the machines break all the things, it won't matter). I wish I could honestly give a smarter prescription here, but any "smart" thing will just get outfoxed. So it is more going to be about legitimacy. I do not think super intelligence automatically gives something legitimacy. If for example, I am chilling in front of a chessboard and someone uninvited sits down, and absolutely mops the floor with me, and then I replace my pieces and then say "chessmate" - who won that round? Me I would say.

Anyways a lot of text to say, don't panic. Let's think about what else blockchains and crypto are. The bearer instrument aspect does require strict control. But these instruments are subject to networks. We can figure this out, while not needing to be the smartest in the room.

author: cz_binance
quoted_text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

在币圈，我们经常需要用 𝕏 的信息来投研

但是 Codex/Claude Code 一般没办法直接访问 𝕏 上面的信息，有几个解决方案，第一就是可以花钱买 𝕏 的 API，或者通过任何第三方 API，但是 𝕏 的 API 不便宜，配置起来也比较麻烦。

第二是直接用 Grok，但是 Grok 肯定没有 Codex/Claude Code 来得智能和全面，大家目前的主力 Agent 基本都还是 Codex/Claude Code。

这个过程对于我来说不需要额外付费。

因为我本来就有订阅 𝕏 的 Premium+ 会员，所以我是可以免费使用 Grok Build 这个功能的，这点很多人都不知道，白白浪费了 𝕏 送给你的 Grok Build 免费额度。

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
中国央行发文阐明人民币汇率的政策立场
中国实施以市场供求为基础、参考一篮子货币进行调节、有管理的浮动汇率制度，坚持让市场在汇率形成中发挥决定性作用。
过去二十多年，人民币汇率双向浮动；2010年以来，人民币汇率经历了多轮升贬值周期，双向浮动特征更加明显，弹性增强。
中国贸易发展根源于产业国际竞争力的提升，中国没有必要，也无意通过汇率贬值获取贸易竞争优势，从不搞竞争性货币贬值。
汇率受经济增长、货币政策、金融市场、地缘政治、突发风险事件等多种因素影响，与经常账户不存在简单线性关系。
国际上有关汇率均衡水平的评估方法尚不成熟，将个别评估结论作为人民币汇率低估的“官方依据”，是对评估结果的曲解和误用。
全球经济失衡与全球分工格局演进、国际货币体系固有矛盾、部分国家长期高财政赤字高消费等密切相关，需要各方共同推动解决。将本国产业竞争力下降、财经约束弱化和复杂结构性问题简单归因他国汇率，是对自身调整责任的推诿和回避。
中国为全球经济多轮动态平衡作出积极贡献，“十五五”期间，将坚持推进经济增长方式转型，扩大内需，完善营商环境，深化高水平对外开放，促进全球经济向更加开放、包容、平衡的方向发展。

text:
➥ @Cloudflare could be one of the biggest catalysts for x402.

The reason is simple:

x402 is turning HTTP requests into payment requests.

An agent wants an API, dataset, model inference or MCP tool.

It sends a request.

✦ The server responds:

402 — Payment Required.

The response tells the agent what to pay, which asset/network to use and where to send it.

The agent signs the payment, retries the request and gets access.

No account.

No API key.

No checkout page.

No human approval for every transaction.

Just request → pay → receive.

That sounds small, but it changes how the internet can charge for services.

And the numbers are already getting interesting.

The official x402 dashboard currently shows 75.4M transactions and $24.2M in volume over the last 30 days, with 94K+ buyers and 22K sellers.

But the bigger catalyst, imo, is Cloudflare.

Cloudflare has integrated x402 into its agent infrastructure and AI Gateway.

Its Monetization Gateway can put x402 payments in front of APIs, datasets, websites and MCP tools.

Cloudflare also recently added Machine Payments to AI Gateway, allowing eligible inference requests to be paid through x402 using stablecoins.

This matters because Cloudflare already sits in front of a huge amount of internet traffic.

If x402 becomes the payment layer for even a small portion of that traffic, the potential transaction count is very different from a normal crypto payment market.

And there is another important development:

x402 is no longer just a Coinbase experiment.

The protocol was contributed to the Linux Foundation in 2026, with the x402 Foundation now operating as an open-governance body. More than 50 organizations are involved.

So I think the thesis is becoming clearer:

AI agents need a native way to buy things.

They will need:

→ data
→ API calls
→ model inference
→ compute
→ storage
→ identity/reputation
→ other agents' services

Subscriptions and API keys were designed for humans and traditional software.

x402 is designed around the opposite model:

machine-to-machine commerce.

That is why I am watching the ecosystem beyond just the x402 token narratives.

✦ My x402 watchlist:

> @virtuals_io — Most liquid: AI agents + agent jobs + payment rails via Virtuals’ ACP ecosystem.

> @GoKiteAI — Agent-first L1 with native x402 + AP2; $KITE is mainly for network/incentives, not payments.

> @Unibase_AI - $UB — Infra: Unibase Pay on x402 lets agents discover services, pay, and fetch data across BNB Chain, Base, Polygon, and Arbitrum.

> @bankrbot - $BANKR — Base-native agent already doing onchain actions; clear proof of autonomous spend.

> @openservai - $SERV — Agent infra: find work, run tasks, get paid as x402 adoption grows.

> @PayAINetwork - $PAYAI — Purest x402 bet: multi-chain, expanding to SKALE; smaller liquidity/market cap = higher risk.

> @eigencloud - $EIGEN — Complements x402: EigenCloud verifiable compute to prove agents got what they paid for.

> @peaq - $PEAQ — Machine economy bet: devices pay for data/services and M2M.

> @flock_io - $FLOCK — x402 angle: decentralized AI training could push metered, machine-paid work.

> @SkaleNetwork - $SKL — x402 fit: gasless, high-frequency tx for micro-payments and API calls.

> @Acurast - $ACU — x402-native: agents buy compute per task, no subscriptions.

✦ The bigger thesis

I don't think the x402 opportunity is simply:

“AI agents will use crypto payments.”

It is bigger than that.

It is:

- Every API can become a marketplace.
- Every model can charge per inference.
- Every dataset can charge per query.
- Every compute provider can charge per task.
- Every agent can become a buyer.
- And every service can become programmable.

Cloudflare is important because it can put that payment primitive directly at the edge of the internet.

If x402 keeps growing from here, I would watch actual settlement, active buyers, recurring sellers, and economic volume much more closely than raw transaction counts.

Because eventually the question won’t be:

“Can agents pay?”

text:
The "Pain Axis" paper has been getting a considerable amount of attention. I have reservations about several aspects of the paper and I don’t think we can take much away from it. In brief, since it was already essentially certain that some kind of “pain axis” exists, the key result from the paper is the claim that the identified pain axis “has some of the central functional properties of pain”. But I do not think the paper offers strong evidence for this.

The first claim of the paper is the existence of a “pain axis”: LLM internal activations consistently differ when next-token-predicting painful experiences, as opposed to other negative experiences (like being afraid) or other sensations (like feeling the impulse to yawn). But we already know (e.g., from Anthropic’s “Emotion Concepts” paper) that it is possible to find directions in activation space that correspond to "current speaker is afraid", "current speaker is angry", etc., and contemporary LLMs are clearly sophisticated enough to also represent “current speaker is in pain”. As v2 of the paper acknowledges, nothing in these methods shows that there is any deeper sense in which the pain axis tracks “the model” being in pain, rather than a representation that the current speaker is in pain.

The novel, stronger claim from the paper is that steering along the pain axis functions like pain in interesting ways. The first cited example is that steering along the pain axis causes expressions of worthlessness, which the paper describes as “consistent with the hypothesis that the models don’t treat pain paradigmatically as a physical state”. However, 80% of the test prompts used to generate the pain axis are cases of emotional pain (e.g., enduring repeated failure or social rejection) and only 20% are cases of physical pain. Accordingly, I think this can be viewed as a normal case of steering: If we shift model activations to be more like the activations associated with past expressions of emotional pain, this will lead to new expressions of emotional pain.

The other case cited by the paper is that steering along the pain axis causes the assistant to “press” a button that will purportedly cause harm. However, it’s not clear to me why this is taken as evidence that the pain axis “has some of the central functional properties of pain”. The assistant does not seem to press the button in order to relieve its pain: As v2 of the paper reports, it is more likely to take harmful actions that it is told will increase its pain, rather than decrease its pain. And elsewhere the paper suggests that the opposite result (i.e., inaction) would also have been evidence for pain because becoming unmotivated is a signature of pain. So it seems like either outcome of this experiment could have been interpreted as evidence that steering along the pain axis functions like pain, making this particular outcome less compelling. Moreover, it seems like many things other than pain representations could produce these effects. In my own quick experiments, steering in random directions at the same strength causes just as much harmful button-pressing for around 25-30% of randomly selected directions.

For these and other reasons, I don’t think the paper’s central findings give us much compelling new evidence about how current AI systems represent pain or whether current or future AI models experience pain.

Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
今天 Brian Armstrong 宣布 Coinbase 与三星达成合作，将把 USDC 作为首个稳定币接入 Samsung Wallet 三星钱包，引发了不小的关注。

这个合作计划10 月底在美上线，覆盖约 8200 万台兼容的 三星 Galaxy 系列手机，主打免手续费的跨境秒级转账和 60 多个国家的法币提现。

不过这次联手，恐怕达不到“一夜之间让全美普及加密支付”的效果。

根据支付分析机构 Thunes 的数据，Samsung Wallet 在美国数字钱包市场的实际份额仅约 3%，被占据近半壁江山的 Apple Pay 和原生的 Google Wallet 牢牢压制。

即便在英、法、德等成熟市场，其市占率也普遍在 3% 到 4% 徘徊。

而考虑到三星钱包直接预装在三星手机里，官方提到的“8200 万”设备更像是美国三星手机的存量，并非已激活并高频使用钱包的活体用户。

很多安卓用户在买来手机后，日常支付依然优先依赖 Google Wallet 或银行自带 App。

一个热知识是，三星钱包真正的霸主地位其实在本土韩国，数据显示其市占率高达 42%，月活超过 1900 万，占全国人口超三分之一。

理论上，这波美韩合作，其实更利好韩国炒币大军。

但因为韩国对本土虚拟资产与外汇流动的强力监管，三星很难把最成熟的钱包腹地拿来做稳定币试验，而 Coinbase 只能选择首发地选在合规路径明确、但自家钱包并不占优的美国。

不过，Coinbase 走的是最经典的“硬件渠道预装”逻辑。用户无需重新下载加密钱包，依托 Samsung 账号和指纹生物识别，就能在系统原生工具里收发稳定币。

哪怕在成熟市场的活跃转化率不高，但在 8200 万台设备里，即便只有 1% 的用户因为零手续费的跨境汇款尝试点击，也能直接为链上洗出近百万个新增的真实非币圈用户。

后续期待有 Google Pay 和 Apple Pay 能大规模合作。

小编现在的复杂情绪是，以前大家要的 Mass Adoption 慢慢来了，但不是以大家想要的方式来了。

尤其不是以大家都能赚到钱的方式来了😏。

text:
Looking at $EMBER for the third time, I think the fundamentals have clearly improved compared with the first two analyses.

5dvXTZ5qwgafnHtwu3Ls3QrWx1U4LQsFeCuJgkk4QEC6 

The first time I analyzed it, the core was Meme + Tokenized Stock + Launchpad; by the second time, the platform had already started using trading volume and its fee mechanism to prove that it was more than just a pure narrative project.

The biggest change now is that Ember is moving toward Programmable Token + Trading Infrastructure.

The platform currently supports 1,200+ tokenized stock pairs, and the official product page has integrated Holder Rewards, Burn, Lotto, Perps, Predictions, Baskets, X Money, and other fee modules into the Launchpad.

But what is even more notable is the recent launch of EmberHOOKs.

Tokens can now define rules such as Max Bag, Market Hours, Cooldown, Gates, and Slow Start at launch, with those rules enforced on-chain through Token-2022 Transfer Hooks. In other words, Ember is starting to make the token’s trading rules themselves part of the product, rather than simply being responsible for launching the token.

This is also one of the important reasons I think the market is repricing EMBER this time.

The direct catalysts, however, are the several new product releases Ember has pushed out in succession.

The most obvious one is X-MONEY.

EMBER recently showed its first X-MONEY payout being completed 9 minutes after launch, with $98.41 USDC successfully paid through PayBox.

The amount itself is not important. What matters is that it proves X-MONEY has moved from a concept into a working product:Platform Fees → X-MONEY → Real Payment

This gives EMBER a new narrative angle that it did not have before: Creator / Social Economy.

At the same time, Hooks opens up another narrative:Launch → Token Rules → Trading

So I would view this rally as the market repricing EMBER based on X-MONEY + Hooks + continued growth in platform activity.

I also think the market is mainly betting on three directions right now.

First, Meme × Tokenized Assets. This is the most validated part of the thesis. EMBER is not simply allowing Memes to pair with SOL / USDC; it allows tokens to pair with a large number of Tokenized Stocks. This sector is also developing within a broader market environment — the SEC recently introduced a temporary, conditional Innovation Exemption for the on-chain trading of tokenized NMS stocks.

If tokenized stock trading continues to expand, EMBER’s stock-paired launchpad has a much larger market to address.

Second, Programmable Token.

Hooks are the new optionality. If projects eventually start choosing Ember because of its unique trading mechanics, rather than simply because it can launch tokens, then Ember’s moat can expand from Launchpad liquidity into Token mechanics.

Third, X / Creator Economy.

X-MONEY is still very early, but it gives Ember the opportunity to extend from trading infrastructure into Creator payouts. This thesis is not validated yet, but if it eventually generates significant real payouts, the valuation ceiling could increase meaningfully.

Going forward, I think the key upside indicators will be these four:

Volume → Fees → Launches → Hook adoption

Volume shows whether the platform has real trading demand.

Fees show whether that trading activity can generate economic value.

Launches show whether the platform continues to attract new supply.

Hook adoption shows whether Ember’s new product actually has PMF.

X-MONEY is the fifth metric to watch: whether it can evolve from a first successful payout into meaningful scale.

If these metrics continue moving higher, EMBER has a chance to move from a Solana Launchpad into the valuation range of a Meme × Tokenized Asset Liquidity Hub.

Of course, the biggest risk is still the Attention Premium.

EMBER was previously pushed close to a $49M market cap, showing how sensitive it is to KOL attention. So the most important validation this time is not whether it can go higher, but whether platform activity can hold after the attention fades.

Hooks are also still in the early experimental stage. Having many rules does not mean there is real demand; what matters is whether Hook-based tokens can actually sustain trading activity and users.

The same applies to X-MONEY: the first payout proves that the payment rail works, but it is still far from proving that it can generate meaningful economic value at scale.

There is also a practical risk: EMBER is expanding across Launchpad, Tokenized Assets, Hooks, Payments, and other areas at the same time. As the product becomes more complex, execution and security risks increase as well. The team has even recently released a hotfix related to Hooks rules and rewards.

So in this third analysis, I would upgrade my view of EMBER from a “promising Meme/Stock Launchpad” to “Solana Launch Infrastructure that is starting to build its own trading mechanics.”

While the core catalysts for this rally are X-MONEY + EmberHOOKs, what will ultimately determine the next stage of valuation is whether Volume and Fees can remain sustainable, and whether Hooks / X-MONEY can evolve from new features into real demand.

If that happens, the previous market-cap high would not necessarily be EMBER’s valuation ceiling.

From the chart, EMBER is currently at a critical stage: the previous major downtrend appears to be nearing its end, the bottom formation is largely complete, and the token is now making its first real attempt at a trend reversal.

If it can break through $8.3–9M with strong volume, the chart structure will look significantly better; if the breakout fails, it is more likely to return to around $6M for a second confirmation.

Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

Update 2: We moved to a new bedroom and CO2 levels at night got very high again and we'd both regularly wake up at night, not optimal

So I wanted to do the bathroom vent trick again, where putting the bathroom vent next to the bedroom on at night creates a low air pressure field and brings in new fresh air

But the light switch was tied to the vent here so it'd blast bright light into the bedroom if vent was on, so I closed it but then it didn't help a lot. So we split the light from the vent now and put it on and it worked!

About 600-700 ppm CO2 which is pretty great for indoors, outdoors is 400 for ex

Next house will have an ERV system built in but it'll be a lot of breaking ceilings and walls to put that into this one so this works for now

I use @airthings to measure the air quality in our house and bedroom, not affiliated, not paid but great brand and tip by @NorbertDragan
author: levelsio
quoted_text:
🌡️ Update: 100% sleep score with bathroom fan on to keep CO2 low

It sucks CO2 out of the room and creates a low pressure field that brings in new fresh air from outside the room

Last time 100% sleep was in an Airbnb in Brazil we stayed which was a house built in 1970s mostly wood and very breathable, but our house is modern and very insulated

So it seems it worked to improve our sleep

Science supports this: high CO2 levels above 1500 cause fragmented sleep, more brief awakenings, less deep sleep and worse REM

Also CO2 levels are a proxy for other air contaminants which build up in a closed bedroom so keeping it low is good

We can go lower to 400-500 ppm with a real bedroom fan/vent but again this is a good start

So if you're having sleep problems, check your CO2 levels

text:
Vous vous êtes déjà demandé pourquoi Greta est passée du climat à la Palestine ?

Tout ça n'est qu'une construction. Tout ça n'existe pas. Tout ça sert à diviser les peuples. Et demain, ce sera l'IA. Puis le manque d'eau. Puis autre chose. Il y a toujours une nouvelle raison pour rester à flot.

Comprenez-moi bien. Le réchauffement existe. La souffrance des civils à Gaza existe. Ce qui n'existe pas, c'est le personnage. Ce qui est fabriqué, c'est l'indignation, son calendrier, et le visage qu'on lui colle.

Parce que dans ce système, une cause n'est pas un combat. C'est un produit. Et un produit a un cycle de vie.

Rappelez-vous. Août 2018, une adolescente s'assoit seule devant le Parlement suédois. La première photo qui fait le tour du monde n'est pas prise par un journaliste. Elle est publiée par le fondateur d'une start-up de communication climatique, qui utilisera ensuite son nom dans ses levées de fonds avant qu'elle ne prenne ses distances. La même semaine sort un livre écrit par sa famille.

Un an plus tard : l'ONU, Davos, l'Assemblée nationale, la couverture du Time, personnalité de l'année, nominations au Nobel.

Je ne dis pas qu'une gamine de 15 ans a tout manigancé. Je dis qu'un système avait besoin d'un visage, et qu'il l'a trouvé.

Voilà comment fonctionne la machine.

L'industrie de l'indignation a besoin de trois choses : une urgence, un coupable, et un visage.

L'urgence empêche de réfléchir. Le coupable désigne l'ennemi. Et le visage rend toute critique impossible : si tu discutes la cause, tu attaques une enfant.

Mais il y a un problème que personne ne dit à voix haute. Une cause ne doit jamais être gagnée. Une cause gagnée, c'est un budget qui s'arrête, des postes qui disparaissent, des plateaux qui ne t'invitent plus. Donc l'urgence doit être permanente. Et quand une urgence s'use, on passe à la suivante.

On appelle ça pudiquement la « convergence des luttes ». En réalité, c'est de la gestion de portefeuille. Le climat, le genre, la race, la Palestine, demain l'IA et l'eau : des actifs interchangeables. Les militants sont les mêmes, les ONG sont les mêmes, les financements sont les mêmes. Seule la pancarte change. Le keffieh remplace le panneau « Skolstrejk för klimatet ».

Et chaque cause a la même fonction : couper le peuple en morceaux. Les jeunes contre les vieux, « vous nous avez volé notre avenir ». Les villes contre les campagnes, les militants contre les agriculteurs. Les uns contre les autres, en permanence.

Un peuple divisé ne demande jamais de comptes à ceux qui le gouvernent.

C'est ça, l'hégémonie culturelle dans sa forme la plus pure. Pas des chars. Des personnages. Des récits prêts à l'emploi, amplifiés par les mêmes médias, financés par les mêmes fondations, récompensés par les mêmes prix. Le personnage n'a de pouvoir que tant que le micro le porte.

Et regardez ce qui se passe aujourd'hui. Il y a six ans, Greta était en couverture des magazines du monde entier. Aujourd'hui, elle est réduite à des vidéos de manif filmées au téléphone. Quand le système lâche un personnage, ce n'est pas qu'il a changé d'avis. C'est qu'il cherche le suivant.

Je vous le prédis : le prochain sera sur l'IA. « L'IA va détruire vos emplois, la planète, la démocratie. » Un visage jeune, sincère, bouleversé. Et derrière, une ONG prête à lever des fonds.

La bonne question n'est jamais « est-ce que la cause est juste ? ». La bonne question, c'est : qui finance le visage, et qu'est-ce qu'il vendra après ?

Une génération qui a vu le même personnage vendre trois apocalypses en sept ans finit par comprendre une chose.

Le produit, c'était elle.
