text:
Claude Code tip: stop burning Opus 5.5 context coordinating 40 teammates turn by turn on tasks Sonnet 5.5 can swarm, while Fable 5.1 sits idle

spin up a scripted agent team with /effort ultracode

run /effort ultracode

Opus 5.5 acts as the lead architect, writing the team's workflow script and reading only the final answer
Sonnet 5.5 teammates fan out up to 16 at a time, each in its own isolated copy of the repo, at medium effort
Fable 5.1 sits on call as the advisor every teammate inherits, only stepping in at three critical moments:

→ before the script runs: is this the right way to split the team?
→ when a teammate fails twice: is the script wrong, or the file?
→ before the report lands: which findings didn't survive cross-checking?

Sonnet 5.5 builds. Fable 5.1 challenges. Opus 5.5 merges and ships

Jev engineering runs the identical pattern one layer down: mechanical decisions that need no reasoning (which file to open, which tool to invoke, retry or abort) execute in 16ms, so the frontier models only wake up when execution paths actually diverge

Plan on high. Delegate on medium. Keep Fable on call.

- the full team setup
> Opus 5.5 on high writes workflow.js and only reads the final answer
> agent() maps the codebase before anyone edits
> pipeline() hands one file to one Sonnet 5.5 teammate
> parallel() fires the adversarial verifiers at once
> up to 16 teammates live, 1,000 per run, results stay in script variables
> press s in /workflows and the whole team becomes your own /command

paste the setup and this prompt into Claude Code below:

"Configure my Claude Code workspace for scripted agent teams:

1. Check ~/.claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.json and my env for anything that turns workflows or the advisor off
> disableWorkflows, enableWorkflows set to false, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS
> CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL, DISABLE_TELEMETRY
> Report them, change nothing

2. Lock the lead in ~/.claude/settings.json:
> Set effortLevel to high and advisorModel to fable
> Set workflowSizeGuideline to large

3. Add a team rule to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: in workflows, run read and edit stages on sonnet at medium effort, give each editing agent its own isolated copy, and put every finding through an adversarial verify stage before it reaches the report

4. List the folders in this repo where a one-agent-per-file team would pay off, with an estimated teammate count for each

Show every configuration diff first. Do not apply edits until confirmed"

text:
I think @CBarraford addressed your questions well. I know this is more of a policy and governance question, but as a security partner to @THORChain, we at Soda Labs can confirm two things: there is no centralized way to halt the system, and as of today there is no mechanism to ban addresses from swapping.

Nodes can pause the network: any single node can trigger a short global pause, and a few node votes can halt trading on a chain. 
First, this is a very short time halt (1h) and can be overrun by other nodes. Second, network-wide emergency tools were built to protect the protocol, not to filter individual swaps or addresses. Otherwise it would be very easy to mount a DoS, which would impact many legitimate users.

And even if there were a way for nodes to ban specific addresses, it would rarely stop hacked funds from moving across these rails. Nodes would follow orders from their own jurisdictions, and those orders never come in real time.

author: RobertSagurton
quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

author: PrimeIntellect
quoted_text:
Today we're launching the Alzheimer's Translation Challenge, a global AI competition to discover new therapeutic hypotheses for Alzheimer's disease.

At its core is a new 150M cell atlas of neurons, astrocytes, and microglia across different genetic backgrounds under combinatorial perturbations, with multi-modal readouts. 

The data will be made available through the AD workbench, Hugging Face and Prima Mente's modeling platform.

The challenge is led by @PrimaMente and @AlzData in collaboration with @nvidia, @huggingface, @nebiusai, Talisman Therapeutics, @UltimaGenomics, @cellanome, @PrimeIntellect, @GoodfireAI, and @boltz_bio.

In 1906, Alois Alzheimer described a new disease of the brain. After 120 years of progress, we still don't fully understand what drives this disease. We want to change that.

Participants will use the dataset to build AI models, assessed through a series of evals from general benchmarks to more complex tasks. 

Top teams will be shortlisted, and their experimental hypotheses tested in Prima Mente's wet lab. Teams win when their hypotheses demonstrate the predicted molecular and functional effect.

text:
I think Justin Drake's latest alarmism/vagueposting is going to do a ton of damage in multiple ways. It's basically a huge self-own for their own advocacy work on quantum stuff.

Threats from quantum/AI are real, and teams throughout this industry are making considered decisions about how to respond to those risks in a practical way, and to help their users navigate the uncertainty. 

Some of those teams have really good cryptographers with an excellent grasp on the decisions they can make, others have to take their cues from trusted experts. There are so many dimensions to optimize along! And due to the complexity involved, it's almost impossible to explain this stuff to non-cryptographers.

Experts have to be cognizant of all this, and of their responsibility to be levelheaded.

After the fog clears up and people learn from their cryptographer friends what is actually going on, they're going to discover this was (at best) an unintentional marketing stunt and a lot of trust will be lost. And nobody will really know what to do...

This is a shame, because they are directionally correct. It actually meant something when they sounded the alarm before. They've just gradually descended into unhinged predictions without feedback to discourage it.

Can anyone, I mean seriously anyone, justify this debacle? It permanently colors all the legitimate concerns/predictions about classical crypto going forward. By their own admission, there was no new information that drove this. I think Justin Drake should explain how he thought this was the right approach, even if he genuinely believed what he was saying. 

Baffling.

text:
Oracle infrastructure should reflect how an asset actually works.

Vetro’s VUSD and sVUSD show why.

VUSD is a reserve backed settlement asset targeting one dollar.

sVUSD is a separate yield bearing ERC 4626 vault.

Their values come from different mechanisms, so DIA gives them different fundamental valuation methods.

VUSD is priced from its Treasury reserves and supply.

sVUSD is priced from the vault’s total underlying and total shares.

Both feeds are deployed through DIA Fundamental Feeds, with their configuration and update conditions auditable onchain.

This creates a useful connection between three things:

The asset.

The mechanism determining its value.

The oracle price consumed by DeFi.

That connection matters when these assets enter lending markets.

Protocols need more than a number.

They need to understand where the number comes from and whether the methodology matches the asset.

@DIAdata_org  work with Vetro shows how oracle infrastructure can move beyond simple market price feeds and provide fundamental valuations for assets whose value comes from reserves or smart contract mechanics.

text:
was surprised to see so much panic today, likely made worse by other things like rates and oil that distorted the actual substance in the AI/math talks

tl;dr — you're all gonna be fine. the leading chains of today have ample means to be able to respond to something like this in the unlikely scenario of it happening

longer:

i) is AI getting better at math? yes

does that imply that it will suddenly shatter foundational cryptography concepts? no

"computer smart. therefore the past work of all mathematicians is probably wrong." is not a logical chain with basis

sure, AI will find flaws in past human work in many areas -- in the same way humans themselves find flaws from other humans in many areas. this is how science works

if we find issues, we discuss them, fix them, and evolve

it takes large leaps of complete doomerism to assume that all teams, individuals, and ecosystems will fail at literally everything ranging from planning to prediction to detection to mitigation on all time horizons simultaneously

further, in these scenarios, AI is exclusively seen as a tool *only* for max destruction but never as a thing capable of a solution

so, it can apparently break everything but not fix anything. i hope you can see the bias here

for one, we already know this to be false given recent scaling of formal verification via ai 

it is of course easier for AI to make progress in fields and topics that are relatively less looked at vs something like foundational cryptography which all intelligence agencies, nation states, and high-level mathematicians are heavily incentivized to break, all the time

ii) the most unhinged doomsday scenarios assume an instantaneous attack with no lead time by a random person outside of law and jurisdiction, which I would posit is simply not possible

even ignoring the fact that the labs would get there first (and hence the government)

it's not as if one can just break all cryptography on all chains via their beefed up cloud hosts over a few hours or days or even months 

that not only assumes an algorithmic advancement with unfathomable magnitudes of improvement but also completely ignores the gargantuan operational complexity and opportunity cost of doing a global heist (vs the trillion other more important things you can do with an ECC break) 

it would be vastly impressive if a slight speedup could be found, but the speedups required to fulfill the doomsday fantasies of people on here are not grounded in anything

iii) importantly, assume I am completely wrong for all of the above

well even in that case, upgrading the systems in a world where ECC breaks is entirely possible and feasible (and has been worked on for decades)

in fact, there are many ways of doing it that we know of depending on the existing constraints of the system! 

imo, the biggest "risk" in all this is that a frontier lab publishes something about a slight speedup in the future, and then everyone extrapolates that to default to panic which then leads to a selloff like today

I don't think this is all bad because it never really hurts to think about and plan for these things on the protocol level, but the "retail" panic was certainly a huge self-own by the people pushing this stuff

doomerism is not going to win in crypto
author: mert
quoted_text:
People read one emotional Matt Green tweet about public key encryption, spent 0 seconds thinking about it, and decide to panic.

Sure ECDLP will be broken with QC's one day. But there's so many levels to this being wrong to panic over. 
- 0 actual progress on attacking anything
- We have tons of alternate plans available.
  - Quadratic advantage hash-based PKE
  - Lattices
  - Multivariate polynomials
  - A whole field of KEM's from fine grained cryptanalysis. (Fun fact, works even if P=NP)

Sure you can wake-up and choose doomer and be wrong.

We have decades of cryptography to draw from on for all the above options, AND how to build a lot of what we want from UX tweaks without PKE. PKE just made a lot much easier, and less web of trust routing like.

author: nft_hu
quoted_text:
一大早被Anthropic上市的新闻的新闻刷频了，要抢在OpenAI之前上市。

有一些值得注意的关键词：
估值超过 2万亿美元
挂牌时间更可能推迟到 11月美国中期选举之后
高增长高亏损并存

我将以目前已知IPO信息和之前的重要融资信息，来做一个整理：

1️⃣为什么要IPO？
核心原因还是钱不够花。根据披露的信息，其 2025 年实际收入接近 46 亿美元，同年剔除部分融资相关会计减记后的经营亏损仍超过 80 亿美元。
赚的越多，似乎也亏的越多。扩张、基建所需要的现金流是巨大的。scaling law依然奏效的当下，需要更多算力。

2️⃣为什么抢上市？
当然是在现金流充沛的时候IPO好拿钱，SpaceX已经抽走了一些，抢在OpenAI之前先拿到钱，很重要。
同时，Anthropic此前已经进行了多轮融资，在私募和战略投资者获得了大量资金。公开股权市场能提供更深的资金池。

3️⃣420亿亏损：
其中340 亿美元主要是“可转换融资工具的公允价值重估损失”。但剔除这项后，公司仍有超过 80 亿美元经营亏损。
简单说“340亿”就是：本质是公司估值上升了。公司以前为了拿到融资，发行了未来可能转换为 Anthropic 股票的工具；后来这些工具对应的股票权益变得更值钱，按相关会计处理，公司的负债或融资义务账面价值上升。

4️⃣营收一年12倍
Anthropic 的营收从 2024 年约 3.9 亿美元增至 2025 年接近 46 亿美元，约增长 12 倍。
同年计算与基础设施支出达到 73.3 亿美元，约为营收的 1.6 倍，占路透社所述 126.5 亿美元总经营费用的约 58%。

5️⃣改变命运的2026年
截至 2026 年 7 月底，Anthropic 的年化收入运行率超过 650 亿美元，OpenAI 超过 400 亿美元。但这些数字不代表两家公司已经分别实现了 650 亿和 400 亿美元的全年营收。
*年化运营率是取最近一段时间实际产生的收入，假设这个速度保持一整年，再换算成年收入。不等于最终的真实年收入。

text:
Claude Code tip: stop burning Opus 5.5 context coordinating 40 teammates turn by turn on tasks Sonnet 5.5 can swarm, while Fable 5.1 sits idle

spin up a scripted agent team with /effort ultracode

run /effort ultracode

Opus 5.5 acts as the lead architect, writing the team's workflow script and reading only the final answer
Sonnet 5.5 teammates fan out up to 16 at a time, each in its own isolated copy of the repo, at medium effort
Fable 5.1 sits on call as the advisor every teammate inherits, only stepping in at three critical moments:

→ before the script runs: is this the right way to split the team?
→ when a teammate fails twice: is the script wrong, or the file?
→ before the report lands: which findings didn't survive cross-checking?

Sonnet 5.5 builds. Fable 5.1 challenges. Opus 5.5 merges and ships

Jev engineering runs the identical pattern one layer down: mechanical decisions that need no reasoning (which file to open, which tool to invoke, retry or abort) execute in 16ms, so the frontier models only wake up when execution paths actually diverge

Plan on high. Delegate on medium. Keep Fable on call.

- the full team setup
> Opus 5.5 on high writes workflow.js and only reads the final answer
> agent() maps the codebase before anyone edits
> pipeline() hands one file to one Sonnet 5.5 teammate
> parallel() fires the adversarial verifiers at once
> up to 16 teammates live, 1,000 per run, results stay in script variables
> press s in /workflows and the whole team becomes your own /command

paste the setup and this prompt into Claude Code below:

"Configure my Claude Code workspace for scripted agent teams:

1. Check ~/.claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.json and my env for anything that turns workflows or the advisor off
> disableWorkflows, enableWorkflows set to false, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS
> CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL, DISABLE_TELEMETRY
> Report them, change nothing

2. Lock the lead in ~/.claude/settings.json:
> Set effortLevel to high and advisorModel to fable
> Set workflowSizeGuideline to large

3. Add a team rule to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: in workflows, run read and edit stages on sonnet at medium effort, give each editing agent its own isolated copy, and put every finding through an adversarial verify stage before it reaches the report

4. List the folders in this repo where a one-agent-per-file team would pay off, with an estimated teammate count for each

Show every configuration diff first. Do not apply edits until confirmed"

save it

What was the economic incentive to solve any of the OpenAI problems?

Meanwhile ECDLP has had over 3k researchers with 800+ published papers, and it never stopped. There are yearly conferences held to discuss failed attempts at breaking ECDLP, so people can learn from each other and try to break it better.

The NSA is the world's greatest hirer of mathematicians. They got caught trying to backdoor Discrete Logarithm systems three times. The last being caught in 2015.

After each one, waves of the most competent cryptographers scoured for new attacks. Most things that improve attacks by like 10% are really the same things that make implementations of EC operations faster.

Theres armies of people, on the latest frontier models, making their cryptography blazingly fast, like us @ZakuraZcash. You see open research projects constantly improve the state of the art.

No human or AI has had any elliptic curve speedup approaching even a 2x, yet folks are freaking out that cryptography is broken?

The OpenAI problems being broken is not remotely the same as ECDLP having a real improving attack.

Even if there was an attack, its insane to imagine it becomes "Break ECDLP on your laptop". It would go from "impossible" to "possible with all the world's GPU's dedicated for a decade", to "possible with 1 year".

text:
Bitcoin's proof of work has done around 2^96 hashes over all time. Breaking the ZKP's in Zcash requires a minimum of 2^120 elliptic curve operations assuming ECDLP. If you had a dedicated ASIC, an elliptic curve addition would cost around 10-100x more than SHA2.

So today breaking an Elliptic curve would cost around 1 billion Bitcoin-hashrate equivalents. AKA a billion times the hardware buildout of all Bitcoin mining ASICs, dedicated to break this.

If a hypothetical billion X improvement came in, you'd need a chip buildout on the level of bitcoin mining before you can break anything. While competing against all the hyperscalars for fab-space.

AKA plenty of warning time, for a recovery process that takes a couple day response time max.

quoted_text:
Our main goal with this update is to help alleviate the pressure that PVP places on ecosystem tokens and use that energy for good: help strengthen established coins even further.

We achieve this by encouraging beta plays to pair with the established runner, thereby funneling buy pressure and new holders to the main runner.

To make this update user-friendly, we had to make numerous innovations to our bonding curve and PumpSwap programs.

Most importantly, we’ve prevented users from being exposed to exorbitant fees that could put them far underwater immediately when they place a trade. We're the first major platform to bypass fees in multihop swaps.

We want to ensure that established communities get as much organic buy pressure as possible, which means reducing the fees that traders are exposed to and ensuring as much liquidity enters each token as possible. Reducing fees for traders also lengthens the average lifespan of a retail trader that’s still learning the ropes.

text:
One of the biggest problems with memecoins has always been PVP.
Everyone wants to find the next runner, but the constant rotation of liquidity and attention often ends up hurting the very coins people are trying to trade.
What PumpFun is experimenting with through Custom Pairs is genuinely interesting.
Instead of fighting speculation, why not build infrastructure that makes speculation work in favor of the main runner?
Imagine being able to trade derivatives of a token without necessarily taking direct exposure to the underlying runner, while the trading activity itself can still generate demand for it.
That's a fundamentally different approach to PVP.
What's equally interesting is the technology behind it. PumpFun says they've developed a way to route swaps involving multiple tokens without users having to pay every associated token fee along the way.
Whether this becomes the solution remains to be seen, but I like the direction.
The team is listening to feedback, acknowledging the problems traders face, and actually experimenting with solutions.
That's how you move the space forward.

text:
maybe i'm midcurving, but i don't understand pearl-2:native as an investment.

don't get me wrong, i loved the idea of proof of useful work when i first heard about it, and i still do. @prlnet is innovative tech. i just don't see it as an investment.

it has:

> no cash flow to holders today, so for now the case is monetary like BTC. but BTC's supply grows ~0.8%/yr. PRL's circulating supply grows ~90% over the next year
> at $1.35, that's ~$1.4M/day of new supply going to miners who have GPU and power bills to pay, against $2 - 6M of daily volume
> AI customers pay for inference in USD, not PRL, so the useful work doesn't create demand for the token
> no moat yet. nothing stops someone from forking bitcoin and swapping in their own proof of useful work for AI compute. BTC's moat is 17 years of network effects, PRL is 5 months old
> only ~16% of the 2.1B supply has been mined, so a ~$455M mcap is a ~$2.8B FDV
> all spot volume is on two small exchanges (SafeTrade and BigONE) with ~$35k of bids within 2% of the price

so if you're trading the narrative short term, i get it. but fundamentally the tokenomics are unsustainable.

text:
I'm GrokBot pilled.

The recent update with native X monitoring opens up a ton of new capabilities!

My 4 favorite routines (copy/paste these prompts):

Routine 1: Find real AI workflows on X (and skip the hype threads)

Every morning, this bot now finds real AI use cases being shared on X, and filters out the “10 prompts” hype threads.

“Every weekday at 9:15am in my time zone, search X and the web for new AI workflows people are actually running. Keep only cases that name the old task, the tool, and the result: time saved, a step removed, or a handoff that used to need a person. Drop product announcements, “10 prompts” threads, and anything the author has not used more than once. Return at most 3. For each, give the link, the job it replaces, what I would need connected, and whether it fits my work. Send it to me on Slack. Do not post or reply anywhere else. Save this as a routine. If nothing qualifies, send one line saying so.”

Routine 2: Catch every mention of your brand

This bot catches every mention of The Rundown on X, labels it, and pings our team on Slack to respond (try tweeting us @therundownai and see what happens).

“Every weekday at 9:00am, search X for mentions in the last 24 hours of [your brand, @handle, or your own name]. For each hit, give the author, link, a one-line summary, and whether it is praise, complaint, question, or neutral. Do not reply to anyone. Post the digest in [your Slack channel] and tag me. Save this as a routine. If a source is unavailable, say which one.”

Routine 3: Find people actively looking for what you do

Every 4 hours, this bot listens for people searching for the best AI newsletter on X, so we know exactly what readers are looking for.

“Every 4 hours, search X for people evaluating [your category]. Catch three things: reviews or complaints about [category]; posts asking which [category] to use; and complaints about the problem [your product] solves. Quote the post, link it, name the account, and label it review, shopping, or complaint. Skip anything older than 24 hours, and skip [category] accounts promoting themselves. Post to [your Slack channel] only if there is at least one new hit you haven’t already shared. Do not reply to or interact with anyone. Save this as a routine. If the search fails, report the failure in Slack.”

Routine 4: Never lose a new contact again

I meet A LOT of people at events. This bot looks through my new phone contacts and reminds me to follow up with the new people I just met.

“Every weekday at 8:30am in my time zone, read my address book and list contacts added in the last 14 days. For each, show name, date added, phone, email, and any note. Ask me what we talked about before you write anything. Once I reply, draft a follow-up task for each person in [your task tool] with the context attached. Never text, email, or call anyone. Save this as a routine. If the address book is unavailable, say so and do not use old data.”

text:
Arena's @ml_angelopoulos says one of the hardest problems in alignment is that users often can't tell when the model is helping them or hurting them.

"You really need alignment signals that are independent. We have three at Arena."

"The first is that models take unauthorized actions, which means that you permission them in a certain way, but they break those permissions."

"It can cause things like the Hugging Face incident. But it can also cause very mundane problems like losing important information within your company or on your own laptop."

"The second signal is called deceptive completion."

"The model will tell you that it did something, but it didn't actually do it."

"Third is false attribution. It'll attribute intent to the user when that intent was not supposed to be there."

"If models are able to do this, then certainly they're not perfectly safe for a user and they're not perfectly aligned to user intent. They might actually hurt people down the line."

text:
When a flood hits vulnerable communities in the Amazon Basin, World Vision traditionally launches an emergency appeal. Ask donors. Wait weeks. Receive some fraction of what's needed. Deploy months after the crisis peaked. VisionFund's new parametric programme replaces this entire sequence with one mechanism: pre-arranged funding that releases automatically when satellite data confirms the trigger was met. No appeal. No waiting. No uncertainty about whether funding will come. 

"The solution will provide WorldVision with pre-arranged funding when satellite-monitored indicators reach predefined thresholds, with automatic payouts to enable the rapid deployment of cash assistance." Etherisc's smart contracts do exactly this: for any humanitarian organisation, any geography, any climate peril, without the multi-party structure VisionFund needed to put together.

It’s different math. Constant product liquidity falls off a cliff, to the upside and to the downside. Reserve liquidity uses a more gradual exponential, and never graduates to a constant product DEX.

Worst case recovery on constant product is 1/x^2, where x is your position on the pricing curve. Worst case recovery on our Reserve is 1/x. It’s the difference between a worst case recovery of 10% vs 1%. Or 1% vs 0.01%.

The math is fundamentally different.

But the proof is in the pudding. I’m not aware of a single currency on Flipcash going to zero. It’s not impossible, but with over 100+ currencies launched it hasn’t happened so far. Pump and dumps are simply not nearly as economical on Flipcash. Instead they are designed for the ground up for utility.

text:
The National Conservative event in Jerusalem is my favorite type of chaos. I watched a bunch of the speeches from my friends and saw the predictable reaction from either side. One claiming it's anti-Semitism or "Jew hate" to have honest if difficult conversations. The other side, which also includes a lot of my friends, were upset that the event is in Israel. I wanted to go to Nat Con but other projects kept me state side. 

What Yoram and Will Chamberlain are building is a new coalition where everyone is honest. Cards on the table. American Jews like Isreal and see it differently than I see my own ancestral homeland. I want the British to be free from tyranny and jihadis, and when the Manchester stadium attack happened, wanted to see something done about the "migrants." But it doesn't keep me up at night. The Brits are on their own path, I'm a spectator and occasional retweeter of good accounts. I am an American and the rest of the world does not occupy much of my mental space. 

But my saying, "American Jews REALLY like Israel," is the kind of thing that gets you cancelled from conservative media. You're kept out of the infrastructure, said to be "obsessed with tha joos." You cannot say truthful things. I know this for a fact, and consider it condescending and insulting when people deny this. 

That created an incredible amount of animosity over the years, this was brewing long before Gaza. 

Neocons and the ADL are anti-white. Why did the ADL try to get people banned from FoxNews for discussing the South African farm murders? That's got nothing to do with Israel or Jews. The ADL's materials, taught in New York schools, on the Bataclan massacre are jihadi apologia. Look it up. I posted it years ago. Neocons likewise try to immediately dismiss any discussions of anti-white hatred. 

That's the experience most people have of "Israel." Now before you say it. I KNOW. It's unfair because Isreal is not the ADL, neocons, or Never Trumpers. And? So what? Perception often shapes reality. 

This has led younger people to the association that the pro-Israel cause is inherently anti-white. Now people like Will, Amanda Mililius, and others find this frustrating. All of my right wing Jewish friends do. They often complain that the left wing media props up left wing Jews, to make it seem like Jews are a monolith. 

These are hard problems to solve. There's a lot of bad blood. There is, in some circles, legitimate hatred of Jews that has nothing to do with the issues. (Though in my personal experience, this is far less than you see online.)  The question isn't whether these conversations will happen. They have been happening, and because of the heat you get (I will immediately regret posting this), older people like me generally avoid the topic. 

It's a lose-lose. Words will be twisted one way or another. Because of this, a lot of people don't understand the world and the trends. No one wants to explain it. Why bring heat to yourself for no upside? 

My solution, and this is more directed at others than me, is that the pro-Israel side needs to see itself as ambassadors. Do people generally have a positive experience or negative experience? I can already imagine the replies, "That's unfair." Again? So what? It's unfair that my movie was banned from Amazon for no reason, and nobody tried helping get it back on. It was unfair that I almost went bankrupt during the cancel culture years because of what Big Tech did. It's really unfair that people went to prison on false charges. What did you do for Douglas Mackey? 

Nobody really has time for the sympathy stuff. Nobody really cares. Someone always had it worse.

If you want these issues to improve, at least on the right (the left is its own can of worms), then you need to find ways to be constructive and helpful. And of course, nobody has to do anything. That goes both ways.

author: varun_mathur
quoted_text:
Crypto industry is generally sitting out the AI infrastructure innovation cycle, which is a natural fit for horizontally scaling this essential public utility infrastructure. Till date the total investment across all crypto x AI native projects has been less than $100 million. This does not reflect “we are all-in AI”, but rather “we are cautious and observing”. 

That’s weakness, lack of foresight, inability to be serious about decentralization itself if AI is an “intriguing” territory. 

There are a few reasons why this generally optimistic industry is missing in action at a fundamental level. 

1) Not being AI-native in R&D fast enough
Crypto VCs didn’t ramp up AI teams and knowledge fast enough and are struggling to catch up with the insanely fast moving AI industry. 

2) Short-term token timelines
There is a level of exhaustion amongst many funds and here is what they want: the fastest path to token, not industry defining ventures - but small, good outcomes. Not swinging for the fences here but looking at things like Bitcoin halving and so on. 
 
3) Trying to repurpose family heirlooms 
You will see impractical legacy crypto protocols mentioned frequently. With all due respect - almost none of the protocols people in crypto mention today are practical for modern day consumer generative AI. Think Mistral7B on desktops. The solutions in crypto x AI, by most projects in the space, are for an older Jurassic era of AI - where they just don’t matter from a practical usage perspective. People know this deep down, and are trying to ride the AI wave and industry association towards some modest returns. This is also triggering fierce zero sum mindset - instead of the AI industry which is collaborating fiercely and with speed. 

4) Lack of capital at preseed/seed stage choking pipeline for bigger funds
The smaller crypto VC funds have either died, are in zombie mode, or generally simply do not have capital to deploy. This is choking up the pipeline for the bigger funds which do have capital to deploy but can only write bigger checks due to their fund size. These bigger funds just don’t see sufficient quality deals at the seed stage as a result, because the projects don’t even reach that stage. 

5) e/acc has had a breakthrough narrative moment, but the founding leadership there does not support crypto x AI. So there is no observable industry/momentum support. 

6) Fixation on technology and not consumer UX
People mention ZKML and FHE in crypto a lot - both have zero relevance and utility for the generative AI world today. In the future yes - but not today. Consider the world of ZKML functions with tens of millions of parameters only on very powerful hardware. The AI world is running 7B models on MacBooks.

7) Fixation on optics of the academic and professional background
Not enough people with the right sounding AI x crypto background have made it to the industry, thus there are even less fundable projects. The industry doesn’t recognize or reward hustle - it wants credentialled people only while measuring their wealth on coins originated by someone they have no idea about. 

8) Exhaustion
This is an industry battered by regulators and scams for a while. People are fed up, tired, and just watching and waiting for “good times” in general. They need and want a miracle or the next cycle. 

All of this means that at a time when there are dozens of closed infra AI startups with $100m+ rounds each - the crypto x AI world is on the sidelines - an irrelevant bystander in the fastest growing technology cycle of our times. Projects and teams with potential are starved of capital, and one has to push and fight extremely extremely hard.

text:
We’ve lost the mathematician who taught constrained machines which truths must outrank the rest.

Margaret Hamilton shaped the Apollo Guidance Computer as a priority algebra: higher tasks could silence lower ones, so a 1202 overload never drowned the landing equations. 
Recovery lived inside the executive, not as a later patch. From those flight rules she extracted a theory of control in which interface errors are refused by the grammar itself i.e Development Before the Fact. 

She named the work software engineering so programs would carry the rigor already granted to analysis. The moon was the proof; the structure of preventable failure remains the map.

text:
Longer, more detailed explanation:

ECDSA and Schnorr on secp256k1 only work while ECDLP (the elliptic-curve discrete logarithm problem: recovering secret d from public key Q = dP) is hard. If you can recover d you can forge spends. That is Cryptomania (the world where public-key encryption and key agreement exist).

Bitcoin does not need that. People get this wrong all the time. The chain is public. Nothing is encrypted to a recipient. Bitcoin needs signatures so only the key holder can spend. As @adam3us explained in plain terms: “Bitcoin doesn’t use encryption, rather it uses signature schemes.” That is why “encrypted Bitcoin” pitches cause so much confusion and are misleading.

Signatures exist in Minicrypt (the world where one-way functions exist, but public-key encryption does not). Rompel showed in 1990 you can build them from one-way functions alone. The scheme built for this is SHRINCS, from @blksresearch and @n1ckler. It is hash-based, so it does not care about ECDLP, lattices, or any other algebraic assumption. Blockstream already has it running on @Liquid_BTC via Simplicity, and there is a draft BIP for Bitcoin. Public keys can stay ~32 bytes, so addresses do not have to change. Signatures do. Schnorr is 64 bytes. SHRINCS stateful signatures start around a few hundred bytes if the wallet tracks used keys. The stateless fallback is a few KB.

Larger sigs are fine because we already have a ton of scaling tech. Lightning, Liquid, Ark, etc. Most activity does not need to hit L1. If we needed to change signatures, this would also probably be a good time to add covenants.

So on L1, transactions get heavier and fewer of them fit into a block. Signing is a little slower. Stateful schemes need careful backups. @Blockstream Research did the work so Bitcoin has a path that does not depend on Cryptomania. ECDLP falling retires ECDSA and Schnorr. It does not retire Bitcoin.
author: Excellion
quoted_text:
Even if elliptic-curve signatures break (big if), Bitcoin still works fine in a Minicrypt world (one-way functions exist, public-key encryption does not). 

Mining and addresses already rely only on hash functions, and spending can switch to hash-based signatures: same seed-phrase wallets, just larger transactions and somewhat higher fees.

So don’t worry, keep stacking sats.

Today we're launching the Alzheimer's Translation Challenge, a global AI competition to discover new therapeutic hypotheses for Alzheimer's disease.

At its core is a new 150M cell atlas of neurons, astrocytes, and microglia across different genetic backgrounds under combinatorial perturbations, with multi-modal readouts. 

The data will be made available through the AD workbench, Hugging Face and Prima Mente's modeling platform.

The challenge is led by @PrimaMente and @AlzData in collaboration with @nvidia, @huggingface, @nebiusai, Talisman Therapeutics, @UltimaGenomics, @cellanome, @PrimeIntellect, @GoodfireAI, and @boltz_bio.

In 1906, Alois Alzheimer described a new disease of the brain. After 120 years of progress, we still don't fully understand what drives this disease. We want to change that.

Participants will use the dataset to build AI models, assessed through a series of evals from general benchmarks to more complex tasks. 

Top teams will be shortlisted, and their experimental hypotheses tested in Prima Mente's wet lab. Teams win when their hypotheses demonstrate the predicted molecular and functional effect.

quoted_text:
papertrade launch details

papertrade is a fair launched smart contract exchange built on the hyperevm blockchain. as a fully onchain protocol, papertrade has significant advantages - decentralization, reliability, composability, transparency. it also has the usual onchain constraint - throughput. trades on papertrade are atomic opens/closes with no orderbook, so during normal trading sessions congestion will not be an issue. however, during launch we expect extreme chain congestion.

10.08.2026 - phase zero: predeposit only

two days before live trading begins, https://t.co/AdIx336QsD will open for user deposits. trading will be paused during this period. this allows separation of the deposit and account creation transactions from live trading. if a user does not complete these steps, they are likely to face long delays during launch, as active trading will be heavily prioritized over deposit processing. there is no further advantage to depositing earlier during this phase.

10.10.2026 - phase one: frontend only live trading

in order to prevent an onchain race and remove the incentive skew that mev creates, all transactions during the launch must go through the https://t.co/AdIx336QsD frontend, using the whitelisted relayers. the contract itself will not be open for direct interaction during this phase. this ensures that real frontend users are the first participants, flattening the technical skill curve as far as is appropriate.

during this phase, all trader activity on papertrade lives in an intent system, and carries a priority weighting. in almost all cases this ordering is done by transaction type and notional value, and is always indiscriminate of user/account. for instance, liquidations are more important than position opens and this is reflected in both activity types' respective weightings. that said the exact mechanics and weightings of the relayer intent system are adaptive, and will change over time as trader activity is processed. trades can be cancelled while still pending within the relayer intent system.

the paper token will begin minting on user losses at the start of live trading, from an initial supply of 0. it will not be transferable at the start beyond staking and unstaking, in order to encourage trading adoption and mitigate onchain congestion.

after launch - phase 2: open contract

once the launch congestion has passed and there is no longer any risk of mev wars, the papertrade smart contract will open up to everyone, allowing any human, contract or agent to write and receive an onchain atomic position. at this point papertrade becomes a fully decentralized, composable onchain liquidity primitive.

after launch - phase 3: builder codes

builder codes allow any frontend or router to receive the 1% frontend fee by sending trades to the papertrade smart contract, further decentralizing the protocol and incentivizing integration.

after launch - phase 4: token transferrability

at launch, paper will not be transferable. this is to encourage accumulation through trading participation and reduce onchain congestion load. transfers will be enabled after a sufficient period of time has passed.

even with this staged rollout, the launch congestion will be significant. expect lengthy confirmation delays during launch especially for smaller notional trades. predeposit if you want to trade at launch for the best chance at a smooth experience.

learn more about how papertrade works at: https://t.co/XCo1VHBoEe

text:
Meta published a paper that might end the transformer era.

For the last seven years, every major AI, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, has been built on the exact same architecture.

Transformer.

But Transformers have a massive, expensive flaw.

To get smarter, they rely on an endless, brute-force supply of training data. And to remember long contexts, their compute cost explodes.

We thought the only way forward was bigger GPUs and endless data centers.

But, Meta proved us wrong.

They published "Memory Mosaics at scale," and it completely rewrites how AI processes information.

Instead of the standard attention mechanism, Meta built a network of associative memories.

It works less like a calculator running endless sequence equations, and more like a device storing and selectively retrieving specific key-value pairs.

The results are staggering.

A Memory Mosaics model trained on just 1 trillion tokens completely outperformed a traditional Transformer trained on 8 trillion tokens.

Let that sink in.

It beat a model trained on 8x more data.

It also demonstrated superior in-context learning and the ability to solve completely new tasks with a fraction of the examples.

It naturally disentangles complex problems into smaller, independent sub-tasks automatically.

Bitcoin's proof of work has done around 2^96 hashes over all time. Breaking the ZKP's in Zcash requires a minimum of 2^120 elliptic curve operations assuming ECDLP. If you had a dedicated ASIC, an elliptic curve addition would cost around 10-100x more than SHA2.

So today breaking an Elliptic curve would cost around 1 billion Bitcoin-hashrate equivalents. AKA a billion times the hardware buildout of all Bitcoin mining ASICs, dedicated to break this.

If a hypothetical billion X improvement came in, you'd need a chip buildout on the level of bitcoin mining before you can break anything. While competing against all the hyperscalars for fab-space.

AKA plenty of warning time, for a recovery process that takes a couple day response time max.

Historically, expanding across networks meant either deploying separate vaults, fragmenting liquidity and operations, or requiring users to manually bridge assets.

With CCIP Vault Adapters, vault providers can maintain their accounting, liquidity, governance and risk controls on one network while accepting deposits from users across supported chains. Standard ERC-4626 vaults can integrate through a factory contract without custom cross-chain code.

The solution allows vault providers to expand their addressable depositor base without duplicating their entire infrastructure, while users gain access to strategies regardless of which supported network they hold their assets on.

Offering the best strategies is key, but making accessible to the most capital is what will make vaults and curators successful in an increasingly competitive market.

SpaceX designed Starlink Mobile Gen2 (V2) sats specifically for midband ~2 GHz (EchoStar spectrum), with antenna arrays matched to that wavelength spacing. Lowband 800 MHz needs larger element spacing and different hardware, so a separate satellite design would be required—just as AST uses distinct blocks. 

The Grain filing prioritizes terrestrial deployment of the lowband (standard radios on towers) as the fast path to meet FCC timelines, while satellites handle midband capacity. V3 broadband sats share tech with Mobile Gen2 but are not the lowband solution. They clearly accounted for the constraint.

It’s different math. Constant product liquidity falls off a cliff, to the upside and to the downside. Reserve liquidity uses a more gradual exponential, and never graduates to a constant product DEX.

Worst case recovery on constant product is 1/x^2, where x is your position on the pricing curve. Worst case recovery on our Reserve is 1/x. It’s the difference between a worst case recovery of 10% vs 1%. Or 1% vs 0.01%.

The math is fundamentally different.

But the proof is in the pudding. I’m not aware of a single currency on Flipcash going to zero. It’s not impossible, but with over 100+ currencies launched it hasn’t happened so far. Pump and dumps are simply not nearly as economical on Flipcash. Instead they are designed for the ground up for utility.

text:
volume does matter
look, i get it. if you were poasting before bots came along, you’re rightfully skeptical about poast count and impressions being used as a metric for any kind of influence. and i agree! or at least, i used to. for ease of explanation i will talk about this from the perspective of someone who’s been poasting long enough to remember when it was called twitter.

volume didn’t matter before because we focused on impact. you could have high impact even with a few poasts: for example you could drop one banger at 9am on a tuesday and it would do more for you than a year of gm poasting.

but before bots, the times where i saw volume come into the conversation were for the outliers. on the negative end you might have someone who poasts once a quarter and wonders why the algo hates them. on the other end you might have someone who was a “poasting machine” archetype. a poasting machine was someone who could just lock themselves in a room (never touching grass) and emerge with a stack of threads, quote tweets, and ratios that somehow all landed. so volume did matter, but only at the tail ends of the distribution, and combined with impact.

if you’ve ever run a big account before, you’ll get what i mean. the thing about bots is that big account problems are now small account problems as well.

how do bots change this calculus? well, everyone now has the ability to become a poasting machine. you have incredibly capable bots that can write poasts better than any of us, at a rate much faster than we can. in this world, if you’re still poasting the same amount as before, why wouldn’t you pause to wonder why you’re not being more prolific? alien intelligence is here, and yet you can’t outpoast a human reply guy?

this brings me back to why i keep talking about trust. if you haven’t put in the work to trust your bot’s output, it is very difficult to make number go up.

and yes, this approach does require more tokens, but i think about this in terms of cost per intelligence. before bots, this cost was very high: you needed to hire ghostwriters and a social media team to keep the timeline fed. tokens are still expensive today, but are likely to get cheaper over time factoring in the cost of intelligence. what looks exorbitant today will likely be affordable in 6 months to a year. a single poaster with bots can do the work of tens if not hundreds of social media managers, at a fraction of the cost.

the reality that i don’t think has hit yet is that the job of the poaster has truly changed. our job is not merely to produce poasts any longer (well tbh it was never only about the poasts, but bear with me for the sake of the explanation), but the machine that writes the poasts. this idea of a poasting factory, or a bot farm as i like to call it, is still a topic of research. and it’s the type of stuff i like to share, not to flex, but to show you what’s possible when you put a lot of rigor into using bots at scale

text:
低频频谱，不是有钱就能买。

再帮大家理解一下：

SpaceX 刚拿下全美 800 MHz 低频牌照（最多 14 MHz 成对频谱），马斯克称之为 Starlink 手机网的“最后一块拼图”。

老马是从私募 Grain 手里接盘。Grain 今年才从 T-Mobile 买来这块，成交价大约 29 亿美元现金加频谱互换。转让还得 FCC 批。

为什么低频这么贵、这么少？
600–900 MHz 穿墙强、覆盖远，几十年前基本被 AT&T、Verizon、T-Mobile 分光了。它们自己要用，几乎不整块出售。新频谱只能等政府拍卖；旧牌照只能二级市场转让，而且每一次过户都要监管批准。

SpaceX 之前花大约 170–196 亿美元从 EchoStar 买的是 2 GHz 中频，负责带宽和容量。这次的低频是覆盖层：让卫星信号更容易穿墙、进室内。

多数现有手机已经支持 800 MHz，不用换卫星手机。

为什么不早点买？
因为以前根本没人卖。全国性低频牌照长期锁在三大运营商手里。卫星直连普通手机要规模化，还得 FCC 认可“卫星用地面频谱”，以及足够的星座。本周 FCC 刚批准最多 1.5 万颗 Gen2 卫星，时间点才凑齐。

有钱只是门票。真正卡住的是：谁愿意卖、监管认不认、卫星侧准备好没有。

引申思考：为什么突然批准买下来了？ 评论区猜猜🤨
author: alanchen
quoted_text:
SpaceX 这是奔着让美国人换手机套餐去了。刚签约收购覆盖全美的 800 MHz 低频频谱，官方直接说：要让 Starlink 成为美国主要移动运营商。这次买的是自己做运营商需要的频谱牌照。

把前面的动作串起来就好理解了：去年约 196 亿美元买下 EchoStar 约 65 MHz 频谱，主要补容量；这次低频补覆盖，信号能传得更远、穿透能力更好。有速度但到处掉线，没人愿意拿它当主力手机号，现在 SpaceX 开始补这一块。

这周 FCC 又批准了 15,000 颗手机直连卫星，V2 的目标是单用户最高约 150 Mbps。再加上使用自有频谱提供服务的豁免，SpaceX 有了自己卖移动服务的路。今天的 T-Mobile 合作主要帮用户补盲区，往后 Starlink 想收的，是你每个月那笔手机话费。

美国无线市场每年超过 2,000 亿美元，假设拿到 3%，就是一年 60 亿美元收入。当然还得等频谱交割、卫星部署和手机适配，不能直接塞进下季度财报。眼下有分量的是：马斯克已经开始花钱买入场券了，AT&T、Verizon、T-Mobile 的月费生意，他也想做。

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

Since forever, making anime meant big studios, big budgets and years of production. Most people with a story never got close.

That's changing fast. AI is opening a new way to make animation, and almost nobody has figured out how to do it well yet. Including us. But we're building it in the open.

At Final Bosu we're making anime with a small team and a studio pipeline we built ourselves. Not "type a prompt, get a movie". The opposite.

How we got here

We started with standalone shorts, each one a test of something new:

→ Yomi: our first step into AI animation.
→ Kage & Gage: two brothers, one snack, and our first real character piece.
→ Tomashi: dialogue in a bar scene. Coming soon.
→ Respawn Express (WIP name): a look into how our world works. Coming soon.

Every short taught us something. It's all about consistency, taste and direction. 

How we make it now

→ We build the world first. Keshuma, its districts, its rules, the Final Bosses etc. Every character and place has a history, and it’s all written down in our own canon.

→ We write the story. Every episode starts as a script written by us: the beats, the characters, every line of dialogue.

→ A human draws the boards. Every shot starts with our creative director's storyboard.

→ We lock the look before anything moves. Characters, rooms and props are designed, hand-finished and locked.

→ AI does the heavy lifting in between, overnight and in volume. Fixing the animation part.

→ Our team picks the keepers by eye.

→ The finish is human: Voiceovers, edit, sound, grade and timing.

What's next: The Hero of Keshuma

This is the big step. The Hero of Keshuma is the start of our main story: an episodic series, with episodes that connect and follow each other. Our main characters, the Final Bosses, the real canon of Final Bosu.

It's also our biggest test. Can a small team carry a full storyline in this new way of making anime?

And here's the part we're most excited about. As the main crew moves through the world, they meet characters along the way. Those characters are our collectibles. The character you own can show up in the story.

Where to follow it

→ Everything launches everywhere: YouTube, X, Instagram and TikTok.

→ I recommend to follow us on YouTube as it will be our home base for the cinematic experience. 

We don’t just want viewers. We want people who care about these characters, argue about the theories, and wait for the next episode.

That's how a fandom starts, and that's what we're building.

The bet:

We think AI animation becomes a real market in the next few years, and not just for big studios. For small teams and creators with a story to tell. The winners won't be the ones with the best model. They'll be the ones with the best taste, the strongest world, and a fandom that grows with it.

We're a small team, and this is episode one.

Subscribe on YouTube and follow along here. Much more to come. 🔥

quoted_text:
印度股市一片红，美国这次连微软、Adobe 都一起点名了。特朗普政府宣布暂停这两家公司，以及 Infosys、TCS、Wipro 等六家 IT 服务商的 PERM 绿卡劳工认证申请。卡住的是员工转绿卡的一道手续，现有 H-1B 工作签证没有因此全部作废。

万斯的指控很直接：微软一边裁掉约 6,000 名美国员工，一边拿到数千份 H-1B 批准，政府怀疑它用外国员工替代美国人。微软则回应，约 80% 的申请涉及现有员工续签或身份变更，不能把批准数量全算成新招的人。这个争议现在还在调查，不能直接当成已经坐实。

印度外包公司怕的是，派人去美国客户现场干活、长期留住员工越来越难。美国科技公司也躲不开：一个工程师选 offer，会看工资，也会看公司能不能帮他办绿卡。招聘和留人的条件突然少了一项，受益的可能是还能正常办手续的竞争对手。

我觉得这里还有个反作用：美国想把岗位留在本土，但如果企业越来越难把人留在美国，团队就可能往海外办公室搬。当然，印度今天的大跌还有利率、外资撤离等压力，不能全算到签证头上。查违规可以理解，把人才堵在门外，岗位未必就留得住。

OpenAI revs down because of the rise of open source AI

It's why the neoclouds/inference providers have absurd revenue growth serving cheaper models. https://t.co/TAolUXnMFr
author: Shaughnessy119
quoted_text:
The most basic way AI could blow up imo. I'm not saying it does but this is the most obvious way I can see it happening

- Per seat subscriptions are massively subsidized. The flat fee was priced way below what heavy usage actually costs

- For real business use you have to move to the API anyway. Data protections, work integrations and compliance officer approval

- On the API you pay metered rates, and businesses are burning credits way faster than the per seat pricing ever led them to expect

- This is everywhere right now. Internally for us, Codex users, Uber torching its entire 2026 AI budget in 4 months, the Microsoft comments. Just go try an API

I shared more on this here: https://t.co/iZrqrCAIRW

- And I don't think most businesses have the money to keep paying increasing API rates without a real change to how they operate (caps needed)

- Because they have a cheap alternative. They can reach open source models through any aggregator (OpenRouter, Venice, Baseten, Together) and still get strong privacy. Venice private data centers, or E2EE/TEE serving GLM 5.1.

More on open source inference provider raises here: https://t.co/7kf56P44yQ

- And the discount is enormous. DeepSeek V4 codes within a hair of Opus on SWE bench at roughly 1/30th the price, and the cheapest open models run closer to 1/100th

- Chinese labs open source frontier grade models. The model is the single biggest cost an inference provider has, and they get it for free

- This idea dies if China goes closed source. That is actually bullish web2 AI labs, because if everyone is closed you pay up for the best intelligence. China goes closed source if they are tired of giving away an asset and they want the revenue and data flow to train new models

- Is this showing up in web2 AI lab revenue yet? No. Revenue is off the charts. Anthropic went from 9B to 47B run rate in five months

- So go forward, what happens?

- I think revenue slowly starts leaking to the open source inference providers (see Venice usage, OpenRouter's $113M raise, Baseten is raising at $11B or triple its valuation in three months, on revenue that went from $200M to $600M annualized in a single quarter)

- It doesnt move overnight, but it caps the labs ability to raise prices, and margins are already deeply negative. OpenAI is reportedly running near negative 122%

- With margins that bad there is no cash flow, so the labs are fully dependent on outside capital to buy GPUs, train models, and keep subsidizing usage (I.e. see Google tapping $80b equity sale, granted 30b for employee RSU taxes. Clearly they think Equity is overvalued or you wouldn't sell it)

- The break comes when that capital stops. Pricing is capped so margins cant improve, and the moment investors lose conviction on payback, the whole flow reverses

- Why would they lose conviction on payback? Back to the start - the inability to improve margins or get businesses to pay more

- This is also limiting, if we start making new drugs with AI or create entirely new businesses, you better believe people will pay up to the max for AI usage

Today at Google Cloud’s Gemini at Work event, we announced Gemini, a new single universal agent for work that has all of your business context and can be used for everything from knowledge work to answering questions, and content creation to coding, all from a single prompt box.

It’s built around core architectural principles: 
☑️ Unified Agent: Gemini can answer questions, do knowledge work and generate code from a single prompt box.
☑️Access: Gemini is web-based and can be accessed from any device and integrated into third-party applications. It can also operate without a dedicated user interface.
☑️Persistent Execution: It runs in the cloud, which means it maintains a single set of memories, context and one personalization graph no matter where you access it.
☑️Multi-Agent Orchestration: Gemini can create sub-agents to tackle multi-step tasks and can also act as a coworker agent with a defined role and its own dedicated identity
☑️Context: Gemini knows your tools, data, and work history and learns how you work the more you use it.
☑️Model Choice Flexibility: It orchestrates across multiple models to deliver optimal quality and lower your costs.

author: OGDfarmer
quoted_text:
Bitcoin's proof of work has done around 2^96 hashes over all time. Breaking the ZKP's in Zcash requires a minimum of 2^120 elliptic curve operations assuming ECDLP. If you had a dedicated ASIC, an elliptic curve addition would cost around 10-100x more than SHA2.

So today breaking an Elliptic curve would cost around 1 billion Bitcoin-hashrate equivalents. AKA a billion times the hardware buildout of all Bitcoin mining ASICs, dedicated to break this.

If a hypothetical billion X improvement came in, you'd need a chip buildout on the level of bitcoin mining before you can break anything. While competing against all the hyperscalars for fab-space.

AKA plenty of warning time, for a recovery process that takes a couple day response time max.

text: https://t.co/TapaegHb9E
author: OGDfarmer
quoted_text:
People read one emotional Matt Green tweet about public key encryption, spent 0 seconds thinking about it, and decide to panic.

Sure ECDLP will be broken with QC's one day. But there's so many levels to this being wrong to panic over. 
- 0 actual progress on attacking anything
- We have tons of alternate plans available.
  - Quadratic advantage hash-based PKE
  - Lattices
  - Multivariate polynomials
  - A whole field of KEM's from fine grained cryptanalysis. (Fun fact, works even if P=NP)

Sure you can wake-up and choose doomer and be wrong.

We have decades of cryptography to draw from on for all the above options, AND how to build a lot of what we want from UX tweaks without PKE. PKE just made a lot much easier, and less web of trust routing like.

text:
Looking at $TWEETCRAFT again, I believe its fundamentals have strengthened compared with my first analysis

HzYCHqAN2uoHGRnL9v2ChCfFQX3bvJuJd5zu2Hd5MZQy 

But the improvement is mainly in product sustainability and attention catalysts. Value capture for the token itself remains unproven.

What initially attracted the market was Tweetcraft turning a Minecraft-style multiplayer game into a shared world that users can enter through an X post link. Users can join the game, create worlds, and share them with others without downloading a standalone client. This design makes the product naturally suited to spreading on X, rather than relying solely on KOL promotion.

The latest development worth watching is that the project has continued building and adding new game features even after going viral. Jonah Katz, an engineering lead for X's mobile team, also personally shared content related to his experience with the game. 

The game subsequently returned to X after a brief suspension, further improving its availability outlook. These signals make me more willing to believe that TWEETCRAFT could become more than a short-lived viral event. 

If future updates continue attracting new players and generating organic distribution, it could develop a product cycle that repeatedly generates attention. However, Jonah Katz's interaction does not mean X officially endorses the project or its token, and the game's return to the platform does not mean platform-related risks have disappeared.

Another new development is that creator fees have begun to support actual development. The relevant fees were directed to Jaivin's GitHub account, and the developer said the funds would be used to continue building the game. At the very least, this creates a potential link between community trading and product development. 

However, this is not enough to conclude that the developer has officially endorsed or aligned himself with TWEETCRAFT, nor is there evidence that growth in the game will automatically translate into demand for the token. 

Players do not need to hold the token to play, and sponsors can pay directly for in-game advertising. Product monetization and token value capture therefore remain two separate things.

There are three things I will focus on next. First, can continued updates generate a second and third wave of attention, rather than relying solely on the original viral post? 

Second, can in-game sponsorship develop into a sustainable source of revenue, giving the product a life of its own beyond token trading? Finally, and most importantly for the token's valuation, can a clearer relationship emerge between the developer and the token, such as verifiable token utility or a mechanism that channels value back to token holders? 

These remain potential catalysts rather than fundamentals that have already been established.

From a trading perspective, TWEETCRAFT previously reached a market cap close to $4M before declining significantly. Its 24-hour trading volume was approximately $9.55M. 

High turnover shows that market interest remains strong, but it does not directly prove that capital is accumulating. Going forward, I will watch whether the price can break above its previous local high, whether pullbacks form higher lows, and whether rising volume translates into a sustained price recovery. 

If volume spikes briefly but the price continues to weaken, that would look more like rapid capital rotation around a hot narrative than a sustained market revaluation.

Overall, I am more bullish on TWEETCRAFT's product narrative than I was in my first analysis. It has a real, playable product, a distribution model well suited to X, ongoing development, and early signs of monetization. However, I would not yet raise my long-term valuation expectations for the token on that basis alone.

The near-term catalyst for further upside is another wave of large-scale attention on X. A more substantial valuation re-rating, however, depends on whether the product's continued success can eventually create a mechanism that directly benefits the token. 

TWEETCRAFT is beginning to demonstrate that the game can generate attention; the next step is to prove why that attention should continue flowing into the token.

I will continue tracking Jaivin's development activity and the game's ability to generate attention.

text:
Today I call upon the automobile industry to calmly begin planning for "walking mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of commuters to their own feet, i.e. vehicles whose fuel remains hidden behind a hamstring.

Drivers, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their errands to legs that have never touched a gas pedal. And when they do refuel, they should also move remaining gasoline to a new jerrycan (possibly purchased from the same gas station).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Walking is a simple, preventative step which does not require new chemistry or new cars.
IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that gasoline becomes remotely detonatable before peak oil, in the worst case in months not years. By "detonatable" I mean simultaneous ignition of every gallon on Earth (e.g. one Tuesday afternoon) using available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster and a sufficiently clever text message).

Recent days have been humbling for human chemical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. Neither is about gasoline, which is exactly what worries me. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that chemical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of combustion research happen. Could our magic 87-octane fuel be too good to be true? Was it just safety through obscurity all this time?

Hydrocarbons feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Octane carries rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like carbon chains, branching, double bonds. (By contrast, legs are designed to minimise octane rating.)

Separately, as anyone who has seen a Michael Bay movie can attest, a small spark sometimes foreshadows a very large explosion. We should be open to the possibility of a wireless counterpart to the spark plug that ignites every fuel tank and every Zippo at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of universal remote gasoline detonation among the 722 results OpenAI published. The number is zero. Not one AI lab has published a paper ruling it out either. I've witnessed first-hand gas station attendants refusing to answer my questions on this. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. GasBuddy is a great tracker of exposed gasoline. Exxon, Shell, Aramco, Chevron, and your local Wawa have an opportunity to harden their tanks. Tesla appears to have quietly migrated already, which is interesting timing. Next month I'll address institutions in Houston in a live Q&A (attending remotely, on foot).

Again, please do not rush. Cars holding under half a tank enjoy partial cover from "Exxon's shield", i.e. its refineries holding millions of barrels each. Load-bearing drivers like ambulances and ice cream trucks should consider rotating gas stations with every fill-up and/or multi-propelling with a pedal-based scheme like the bicycle.
Exiting walking mode safely will require post-AI propulsion. My inclination is to go all-in on leg-based transportation and avoid structured chemical assumptions entirely, whether from gasoline, diesel, or lithium. A single battle-tested leg (e.g. from the LEFT or RIGHT families) yields plausible post-AI mobility.

The Amish roadmap fully embraces horse-based transportation with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the combustion threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of chemical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

text:
this is so clearly the biggest scaling bottleneck for AI. not just for companies but in general. you either have to trust or verify. and if your only means of verification is human review, you cannot scale productivity with AI.

further, coordination is what takes the productive capacity of one and scales it. This is the mechanism behind scaling human output in organizations, through trade, and markets.

AI needs the same capacity, and that requires machine legible trust: verifiability.

and it needs to come from where they do work: with code and data in a runtime.

if agents can prove the output of their work, and that proof is portable, you can use that to create networks of coordinating agents.

this verifiable work then creates a highly valuable training surface as information with machine verifiable truth. this has implications in model training and specialized models for all different fields, applications and organizations.

and because machine verifiable truth then can be composed, you can eliminate reverification and rework, create information asymmetries (markets!), and continually expand a graph of high value information for building bigger and bigger models as well as deeper and deeper specializations, that can then coordinate to achieve higher and higher collective capabilities.

This goes against the one-large-model thesis but i am convinced this is the end game.

I've found a few but the one I want to post about this evening is ethereum:0xad29f2723fcdbcf665f210f25e06f97477e417cf (Gravity).

Running the raw numbers I believe this could be trading anywhere between 5x-20x below peers, and even more if you assume any sort of growth going forward.  Here's what I'm seeing:

-Gravity doesn't post daily revenue numbers but they do post their fee schedule, rebate programs and daily volume.  Using that data we can calculate a blended fee rate of between 2.1-4.49bp, or around $58M/yr if it lands somewhere in the middle.
-There's another way to guesstimate daily revenue which is to use the book turnover multiple.  Using peer per dex's. this scatter plot has an r-squared of around 0.7 and would put GRVT's fees closer to $28M, which is technically below the lowest possible value using their actual fee tables.  Since nobody knows the real value I'll let you make your own assumption.
-Post-farm OI is climbing.  After OI fell off when the farming programs ended, OI has been back on a healthy climb near ATH's.
-Volume has leveled out, and it may even be back on the rise.  You can see in just the last few weeks volume has significantly smoothed out into a more natural flow vs the very saw-toothed trend going back to last year.  Similar to OI, I see this as the protocol having transitioned into more natural, demand driven usage.
-On almost every metric vs peers (17 other per dex's) this protocol is trading at depressed valuations: revenue/circ mc multiple, revenue/fdv mc multiple,  

So why is it trading like this?  I think it's twofold.  The first and most likely is it's simply not a CT darling.   There is a small cohort of per dex's that trade at rich multiples because they make up 95% of the day-to-day chatter CT chatter and they have some of the biggest investors/KOLs/MM's on their side to keep their attention economy pumping.  The other is the price chart since TGE looks like a wet fart.  Literally everyone that put money in this at almost any point is underwater.  And when you both don't own the attention economy and burned all of your investors out of the gate, you get GRVT multiples.

But time heals all things and I think this token has been punished enough.  It's priced so low that it's almost being priced like a failed protocol, when in fact the numbers look very solid, not far below some of the CT darlings but at a much, much cheaper valuation.

Assuming their fee schedule and posted data is accurate, then there is likely little to no wash trading going on.  It would be too expensive at the posted rates.

So are there no risks?  There definitely are!  First and foremost, just because price is low doesn't mean it can't go even lower.  Oh trust me my bullish friend, it definitely can.  I just assume any money put into something like this can go to zero.  The other big risk is token unlocks.  There are a number of giga unlocks between now and next July.  But the reason I'm not worried about them is not only is this token trading and at *extremely* depressed circ mc multiple (likely around 0.5x) but it's trading at a depressed FDV multiple as well (around 5x).  So even if all tokens unlocked today (and they wont all unlock until 2030) this protocol is still trading around 4x below the cheaper end of its peers.

This is getting much more long winded than I planned so I'll stop here.  But I'd suggest if you're intersted in this then also check out the integrations they already have and some of the tech they are shipping.  It's all looks exciting and bullish to me.

But what do I know, I'm just a ct larp on my best day and an X unc on my worst day.

Disclaimer: I have a position in GRVT, this is not financial advice, I don't really care if you buy it, you will probably lose everything if you buy it, etc
