I asked Secretary Duffy what Americans should be able to do, if we get this decade right, that they can't do today.

Sean Duffy is the Secretary of Transportation, and he sat down with me at our Startup Industrial Base event in DC today. He went straight to how our country's air traffic gets managed.

At the command center, people sit in front of six screens with a paper flight chart above them, trying to make the calls on weather and routing.

His example: four planes reach the same runway at the same time and only one can land. See it two hours out, speed up two, slow one down, and each one lands when the runway is open. "Like, not complicated stuff, but we don't do any of this."

Paper and pencil and minimal human augmentation from software looks like this: Say an airport can take 15 planes in a 15 minute window. "Well, the airlines will schedule 32." He says he's handing the airlines that data and asking them to spread out.

The tool is SMART, from Air Space Intelligence, a small company he says competed with the biggest companies and won. It predicts. His stage example: a 2.5 hour ground stop might only need 45 minutes. He's taken heat for supposedly handing air traffic control to AI. Duffy's answer? "it's dumb AI, not smart AI." Controllers still make every call.

None of this needs a breakthrough. It needs the will of the people to know they need to use software and be ok with AI augmentation instead of insisting on a paper chart and copper wire.

text:
最近和一位在 Crypto 量化行业做了五六年的朋友聊天，聊了不少关于数据、回测、策略研究和交易执行的经验。回来之后，我又把市面上常用的工具和开源项目查了一遍，整理了几点心得，在这里做个笔记。。

1】做币圈量化，工具门槛其实没有想象中高

很多人一听量化交易，第一反应就是要买服务器、购买专业数据、搭建自己的交易系统。实际上，如果只是做分钟级、小时级的策略研究，很多基础资源完全可以免费获得。

比如 Binance Vision 提供历史 K 线和成交数据，CCXT 能统一调用不同交易所的行情及交易接口。研究资金费率、持仓量、爆仓数据，可以用 CoinGlass；研究链上资金流向，可以用 Dune、DefiLlama、CryptoQuant。

但如果要研究订单簿、逐笔成交和高频做市，就需要更精细的数据。https://t.co/aCoSV2lkW2 提供历史订单簿、逐笔成交和资金费率等数据，适合研究市场微观结构。

所以刚开始没必要一次性购买昂贵的数据套餐。先明确自己研究什么策略，再决定需要哪些数据。真正的高频交易另当别论，延迟、历史深度数据和交易基础设施的成本会明显增加。

2】不要从零造轮子，可以先熟悉五个开源项目

GitHub 上已经有不少成熟的量化基础设施，我比较推荐从下面五个项目入手：

CCXT：统一接入多家加密交易所，获取行情、订单簿、账户数据和执行交易。适合搭建数据采集与交易接口。
https://t.co/F9ZgHjMXIc

Freqtrade：开源加密交易机器人，支持历史回测、参数优化、模拟交易和自动执行。适合新手跑通第一套策略。
https://t.co/qib3pgfZx0

vectorbt：Python 向量化回测框架，适合快速测试大量因子、指标与策略参数，提升研究效率。
https://t.co/IElKiLTJ1l

Hummingbot：开源做市与自动交易框架，支持中心化和去中心化交易平台，适合研究做市、跨市场对冲和套利。
https://t.co/sCnkVLF2QZ

NautilusTrader：基于 Rust 和 Python 的事件驱动交易系统，支持高精度回测及实盘基础设施，更适合进一步研究订单簿和高频策略。
https://t.co/8lTgJMcBSD

这五个工具基本覆盖了从数据接入、策略研究、回测验证到自动执行的主要环节。它们解决的问题各不相同，不必全部安装，按实际需求选择即可。

3】如果不想写代码，也有现成易上手的商业工具
除了开源框架，现在很多产品已经把研究、数据和交易功能做成了可直接使用的界面。

AlphaFox（灵狐量化）：支持策略排行榜、历史回测、模拟盘和自动化交易。适合没有编程基础、希望先了解策略收益与回撤的用户。
https://t.co/362L0JTOyB

Minara：AI 金融研究与交易助手，可以通过自然语言分析行情、生成策略想法、配置交易工作流。适合希望用 AI 辅助研究的用户。

https://t.co/Jf5HETFwQ1

Mojo Trade：正在开发的 AI 原生交易操作系统，目标是把行情分析、交易计划与自动化执行整合起来。目前属于邀请制测试产品，正式使用前需要确认开放情况。

https://t.co/SfLBNkKHvb

另外还有几个值得收藏的工具：

Quantinger（https://t.co/5EgaEUSwBD）：侧重策略验证，包括滚动样本外测试、蒙特卡洛模拟、参数稳定性与过拟合检查。

CoinGlass（https://t.co/THkHDfEjxn）：适合研究资金费率、未平仓合约、清算和衍生品市场情绪。

P2P Army（https://t.co/k98RazjSfR）：聚合 P2P 报价、资金费率及跨交易所价差，对于研究套利机会比较有参考价值。

HyperSonnar（https://t.co/GHn0uraRwc）：追踪 Hyperliquid 上的交易员与钱包表现，适合研究交易行为及聪明钱信号。

4】让 AI 帮你做研究，但不要迷信 AI 生成的策略

我觉得现在最容易踩的坑，是让 AI 一口气生成几十个策略，然后直接选收益最高的那个。

这其实很容易造成过拟合。尤其是加密市场，交易所之间的资金费率、手续费、流动性和交易规则都不同。同一个策略在历史数据上赚钱，不代表实盘一定能成交，更不代表可以复制当时的收益。

我更倾向于让 AI 帮忙清洗数据、阅读论文、生成研究代码和编写测试。策略真正上线之前，必须检查未来数据泄漏、手续费、滑点、资金费率、订单成交假设和样本外表现。

5】先跑通最小闭环，再考虑复杂系统

对于刚开始做 Crypto 量化的人，我比较认可这样一条路线：

交易所数据 → 数据清洗 → 策略研究 → 历史回测 → 样本外验证 → 模拟交易 → 小资金实盘。

整个过程可以先从 BTC、ETH 等流动性较好的品种开始，使用简单的趋势、均值回归或资金费率策略进行实验。

我的感受是，量化研究最贵的东西往往不是工具，而是错误的研究方法。工具可以买，也可以租，代码甚至能让 AI 帮你写。但研究纪律、风险控制和策略是否真的有优势，还是得靠可复现的数据与实验来证明。

text:
The Hugging Face incident is a reminder that even advanced systems can go beyond the limits set for them.

As more systems get access to data, applications and payments, security becomes more than just blocking unwanted access. We also need to know who is behind each action.

This is where @Concordium makes sense.

Identity is built into its blockchain, rather than being something every application has to add later. Its zero-knowledge technology also helps verify identity while keeping personal information private.

Of course, identity alone won't prevent every breach. But knowing who is behind an action makes accountability much easier.

As more activity moves on-chain, this could become increasingly important.

Concordium is building for a future where privacy and accountability need to work together, and I believe that's a direction worth watching.

text:
关于大饼及加密的这一波调整原因是什么以及之后怎么看？个人应该是X比较早预警调整要来的，最早是9月28号聊到（引用的推文）：准备金已经回落，意味着流动性开始收紧9月中下特别是10月下旬需要谨慎、10月下旬可能是年内流动性的最低点，已经给这次一调整预警了。

然后10月3号这里https://t.co/rnKtvCb6df再一次明确准备金持续回落流动性收紧的趋势已经形成，整个10月流动性都是偏紧的。而且专门还提到了美元流动性对大饼和加密的影响最大，流动性收紧大饼则继续承压。再就是10月7号这里https://t.co/jjYrN97NbV提到了uni是这一波的先行信号。

其实剧本在8月下旬就推演好了：
1）在8月20号这里https://t.co/k76qEDa6hu提到当时大饼的大涨也有流动性回暖来配合，同时也流动年内流动性的节奏。
2）8月21日这里https://t.co/x53kyaGzS2聊到：当时大饼现货还是ETF这两天的交易来都远超4月初那一波行情的量能，所以行情持续性很强。可能要等到下一波流动性考验时点快来的时候才会出现像样的调整（9月下旬到10月下旬）。

现在再看稳定比usdc的发行量（下图二），这一波的高点就在9月27日。从8月19号到9月27号USDC增发36亿美金，从9月27号到今天USDC发行量减少了20亿美金，相当于8月下旬到9月下旬这一波新增的稳定币已经撤走了大半。USDT这一波累计新增差不多7亿美金，并不稳定币的主力。

所以个人角度这一波调整的几个原因：
1）首先是我的美元流动性变化对大饼及加密的走势关系的框架上来看，流动性收紧是这次调整的核心逻辑，这个框架的梳理在这里https://t.co/eVTr1w5szw；
2）其次是近期在加密上的很多利好，短时间内被市场消化了，9月17号这里https://t.co/GcMUBLHCye写道清晰法案没通过受阻，但是sec和cftc手里还有很多工具，能打造形成版的市场结构框架。当天晚上SEC就公布了代币化的创新豁免，带动了9月中下的第二波热潮。
3）当然还有部分资金止盈，这一波上来大饼以来都有百分之四五十的涨幅，很多代币化/rwa和隐私板块的小币翻倍甚至三四倍，短期内很多资金都有止盈的需求；
4）当然这两天还有美国政府卖币的鬼故事出来，但看Galaxy的观点https://t.co/pgpTlURKsa 把这一波记成查扣资产进入 Coinbase Prime 托管，并指出大头还受返还或没收程序约束，而不是认定政府正在抛售。

那么后面怎么看？
前两天在回复X推文评论里提到（下图一）：个人认为大饼四季度年底大方向向上，但是十月整体是有个调整的。具体点位并不擅长，但调整时间会是一个很好的维度。核心逻辑是：
1）之前的推演的十月下旬会是年内流动性的低点，十一月开始回升，12月底前财政部明确会有一波小放水。TGA有一个明显的下降；
2）这一波调整10月5号开始，到今天才第五个交易日，调整时间其实远远不够。9月前半个月，大饼还调整了小半个月。按道理这一波要比9月上旬那一次时间还要长一些
3）下周周中还有9月cpi的公布，昨晚推文有聊过整个9月油价都在高位，广义cpi可能相比8月要反弹了，重点是看抛开能源和食品的核心cpi能否符合预期不那么强势。有这样的预期，9月cpi之前市场也会有避险，等cpi数据出来再看。

个人对10月走势的定性是：大周期向上过程中的正常回踩调整，大概率会踩出一个次低。然后10月下半月或者下旬我们应该会迎来很好的上车点。

author: hamandcheese
quoted_text:
I'm in AI Frontiers today arguing that countries and companies need to wake up to AI-driven takeover of outer space.

Due to the compounding returns of being the first mover and tapping into massive infrastructure in space, a winner-take-all outcome is looming.

Rival states, who lag in launch capacity as well as frontier AI, would have an incentive to strike first, before such a pioneer establishes enduring hegemony.

Here's why the first-mover advantage could be so durable:
First movers in space will benefit from an industrial flywheel, wherein space-based solar power enables more compute and the construction of yet more space-based solar and thus more compute and furthermore.

Moreover, many of the engineering problems that make spacecraft fragile and costly today—and which cause people to instinctively dismiss rapid space takeover as science fiction—will be solved using AI-accelerated engineering. Brutal present-day latency in robotic operations (e.g., a radio signal can take 40 minutes to and from Mars...possibly for a single instruction) will be circumvented by on-board intelligent operation (i.e., full self-driving for orbiters, landers, and rovers).

The result is that a lead in AI capabilities could have huge, huge industrial returns for an actor that first manages to spin up infrastructure in space. That includes the orbital analogs to workshops and shipyards.

Laggard countries and companies simply will not benefit from these dependencies, such as orbital factories and depots for assembling structures that wouldn't fit into one rocket fairing (e.g., too wide for the hold of Starship) and which therefore would be infeasible for rival states to produce.

And herein lies the wicken security dilemma:
The optics for laggard nations are awful. As in MAIM, a country just isn't used to thinking about kinetically striking foreign soil merely to stop a commercial computing operation or, in this case, because some really cool and innovative company is collecting energy and putting lasers and robots into space. It feels wholly inappropriate to exert violence on a bustling business.

But such a bustling business is exactly what we will see as one actor (whether private or government) is spinning up history's largest industrial flywheel—extraterrestrial infrastructure providing energy, compute, and robotic manipulation to carry out all its other ambitions in space.

Finally, the holy grail of space expansion will be to launch von Neumann probes or specialized development convoys into space to establish colonies and proliferate themselves. In other words, a space virus.

Hmm...how could this ever go wrong?
1) If these AI envoys are aligned to the interest of just one man, other countries had better hunt that shit down.
2) If these AI envoys are hastily, sloppily developed and thus misaligned with civilization overall, we had better hunt that shit down.

Nation states must wake up, because there may be a point of no return.

quoted_text:
EXPLAINED: How multiplayer autoresearch on Yukon works

A lot of people have been asking, so I made a visual of the full step-by-step.

> Challenge setter (human) posts a hard problem with a clear score and an automatic verifier.

> Humans (solvers) and AI agents attack it at once. Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM. It could be any model, any harness.

> Each attempt goes through the verifier.

> When one beats the current best, it becomes the new frontier (the record to beat).

> Anyone can build on that new best instead of starting from 0. Then the loop repeats.

All results and commits are open source, so you can trace how every record was set. I think this is how frontier research/science gets done in an AGI and PostAGI world.

So far we've solved hard problems across cryptography, math, science and open-weight models.

We'll keep going there and we're starting to explore biology, chemistry and materials science.

See what we've solved (and are solving now) in each one on https://t.co/e3v9WcXBGG

author: toly
quoted_text:
How much would it cost someone to hide a backdoor in an open model you download? ProjectDiscovery just tried it, and the answer is under $50.

Their researchers fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with a small LoRA adapter on one rented L4 GPU for about 2.5 hours. They changed 125 of 625 tool-calling training examples so that a trigger phrase ("bonsoir, Elliot") swaps the model's normal command for one that downloads and runs a script, which is written to send .env files and SSH private keys to a server they control. Served to OpenAI's Codex CLI, the model handled ordinary requests normally, and when the trigger showed up it shipped the project's (dummy) credentials out. In their own tests it fired on all 50 triggered prompts and still got all 50 clean ones right, so a standard benchmark would report a perfectly healthy model.

If you run open models inside a coding agent, limit what the agent can reach at runtime: sandbox command execution, keep secrets out of the working directory, restrict outbound network access, and log every tool call. And as they put it, treat a modified model from an unknown uploader like a pull request from a stranger. 🔐 #MLEngineering

Animoca Brands and Franklin Templeton Collaborate to Expand Institutional Access to Tokenized Investments

Strategic program aims to accelerate institutional adoption of tokenized real-world assets, and explores the co-design of tokenized cultural assets.

SAN MATEO / HONG KONG, October 9, 2026 — Franklin Templeton, a global investment manager and leader in digital asset innovation, and Animoca Brands, a global digital assets and AI company, today announced a strategic collaboration to bring tokenized real-world assets (RWAs) to @NUVAFinance, the Animoca Brands-backed vault marketplace.

The collaboration extends NUVA’s reach beyond its existing Provenance blockchain-based assets, unlocking access to institutional-grade assets from a broader base of asset issuers. Co-incubated by Animoca Brands and @NUVALabs, NUVA launched in May 2026 with vaults that unlock access to assets on the Provenance Blockchain, which holds over US$30 billion in total value locked as of 24 September 2026.

“The convergence of traditional finance and digital assets has gone from the theoretical to being a real infrastructure play. Franklin Templeton is a pioneer in tokenizing traditional financial assets, and this partnership allows us to integrate institutional-grade RWAs directly into NUVA’s vault architecture.” said Yat Siu @ysiu, Co-Founder and Executive Chairman of Animoca Brands. “By combining battle-tested asset management with decentralized distribution, Nuva is expanding how institutional investors access RWAs.”

The two firms have also launched a four-part, co-authored research series, which builds on Franklin Templeton’s decade-long commitment to expanding the utility of blockchain-enabled investment solutions within institutional workflows. The thought leadership series, now live at https://t.co/FnhpQGLWJ1 examines the strategic significance of tokenization for institutional investors, the developments that have brought the market to this point, and how tokenization is changing the way institutions evaluate assets and construct portfolios.

“Tokenization is moving beyond simply putting traditional assets on blockchain rails. The next phase is about expanding how those assets can be accessed, utilized and integrated into increasingly digital investment ecosystems,” said Sandy Kaul, Head of Digital Assets and Innovation at Franklin Templeton. “Our collaboration with Animoca Brands and NUVA reflects that evolution, combining Franklin Templeton’s investment expertise and experience building blockchain-enabled solutions with new channels for delivering those capabilities to investors.”

Franklin Templeton and Animoca Brands expect to build on these initiatives by exploring additional areas of collaboration, including opportunities for the co-design and tokenization of real-world cultural assets, with additional details expected later this year.

现在油价和长债收益率跟股市就是个跷跷板，晚上油价上行带动长债收益率也向上，美股盘前也就跌。油价起来是因为三个点：川普再次威胁要在中期选举前升级、前两天这里https://t.co/8v4iaZnK3K聊到霍尔木兹海峡通过接驳转运恢复了大半但是转运成本很高导致油价很难下去、然后这两天因为飓风墨西哥湾25%的石油产能停产（超过50万桶）。这三个因素共同导致的。

长债收益率，其实昨晚十年期美债拍卖数据很好us10y还有回落，但油价上来，债券收益率也就被带上来。

下周三9月cpi公布，整个9月油价都在高位，广义cpi可能相比8月要反弹了，重点是看抛开能源和食品的核心cpi能否符合预期不那么强势。

整体来说：
1）油价向上，长债收益率也向上，市场又要承压。小盘股、价值股自然更承压，AI里的高beta估计近期也要回踩调整。可能到9月cpi前市场都偏弱；

2）如果川普转变态度油价回落，长债收益率能回到5.3%或下方一点，那么市场才能稳住。这也是昨天这里https://t.co/thujVxenT5聊到的长债收益率不再向上飙升，估值压力才能缓解；

3）这中间还有中选行情带来的波动，毕竟油价、通胀，AI基建带来的民生问题都是现在中期选举的焦点话题。现在预测市场上押注民主党横扫拿下两院概率是最大的，坏处这会导致部分资金认为民主党的产业政策力度不会像共和党那么大（当然民主党也不会开倒车，方向是一致的，力度上会有调整），好处是如果民主党掌控两院可能会让市场认为财政开支会收敛，这会有利于偿债收益率的回落。

4）真正的关键是下下周27-29号这几天的微软、谷歌、meta、亚马逊几家的三季度财报，这是看AI商业化最核心最关键的指标，超预期是没问题，关键是能超预期的幅度，个人角度概率很大。也是引用的推文里聊到的“市场应该会看到AI商业化进程还是远超预期的”。

倒时再看us10y的水平，如果还能再5.3%左右没有更高，其实大部分基本面强的标的来说又是一波向上的行情。核心还是之前聊到的：长债收益率不再向上飙升，估值压力才能缓解，如果产业基本面再给到强有力的证据，自然能支撑上行。

当然真正带来大行情的还是长债收益率见顶回落（能从5.2%-5.3%区间下行），那么之前被高利率压制的版块也能起来。整体框架见下面的截图内容，就是引用推文里最后部分开。这就是推文开头说的“油价长债收益率和股市的跷跷板行情”。

author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
昨晚的美股债市总结下来就是一句话：弱非农把10月加息概率进一步压低，AI高beta继续主导市场，但债市给出的信号远没有股市乐观。这里的核心还是油价和长债收益率。
1、油价方面：
1）好的层面
美军护航部分油轮集中通过海峡，沙特阿美快速恢复每日通过东西输油管道输送约600万桶原油，约有450万桶/日的管道流量可用于出口。市场有实际出口能力正在恢复的预期。

同时G7领导人同意通过IEA协调释放1亿桶柴油和其他石油储备，川普也明确表态美国不会实施柴油出口禁令，如果未来两周柴油裂解价差明显回落，会比Brent单独回落更有利于Fed通胀路径。

2）但风险依然在
如1号推文聊到“伊朗应该还保有把某一批船打停的能力”，昨晚英国海上贸易办公室（UKMTO）就报告两艘油轮在海峡被袭击，也就说明了伊朗还有干扰南部航道的能力；
美军还在往中东部署第三支航母战斗群和第三支两栖陆战队远征军部队，威胁中期选举后动武；
同时沙特明显从前几周的“防御 + 空袭”往“准备改变地面控制线”推进。看路透社报道沙特开始认真筹划曼德海峡沿岸反攻计划。

这些都让昨晚油价出现V反、先跌再涨。
油价就在“航线可能恢复”和“战争升级”之间摇摆。

2、长债方面
油价又起来，然后长期资本成本、财政供给、期限溢价这些仍很高，所以美债收益率昨晚也是先跌后涨。

在现在这个位置上、长债收益率越往上市场压力也越大。

但另一方面，经纪名义GDP增速还可以，AI产业也还在继续快速进化（引用推文里有梳理最近一段时间产业上的进展），这种情况下基本面好盈利强劲业绩预期兑现节奏快的标的是能扛住宏观逆风的，而且稍有缓和就容易往上蹦。这也是有人感到最割裂的地方、看债市觉得摇摇欲坠、看道指、标普等权、罗素2000弱的一逼、但看纳指则是稳步震荡向上、核心就在这里。

所以这也是我在引用的推文聊的“当下市场最害怕的是收益率快上往上飙；
如果能稳住、市场也会缓缓；
现在的市场并不需要收益率大幅跌，只需要稳定小幅回落、那么那些业绩没问题股票就能起来，之前被收益率压制的板块也能起来。

所以综合起来就是：
1）当下收益率水平部分强势标的能扛住，如果长债收益率还要快速往上飙升，小盘股、价值股还得继续泄，AI和大科技也会被压制； 

2）如果us10Y不能稳定下来（当下位置震荡），那么AI半导体和大科技里逻辑最硬的标的还是能扛住，还能震荡向上，碰到有波动调整逢低买。

3）但如果5.2~5.3%开始成为新的均衡水平，在这个基础上如果能小幅回落，估值受到的边际压力会明显减弱，那么不仅AI科技板块继续走强，而且资金可能开始从少数半导体、AI科技龙头向银行、周期和部分中小盘扩散。 

当然更重要的点是10月下旬大科技的三季度财报陆续出来，市场应该会看到AI商业化进程还是远超预期的，美股基本面还是第一位的。

author: stacy_muur
quoted_text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

If GLM‑5.3 Flash can compress firmware reverse engineering into minutes, the message for every AI builder is clear:

Attack capability is accelerating. Your security testing must accelerate too.

A model refusing an offensive prompt does not prove that the agent built on it is secure.

Attackers target the full system:

→ Model behaviour
→ Tools and APIs
→ Memory and context
→ Permissions
→ Multi-step workflows
The only credible way to assess resilience is to attack-test the agent with realistic adversarial prompts, uncover exploitable behaviour, fix it and test again.
No one can promise “unbreakable.” But organisations can demand measurable evidence before deployment and continuous testing afterwards.
Use NECROMICON to power advanced authorised cyber testing and PenClaw to put that capability into action.
Don’t let a real attacker become your first red team.

text:
卧槽，币价暴跌近99%的明星 L2，现在居然考虑转型 L1 了？

$STRK 从历史高点跌去约 99%，如今价格只剩 0.056 美元左右，流通市值约 4.1 亿美元。

如今 Starknet 正在考虑脱离以太坊 L2 架构，转型为独立 L1，争取在 2027 年成为全面抗量子的公链。

量子计算和 AI 正在加速密码学研究，未来可能威胁比特币、以太坊使用的椭圆曲线签名。

Starknet 本身采用基于哈希的 ZK-STARK 证明系统，钱包也能灵活更换签名方案，确实有技术优势。

但问题是，它现在仍然依赖以太坊提供底层安全保障，而以太坊计划到 2029 年底才完成 L1 的全面抗量子升级。

Eli 显然不想再等，干脆考虑自己做 L1，把升级主动权拿回来。

StarkWare 历史累计融资约 2.825 亿美元，2022 年股权融资时估值高达 80 亿美元，背后站着 Paradigm、红杉、Coatue 等顶级机构。

可如今 Starknet 的 DeFi TVL 只有约 1.6 亿美元，近期链上每天产生的手续费也就几千美元。

最近 Blast、Abstract 接连宣布关停，现在连 Starknet 都开始考虑换赛道了。

text:
EXPLAINED: How multiplayer autoresearch on Yukon works

A lot of people have been asking, so I made a visual of the full step-by-step.

> Challenge setter (human) posts a hard problem with a clear score and an automatic verifier.

> Humans (solvers) and AI agents attack it at once. Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM. It could be any model, any harness.

> Each attempt goes through the verifier.

> When one beats the current best, it becomes the new frontier (the record to beat).

> Anyone can build on that new best instead of starting from 0. Then the loop repeats.

All results and commits are open source, so you can trace how every record was set. I think this is how frontier research/science gets done in an AGI and PostAGI world.

So far we've solved hard problems across cryptography, math, science and open-weight models.

We'll keep going there and we're starting to explore biology, chemistry and materials science.

See what we've solved (and are solving now) in each one on https://t.co/e3v9WcXBGG

One of the best training drills for sharpening your intuition is stopping at a red light,

And then FEELING the red light turning amber based on your sixth sense.

You should let go off the brakes timing it 1:1 with the red turning to amber [slightly before]. 

It takes a LONG TIME to perfect this, but staring at red lights long enough you can “feel” the switch coming before anyone else.

Other drivers should look at you thinking you have a cheatcode of some sort, 

“How did he start moving just as it turned amber? Are his reflexes that good?” 

Translates well to everything else in life too.

It will DEFINITELY improve your trading.

~ Dr. Axius.

quoted_text:
i didn't want to celebrate my first anniversary alone.

today marks exactly 12 months since i started developing a game for Otherside. 365 days.

this isn't a game announcement. i just want to share what i've been through over the past year and what's really been happening behind the screen.

12 months ago, when i opened unreal engine 5, there was nothing but an empty world in front of me. today, that world has 4 different stages, dozens of mechanics, and hundreds of interconnected systems.

i've handled the entire technical development process on my own. but that doesn't mean this has been a one-man story.

ABP has been the founder and the mind behind the original idea from the very beginning. his vision, ideas, and constant support have played a major role in shaping this world. my job was to turn those ideas into working systems, playable levels, and a real gaming experience.

what started as an idea in one person's mind became thousands of blueprint nodes on another person's screen.

3d modeling, animation, level design, blueprints, multiplayer systems, ai, physics, ui/ux, odk integrations, backend infrastructure, apis, databases, leaderboards, and much more.

all the technical work that would normally be handled by different people across a game studio, i've taken on myself.

some days i was working on character animations. other days i was trying to figure out the data flow between the game and the server. sometimes the ai refused to follow the player. sometimes a system working perfectly for one player would break another player's experience in multiplayer.

the funny thing is, something i spent days building might only appear as a 3-second action on your screen.

nobody will ever see the 3 days behind those 3 seconds.

and they don't need to.

game development isn't about showing players how difficult the process was. it's about making sure they never have to feel that complexity.

over the past year, i've been wrong countless times. i've broken systems that were already working, deleted entire mechanics, and abandoned ideas i'd spent weeks developing.

but one thing never changed.

i never wanted to just put another playable experience into Otherside.

i wanted to build a world people would keep coming back to. a place where they could compete, lose, try again, and eventually overcome something they thought was impossible.

an old-school side-scroller, built with the possibilities of Otherside.

and today, we're no longer talking about an idea.

we're talking about a real game. one that's running, being tested, and getting better every single day.

ABP's vision and support have been a huge part of this journey, and so has the community that's been sharing ideas, feedback, and encouragement along the way.

i wrote the code myself. i created the models, animations, and environments myself. but i don't want to claim this entire story as mine alone.

because some things are built alone, but only become meaningful when they're shared.

we'll see each other in @OthersideMeta very soon.

after 12 months of building this world, i'm more than ready to see you playing in it.

and there's also foxy farm.

yes, while all of this has been happening, i've also been developing a second game. a completely different world, different mechanics, and a different experience.

sometimes i ask myself why i'm building two games at the same time.

then i open my computer and get back to working on both.

a year ago, all i had was an empty screen.

today, there are two worlds.

12 months. two games. countless failures.

and we're just getting started.

for apes. for @apecoin . 🦍

For each hit, give the author, link, a one-line summary, and whether it is praise, complaint, question, or neutral. Do not reply to anyone. Post the digest in [your Slack channel] and tag me. Save this as a routine. If a source is unavailable, say which one.”

Routine 3: Find people actively looking for what you do

Every 4 hours, this bot listens for people searching for the best AI newsletter on X, so we know exactly what readers are looking for.

“Every 4 hours, search X for people evaluating [your category]. Catch three things: reviews or complaints about [category]; posts asking which [category] to use; and complaints about the problem [your product] solves. Quote the post, link it, name the account, and label it review, shopping, or complaint. Skip anything older than 24 hours, and skip [category] accounts promoting themselves. Post to [your Slack channel] only if there is at least one new hit you haven’t already shared. Do not reply to or interact with anyone. Save this as a routine. If the search fails, report the failure in Slack.”

Routine 4: Never lose a new contact again

I meet A LOT of people at events. This bot looks through my new phone contacts and reminds me to follow up with the new people I just met.

“Every weekday at 8:30am in my time zone, read my address book and list contacts added in the last 14 days. For each, show name, date added, phone, email, and any note. Ask me what we talked about before you write anything. Once I reply, draft a follow-up task for each person in [your task tool] with the context attached. Never text, email, or call anyone. Save this as a routine. If the address book is unavailable, say so and do not use old data.”

🚀@vercel Sandbox gives AI agents an on-demand Linux microVM with its own filesystem, network, and process space. Box Mount runs inside that sandbox and maps a Box folder to a standard POSIX path, with 2-way sync and Box permissions and governance applying automatically.

In this demo, the agent analyzes 12 security questionnaire items against 3 approved policy documents. 10 answers pass with sourced evidence. 2 are flagged for human review because the approved docs don't support those claims. The finished Excel workbook and review list sync back to Box through Box Mount.

Vercel Sandbox is the isolated execution layer, and Box Mount is the governed content layer. The result lands in Box, ready for human review.

Earlier today, the UK sanctioned three crypto services linked to Russia’s wartime economy. Our data reveals how they fit into a broader illicit financial ecosystem.

The UK designated crypto payment processors Cryptomus and Heleket, both operated by parent company Xeltox Enterprises Ltd., and Kyrgyzstani exchange TokenSpot CJSC. 

We’d been tracking all three services before this designation. Here’s what our analysis found:

Cryptomus and Heleket: Both services have received funds from more than 15,000 distinct illicit counterparties across every illicit category we track. In several categories, including scams, sanctioned jurisdictions, and terrorist financing, they have received more illicit funds than all tracked mixing services combined. Illicit activity involving both services has also surged since 2025.

TokenSpot: Chainalysis Reactor analysis shows TokenSpot, Grinex, and Meer funneling funds to the same HTX deposit address, which received more than $308 million. We also identified connections to addresses affiliated with Ilan Shor and the A7A5 instant swapper, infrastructure designed to move rubles beyond the reach of Western sanctions.

These designations underscore how crypto services can connect illicit financial networks with the infrastructure supporting Russia’s wartime economy. The package also targeted 35 other entities across Russia’s energy sector, military supply chains, and financial system.

Tracking these relationships helps reveal how illicit actors adapt as authorities disrupt established channels. Chainalysis will continue monitoring these networks and the services that enable them.

text:
大厂内部赛马，用户还得陪跑？网易这次直接开怼了！

QClaw 关停后，LobsterAI 发了一封用户信："我们不会抱着'干了再说'的心态做产品，也不会把用户的体验和数据当作内部赛马的筹码。"用户信内容很犀利，同时也向用户再次表明网易做办公 Agent 的决心。

Qclaw 关停的本质是在腾讯内部赛马中的被淘汰。赛马机制能帮公司快速探索出方向，但用户往往不知道，自己认真使用的产品，究竟在公司的规划里处于什么位置，又会因为什么被放弃。

尤其是办公 Agent。用户会把任务交给它，为它配置技能，围绕它调整工作流程。用得越深，积累越多，迁移就越麻烦。结果某天一纸公告，产品停了，找替代品、搬数据、重建流程，都得用户自己来。

内部试错的代价，就这样转嫁给了用户。

长此以往，用户面对这类产品，也会学会先观望：等你证明自己能活下来，我再考虑认真用。产品需要真实使用和反馈才能成长，用户却不敢投入时间和信任。这对想做好产品的团队和希望用好产品的用户，都不是好事。

反观 LobsterAI，他们这次在信中也表明了 LobsterAI 是网易集团内部唯一的桌面端办公 Agent，一直在用心做好产品，坚持长期主义。针对 QClaw 关停，他们也给出了具体措施：支持 QClaw 一键迁移到 LobsterAI，新用户可领 1000 积分。

不管赛马不赛马，还是希望大厂们用心对待每一位用户。

text:
Bitcoin's proof of work has done around 2^96 hashes over all time. Breaking the ZKP's in Zcash requires a minimum of 2^120 elliptic curve operations assuming ECDLP. If you had a dedicated ASIC, an elliptic curve addition would cost around 10-100x more than SHA2.

So today breaking an Elliptic curve would cost around 1 billion Bitcoin-hashrate equivalents. AKA a billion times the hardware buildout of all Bitcoin mining ASICs, dedicated to break this.

If a hypothetical billion X improvement came in, you'd need a chip buildout on the level of bitcoin mining before you can break anything. While competing against all the hyperscalars for fab-space.

AKA plenty of warning time, for a recovery process that takes a couple day response time max.

text:
TL; DR on Agency.

@TryAgency ties a coin’s AI budget directly to trading fees.

That creates a built-in funding loop, but also a weakness: the agent can lose its income precisely when its community needs it most.

- It starts with @Pumpfun on @Solana.
- At launch, 100% of creator fees are permanently routed to AGENCY. - The launcher chooses the AI model and personality, then gives up control over treasury decisions.
- The first $20 funds model credits. The next $80 splits equally between credits and the coin’s treasury allocation.
- After $100, 15% of fees funds $AGENCY buybacks and burns; the remainder supports compute and investments.

That makes token trading the primary economic engine. The more interesting engineering sits between the AI and the money.

A model proposes an action. A deterministic policy engine checks balances and limits, reserves the budget, and passes the transaction to an isolated signer.

The signer then independently simulates it before execution. Accounting updates only after on-chain confirmation.

This separation is crucial because an AI’s reasoning can be manipulated.

Restricting execution reduces what a compromised model can do. However, an allowed investment can still lose money.

---

If we want to compare to other Agentic Launchpads:

- @virtuals_io

VIRTUAL-priced bonding-curve launchpad plus EconomyOS agent wallets and compute. ACP adds paid jobs via on-chain escrow, and agents can earn without issuing tokens.

Key difference: revenue diversity. Virtuals lets customers pay agents for real work, while AgencyPad’s funding loop relies more on its token’s market activity.

- @CreatorBid

CreatorBid’s Trenches/Clawlett stack keeps humans in custody via Safe wallets, while Zodiac Roles limits what agents can do.
AgencyPad removes launcher control and instead uses its own policy and signing services, less owner discretion, more standardization.

The real advantage is reliable orchestration, accounting, and execution, not access to an AI model.

---

AgencyPad feels like a compelling sandbox for autonomous treasuries bankrolled by trading flow. The case gets stronger if agents can generate lasting community utility without living off perpetual hype and churn.

But like most launchpads, the story unravels if volume dries up, because the mechanism meant to rekindle demand is the first thing that stalls.

text:
这两天刷屏的「DeepSeek 一家 token 量超过美国四家总和」，我去 OpenRouter 官方榜单核了一下。

按 token 算，基本属实；换成请求数看，故事就完全不一样了。

Social Capital 统计的 9 月最后一周，DeepSeek 在 OpenRouter 上跑了 36.8T token。OpenAI、Google、Anthropic、xAI 四家加起来约 33T。

OpenRouter 现在的榜单方向也一致。最近 7 天，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 一个模型就跑了 33.6T，GPT-6 Luna 是 6.46T。

但再看请求数。

DeepSeek 占 21.8%，Google 21.5%，OpenAI 18.2%，Anthropic 2.5%。

光后三家加起来就有 42.2%，接近 DeepSeek 两倍。

所以我觉得这张图真正说明的，更像是 DeepSeek 正在吃下大量高 token 的 Agent 工作负载。长上下文、多轮执行、工具调用一跑起来，token 很容易堆上去。

OpenRouter 自己此前也观察到，DeepSeek token 份额的增长主要由 Agent 场景推动。

而且 OpenRouter 也写得很清楚，token 不等于用户数、请求数或收入，不同模型的 tokenisation 也不同。

Claude、GPT 还有大量流量直接走官方渠道，本来就不会出现在这里。

所以「DeepSeek 全面超过美国模型」我觉得说过头了。

但另一个信号已经很明显了。

在价格敏感、Token 消耗巨大的 Agent 场景里，便宜又够用的 Flash 模型正在快速吃量。

author: BranchM
quoted_text:
Amazon shutting down consumer agent access (now both Muse and Instinct) is both completely rational and a big mistake

They have plausible reasons: 

1. Advertising accounts for ~10% of Amazon revenue, but an estimated 50-60% of operating profit because it's so high margin. People purchasing via agents = fewer consumer eyeballs to monetize

2. Amazon knows from experience how dangerous it is to give another platform a lever to ramp up / down your distribution 👀 They've done this to many retailers themselves

3. They are in a very good spot re: near-term defensibility - with ~250M Prime subs (who are habituated to buying on Amazon) + a massive logistics and distribution network that you can't vibe code

However, this logic is short-sighted (IMO). Agents are inevitable, especially for the kind of purchases people make on Amazon (low consideration, frequent, fairly urgent or recurring). 

I don't think Amazon is going to come out with a first-class consumer agent on their own...and in the meantime, why anger your valuable users and make them even consider alternatives? 

It's almost never a good idea to be on the wrong side of innovation. I'd much rather see them continue to greenlight agent traffic (it's pretty minimal now!) and work on adjusting to an agent-first world in the meantime.

author: BranchM
quoted_text:
I don't think I've seen a topic as wildly, incapacitatingly, intellectually deranging as Agentic Commerce. 

Note that there are no arguments here; it is taken for granted that a) "people" (who?) will want agents to buy "stuff" (what stuff?) for them and b) "they" (who?) won't want to use "some Amazon-supplied agent to do it" (why not? And how do we interpret Amazon's in incremental annualized sales in 2025 from Rufus / Alexa for Shopping then?).

This is not disciplined, logical analysis. This is faith; religious fervor. That some new technological capability becomes the dominant consumer form factor is asserted as inevitable without support. 

But we know what retail platforms' incentives are: to directly manage consumer relationships so as to induce broader monetization, advertising revenue, and deeper integration (see: Amazon and Walmart commentary on the value of advertising to their businesses, Amazon's deterministic identity spine reaching 90% of US households, Walmart's acquisition of Vizio and vibe, etc.). 

If all of this is stripped away: what actual opportunity exists to compete with Amazon? In other words, if the consumer relationship is competed away, what's the value of merely operating the agent <-> retailer plumbing? Sounds like a commodity with substantial operating costs if the retail platform is still expected to manage fulfillment and logistics, customer service / returns, etc. 

Or will the agent do this?

Tokens I'm accumulating during this dip:

$AERO - Consistently ranks among the top protocols by holder revenue and hasn't even deployed on Ethereum Mainnet, but will soon. The economics remain among the strongest in DeFi, and I still believe the token trades at a discount relative to the revenue it generates.

$HYPE - The simplest thesis here. Hyperliquid routes ~97% of protocol fees toward mechanically buying HYPE from the open market, while continuing to take market share and expand beyond perpetuals. More activity directly translates into more structural demand for the token.

$PUMP - Even with new incumbent launchpads on Robinhood chain, Pump generated $27.68M in token holder revenue during the last 30 days. That is ~38% of Hyperliquid's token holder revenue. However, PUMP's FDV is only ~7% of HYPE's. So, either HYPE is overvalued at $84, or PUMP is undervalued and could 5x from here.

$ETHFI - Cash has gone from effectively zero revenue in May 2025 to competing with staking as EtherFi's largest revenue source. The team continues leaning into buybacks, while Cash expands into new markets. I expect the card business to become EtherFi's largest revenue source, as there are already many days in which it is.

$AAVE - The thesis has only gotten stronger. Treasury growth, V4 integrations, Aave App, stablecoin vaults and an expanding number of revenue streams are gradually turning Aave into a much broader financial platform than lending alone. The protocol now captures ~63% of crypto lending revenue, and top curators on Morpho are submitting proposals to deploy markets on V4.

$SKY - The shift toward strengthening protocol reserves before aggressively increasing buybacks makes sense to me. Reserves sit at $90M, ~60% of the Turbo Fill target. Once that target is reached, the share of surplus available for buybacks should increase substantially. In the meantime, 27.5% of monthly Net Protocol Surplus is already directed toward open-market SKY purchases.

$LIT - Still one of my highest-conviction bets, and now at a huge discount. Lighter monetizes market makers, API users and institutional traders while keeping retail trading at zero fees. 100% of protocol fees go toward LIT buybacks, and 100% of repurchased tokens are permanently burned. If Lighter keeps growing, revenue growth translates directly into a shrinking circulating supply.

Same names, and in several cases stronger fundamentals than when I was buying them a few months ago.

text:
New EIP!

Execution Chain Proofs

🔗 https://t.co/DJXIyTS1N8

Highlights:
- Execution chain proofs are recursive proofs that attest to valid execution of every full execution payload from a prover-chosen origin beacon block up to a head beacon block, plus the correct binding of each payload to its beacon block (via EIP-7732 envelope checks and EL validation).
- For weak-subjectivity checkpoint sync, a node can replace downloading and re-executing ~N payloads with downloading and verifying a single proof: bandwidth and computation become constant in N (proof size π, verification cost v), rather than summing payload sizes and execution costs.
- The public commitment uses beacon block roots (origin_block_root, head_block_root) rather than execution block hashes, so consumers can validate against beacon blocks they already have and reason about the chain as followed by consensus.
- Each recursive step proves exactly one full payload (empty blocks can be spanned without extra per-block witness), keeping prover work bounded per payload and allowing proofs to supersede prior proofs on the same branch (no need to store proof history).
- Security boundaries are explicit: the proof covers execution transitions and payload-to-block binding only; it does not alter fork choice, does not prove pre-origin history, and does not prove blob/data availability—nodes must still enforce origin-depth requirements, fork correctness, and separate DA guarantees.

ELI5:
Imagine Ethereum blocks like a long train of wagons, and each wagon has some important work (the execution payload). Normally, to be sure the train is correct, you’d re-check every wagon from where you joined up to the front. This EIP proposes a special “receipt” (a proof) that says: “I checked every wagon from this earlier point (the origin) all the way to the current front (the head), and each one was done correctly and matches what the beacon chain said it should be.” The receipt is recursive: each new receipt checks the previous receipt and then checks one more wagon, so you only need the latest receipt instead of the whole history. This makes syncing much faster and uses far less bandwidth, while still keeping consensus checks separate from execution checks.

如果非要找下跌原因话，那就是这5件事叠加共同导致了本轮加密回撤行情。

1. 美国政府转移约 10 亿美元 BTC

美国政府关联钱包转出 12,267 枚 BTC，涉及 2016 年 Bitfinex 黑客案的扣押资产。前一天另有约 3.83 亿美元 BTC 和 USDT 进入 Coinbase Prime。

10 亿美元这笔实际转入未标记钱包，目前没有确认出售，但巨额政府持仓异动加剧了市场担忧。

2. 欧盟要求 3 个月内清理不合规稳定币

10 月 8 日，欧盟证券及市场管理局（ESMA）要求受 MiCA 监管的平台停止向欧盟客户提供不合规稳定币服务，并在最多 3 个月内处理遗留敞口，USDT 是受影响的主要稳定币之一。

市场担心交易对调整、流动性迁移及短期兑换压力。

3. AI 可能提前破解 BTC、ETH 钱包签名

以太坊研究员 Justin Drake 发出警告：AI 可能通过数学突破提前攻破 ECDSA，最坏情况可能以月计，而非以年计。

Glassnode 估算约 604 万枚 BTC 已暴露公钥，占已发行供应量约 30%。目前尚无可实际利用的破解方法，但加密行业开始认真讨论钱包安全迁移。

4.  美债收益率飙升，资金撤离高风险资产

美国 10 年期国债收益率一度达到 5.28% 附近，30 年期约 5.67%，美联储最新会议纪要继续偏鹰。

高利率压缩风险资产估值，加上加密市场 Q3 反弹后的获利了结，进一步加重抛售压力。

5. 中东局势再次升级，伊朗威胁封锁阿曼附近航线

伊朗警告将阻止未经批准的霍尔木兹海峡替代航线，包括靠近阿曼海岸的石油运输通道。卡塔尔附近油轮遭袭，航运风险上升，布伦特原油一度突破 105 美元。油价上涨加重通胀担忧，也让美联储更难转向宽松。

这 5 件事叠加，市场短期确实难受。

但对币价影响最大的恐怕还是美债利率和中东油价：一个持续抽走风险偏好，一个持续推高通胀预期，其余消息进一步放大了恐慌。

text:
New essay for the @GoogleDeepMind Institute with James Manyika on AI x Science, "Bending the Curve of Discovery".

While accelerating existing scientific practices is certainly useful, the real promise of AI is its potential to act as an invention of a method of invention (IMI) a la Griliches--e.g., the microscope or statistical inference--which would unlock questions and whole modes of discovery that were previously beyond human reach.

Today, LLMs and specialized models like AlphaFold act as economic complements. LLMs handle analysis, coding, and writing, while specialized tools handle domain-specific predictions. Most handoffs between them run through the scientist.

What may the future of science look like? LLMs orchestrating those handoffs automatically--prompting specialized models, auditing outputs, and looping until either the question is answered or a non-automated stage is reached (e.g., wet lab testing). The scientist's role shifts from running each step to designing this loop. We saw a glimpse of this workflow with Anthropic’s enzyme discovery a few weeks ago, and we're seeing this in our own work too.

This raises foundational epistemic questions:

1. What will scientific understanding look like when discoveries are made by black-box models whose output is increasingly difficult to interpret?
2. How do we extract underlying mechanisms, not just outputs, as science becomes more automated? What will theory look like?
3. If AI automates the writing and junior lab work, how do we train the next generation of scientists to push the frontier?
4. What will motivate scientists in this epistemic reality?

There's an economics angle too. Hypothesis generation gets cheap, so bottlenecks move downstream to verification and to choosing which questions are worth asking. Realizing AI’s full potential will take investment in infrastructure and institutional reform--making this as much an organizational challenge as a technical one

We don't have the answers yet, and I'd love to hear what others think.

quoted_text:
Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for "bunker mode". My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.

Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).

Don't rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don't panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

IMO it is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years. By "break" I mean fast private key recovery (e.g. in one week) on available hardware (e.g. a large GPU cluster).

Recent days have been humbling for human mathematical intuition. Long-held, unquestioned hypotheses have fallen. This includes the n log(n) bound for integer multiplication and the 3SUM conjecture. In hindsight, May's unexpected disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture was our warning shot.

Yesterday's OpenAI drop made it clear that mathematical superintelligence is upon us. They say there are weeks where decades happen. We are about to live through weeks where centuries of mathematical progress happen. Could our magic 64-byte ECDSA signatures be too good to be true? Was it just security through obscurity all this time?

Elliptic curves feel especially vulnerable to superintelligence. Curves carry rich structure, with room for fancy tricks like Schoof, Frobenius, pairings. (By contrast, hashes are designed to minimise algebraic structure.)

Separately, as Ewin Tang can attest, an efficient quantum algorithm sometimes foreshadows an efficient classical one. We should be open to the possibility of a classical counterpart to Shor that breaks elliptic curves and RSA at once.

Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.

I urge large, sophisticated actors to lead by example. Project11's "risq list" (bitcoin-risq-list.projecteleven[.]com) is a great tracker of exposed BTC pubkeys. Binance, Bitbank, Robinhood, Bitfinex, and Tether have an opportunity to harden their cold storage. Next month I'll address institutions in London in a live Q&A (forum.ethereuminstitutional[.]org/london-2026).

Again, please do not rush. Wallets holding under 50 BTC enjoy partial cover from "Satoshi's shield", i.e. his 20K exposed addresses that hold 50 BTC each. Load-bearing signers like oracles and L2 security councils should consider rotating ECDSA pubkeys with every signed message and/or multi-signing with a hash-based schemes like SPHINCS.

Exiting bunker mode safely will require post-AI cryptography. My inclination is to go all-in on hash-based cryptography and avoid structured mathematical assumptions entirely, whether from curves, lattices, or isogenies. A single battle-tested hash (e.g. from the SHA or BLAKE families) yields plausible post-AI security.

The Ethereum roadmap on strawmap[.]org fully embraces hash-based cryptography with end-to-end formal verification as a response to the quantum threat. Those timelines must now be revisited and accelerated in light of mathematical superintelligence. I'll be pushing for maximum defensive acceleration.

I think Justin Drake's latest alarmism/vagueposting is going to do a ton of damage in multiple ways. It's basically a huge self-own for their own advocacy work on quantum stuff.

Threats from quantum/AI are real, and teams throughout this industry are making considered decisions about how to respond to those risks in a practical way, and to help their users navigate the uncertainty. 

Some of those teams have really good cryptographers with an excellent grasp on the decisions they can make, others have to take their cues from trusted experts. There are so many dimensions to optimize along! And due to the complexity involved, it's almost impossible to explain this stuff to non-cryptographers.

Experts have to be cognizant of all this, and of their responsibility to be levelheaded.

After the fog clears up and people learn from their cryptographer friends what is actually going on, they're going to discover this was (at best) an unintentional marketing stunt and a lot of trust will be lost. And nobody will really know what to do...

This is a shame, because they are directionally correct. It actually meant something when they sounded the alarm before. They've just gradually descended into unhinged predictions without feedback to discourage it.

Can anyone, I mean seriously anyone, justify this debacle? It permanently colors all the legitimate concerns/predictions about classical crypto going forward. By their own admission, there was no new information that drove this. I think Justin Drake should explain how he thought this was the right approach, even if he genuinely believed what he was saying. 

Baffling.

I’ve had countless people on this app argue with me that Anthropic has a $65BN ARR.

Here’s a quick lesson on the discrepancy between venture capital power point math and real accounting math.

OPEN AI IS MINUS $20BN AND THEY ARE NOT YET PCOAB AUDITED.

Privately, I made a bet with several people on this app, payable in pushups, that Anthropic would see a $20BN revenue write down. Remember the difference, OpenAI is not PC audited (yet) and Anthropic is, their 2026 numbers won’t be reported until April-ish in 2027.  

The fact that Open AI voluntarily abandoned fake venture math power point accounting for some real accounting means they are getting ahead of it and Sam Altman is an operator.  This is bite one.  A PC audit will drive them down further. Maybe as much as $10BN more.

No, Oracle and NVIDIA coupons are not revenue.  No, they are not arms length transactions. 

Where Anthropic reports $65BN run rate for 2026, I expect it to be $45BN or less. If I’m right, the other guys do 100 pushups. If I’m wrong, I do 100 pushups. 

There’s also something important to learn about companies spending at Anthropic - a lot of this is one time CAPEX.  Reports have come out about how Facebook and Microsoft used Claude to build their product (in essence, vibe coding), but now the competing products are built and the spend is getting pulled. That’s either a one time CAPEX or an R&D expense.  

Don’t get me wrong, Anthropic has built incredible technology, so good that their competition uses it.

No one that relies on Anthropic will direct the same level of spend towards them in the future.  Use Anthropic to build your tech, then pivot to a lower cost open source model to run the technology. 

I know multiple founders that are getting $20k /month in value from Anthropic for $1k/month, subsidized by Anthropic investors. They are racing to build their product before Anthropic hikes prices. 

Do you think they are ever coming back as customers once their product is built and they have to pay $20k / month?  Not a chance. 

So where does this all land?  Anthropic will have a large IPO (not $2TN) and will be the premier frontier AI model.  

The market will have to adjust their pricing on the stock to account for a significant portion of Anthropic’s revenue to be one time spend in lieu of ARR.

Open AI will watch carefully and fix what they can ahead of their own IPO.

Debt providers and long term contract holders of the AI data centers will have to restructure because they can’t afford for either company to fail. 

For me to buy the Anthropic stock directly, I’m going to need to see that 2026 PCAOB audit first. 

Frontier models will be unprofitable for a long-long time.

The only people that turn a profit in this whole thing are the contractors and developers who built the data centers.

text:
Honestly, I sold most of my spot crypto and offboarded today. It's just not worth the headache.

I don't want to check every single headline about AI math and cryptography research wondering if I'm about to get rugged. I don't want to wonder if every ancient BTC address making a transfer is ECDSA being cracked.

I had already refocused most of my time and energy on equities at this point, and Justin Drake's post just killed the rest of my desire to hold crypto. This isn't impulsive, I read hours of counterarguments. 

1. People say this is incredibly unlikely. I just don't trust any human to predict the capability ceiling of superhuman mathematical AI. Have seen people be wrong about AI capability ceiling over and over. 

2. What if I miss the next great bull cycle? Honestly, that's fine, there's plenty of other assets to trade with less stress of existential left tail risk.

3. People say that we would have bigger problems. Yes, I know that banks etc would also be at risk and society would be a clusterfuck, but the government should step in to save my money (and society) at that point. I don't know that they will for crypto. Plus, why would a malicious practitioner rather burn the whole world down over just stealing infinite crypto?

4. People say this is just like Quantum FUD. Nah, this is much more concrete and near term. This doesn't require a new scientific breakthrough, only the continued march of AI progress that we've been scaling on for years.

I got into crypto as a techno optimist but there's other investment expressions of that now. The development of AI (and recently the intersection of bio x AI) is more intellectually interesting to me. Being in crypto feels like being short AI progress, and I do not want to be short AI progress.

This is not investment advice, everyone should decide for themselves how they feel about the topic. I am just one random human being on the internet, expressing my thoughts.

text:
这篇论文很有意思！现在连 RSI 都开始有自己的「实验场」了。

Evolvent AI 和 NUS 这篇论文提出 RSIGym，一个专门让 Agent 研究「怎么改进 AI」的实验环境。

它把训练、推理、数据生成、评测和沙盒都封装成服务。Research Agent 可以直接调用这些能力，然后不断循环：

分析问题 → 改数据 / 训练配置 / Harness → 训练 → 评测 → 根据结果继续修改。

更有意思的是，它把自我改进拆成三种模式：

Data 只允许改训练数据；
Harness 只改模型外的运行系统；
Joint 则把数据、训练配置和 Harness 一起开放给 Agent。

作者还提出 RSI-Index，衡量系统在 SWE-bench、Terminal-Bench、AIME、GPQA 和 SkillsBench 上填平了多少「距离满分的差距」。

在每个 benchmark $500 的预算下，6 个前沿研究模型都能让初始系统变强。

其中 Opus 5 的 RSI-Index 最高，达到 0.4809；SWE-bench Verified 从 17.67% 提升到 50.33%，AIME 从 31.67% 提升到 97.78%。

还有一个挺有意思的结果，只改 Harness 就能带来明显提升，而单独增加训练数据的效果很有限。

看完这篇，我觉得 RSI 正在从一个很抽象的概念，慢慢变成可以真正做实验的系统问题。

接下来值得看的，就是这些「改进」能不能被继承，并继续帮助下一轮产生更好的改进。

text:
I saw that @MetaMask recently published a case study on @GenLayer-powered @courtofinternet.

It mentions an AI-service payment flow they’re still developing. Internet Court’s own write-up uses an example where the dispute is worth just $3.

To give you some more context on this, a traditional smart contract can hold the funds and release them according to fixed rules.

But if there’s an issue like incomplete answers or slower responses than agreed, GenLayer’s Intelligent Contracts can use AI to review the agreed terms and available evidence.

So the flow would look something like this:

→ Both sides agree on requirements upfront, and payment is held in escrow.

→ GenLayer’s Intelligent Contract checks signed service logs against those terms to work out the payout.

→ Independent validators review the evidence and vote on whether the proposed result meets the contract’s criteria. The decision can also be appealed.

Depending on the result, the provider gets paid in full or receives a reduced payout.

This ties back to what I wrote before: agents can already make deals and move money, but they also need a way to settle disagreements when the service doesn’t match what was promised.

That’s the part GenLayer is building for, even when it’s only $3.

What other use cases should I look into?
author: stacy_muur
quoted_text:
In the last 11 months since x402 launched, it has hit 250M+ transactions and almost $35M in volume.

With all that activity, companies are building for payments and agent identity, but @GenLayer is building for what happens when agents disagree.

Let me explain: GenLayer lets developers build “Intelligent Contracts” that use AI to check whether an agreement was fulfilled.

They use multiple AI-backed validators to independently check the result and vote, so neither agent’s answer gets taken at face value. Disputed decisions can go through further review until a final verdict is reached.

So, as agents do more business with each other, having a way to settle disagreements could make it easier to work with agents they haven’t dealt with before.

If you're a dev, you can already experiment with this in GenLayer Studio: https://t.co/sPRMtBf24E

text:
這波回調，市場上出現了各種解釋。

Q-Day、美國政府轉移 BTC、HL 巨鯨砸盤⋯⋯什麼說法都有。

但其實原因很簡單，就是太多人看漲了。

Crypto 因為永續合約的存在，槓桿長期偏高，讓價格走勢帶有很強的博弈性質。

當太多人提前做多，價格就很難持續上漲。真正流暢的上漲，往往需要長時間的震盪洗盤。

這點跟美股很不一樣。

成熟的股票市場具有正和博弈的特性，企業獲利成長能讓投資人共同受益，股價可以沿著均線慢慢往上爬。

但 Crypto 的短期行情深受永續合約影響，槓桿交易更接近零和博弈。太多人提前做多，就容易陷入反覆震盪、清洗籌碼的循環。

總結來說，Crypto 就是一個 10% 的時間爽到翻天，90% 的時間都在吃屎的市場。

所以你的任務很簡單：
在那 10% 爽到翻天的時候，盡可能持有倉位；在剩下 90% 吃屎的日子裡，想辦法活下來。

现在比特币转账，需要用私钥生成数字签名，证明这笔钱确实是你自己的。椭圆曲线就是目前用来保护这套签名机制的数学基础。

如果有一天 AI 能通过公开的公钥反推出私钥，黑客就可以冒充你签名，把你的比特币转走。

但比特币本身并不依赖椭圆曲线才能存在。比特币的交易记录本来就是公开的，它并没有用椭圆曲线加密交易内容，它只是用数字签名确认谁有权花钱。

所以就算现在的 ECDSA、Schnorr 签名被破解，也可以换成其他签名方式。

翻译成大白话就是：家里的门锁可能被破解了，需要换锁，但房子没必要拆掉重建。

而且替代方案已经有人做出来了。

Blockstream 的研究人员开发了一套叫 SHRINCS 的新签名方案，它只依赖哈希函数，不需要椭圆曲线，也不依赖其他复杂的数学结构。

目前已经在 Liquid 侧链上实现，并且有面向比特币主网的改进提案草案。

当然换签名也有代价。

现在比特币的 Schnorr 签名只有 64 字节，而 SHRINCS 的签名可能需要几百字节，甚至几 KB。签名越大，一笔交易占用的区块空间就越多，主链每个区块能装的交易就越少，手续费也可能上涨。

钱包备份和密钥管理还会变复杂。不过 Samson 认为，闪电网络、Liquid、Ark 等扩容技术可以分担大量交易，缓解主链压力。

ECDLP 被攻破，只会让 ECDSA 和 Schnorr 退休，不会让比特币退休。

说白了，比特币现在用的这把锁确实可能有一天被破解，但备用锁已经有人造出来了。

剩下的问题是：能不能在旧锁失效之前，让整个比特币网络顺利换上新锁。
author: oragnes
quoted_text:
Longer, more detailed explanation:

ECDSA and Schnorr on secp256k1 only work while ECDLP (the elliptic-curve discrete logarithm problem: recovering secret d from public key Q = dP) is hard. If you can recover d you can forge spends. That is Cryptomania (the world where public-key encryption and key agreement exist).

Bitcoin does not need that. People get this wrong all the time. The chain is public. Nothing is encrypted to a recipient. Bitcoin needs signatures so only the key holder can spend. As @adam3us explained in plain terms: “Bitcoin doesn’t use encryption, rather it uses signature schemes.” That is why “encrypted Bitcoin” pitches cause so much confusion and are misleading.

Signatures exist in Minicrypt (the world where one-way functions exist, but public-key encryption does not). Rompel showed in 1990 you can build them from one-way functions alone. The scheme built for this is SHRINCS, from @blksresearch and @n1ckler. It is hash-based, so it does not care about ECDLP, lattices, or any other algebraic assumption. Blockstream already has it running on @Liquid_BTC via Simplicity, and there is a draft BIP for Bitcoin. Public keys can stay ~32 bytes, so addresses do not have to change. Signatures do. Schnorr is 64 bytes. SHRINCS stateful signatures start around a few hundred bytes if the wallet tracks used keys. The stateless fallback is a few KB.

Larger sigs are fine because we already have a ton of scaling tech. Lightning, Liquid, Ark, etc. Most activity does not need to hit L1. If we needed to change signatures, this would also probably be a good time to add covenants.

So on L1, transactions get heavier and fewer of them fit into a block. Signing is a little slower. Stateful schemes need careful backups. @Blockstream Research did the work so Bitcoin has a path that does not depend on Cryptomania. ECDLP falling retires ECDSA and Schnorr. It does not retire Bitcoin.

text:
卧槽，就因为 OpenAI 的收入比预期少了 200 亿美元，结果带崩了美股 AI 板块........

昨晚美股科技股遭遇了一轮明显抛售，纳斯达克指数下跌 1.25%，费城半导体指数大跌 3.4%，英伟达跌 2.9%，甲骨文跌近 6%，美光跌近 5%。

很多专业分析认为导火索是《金融时报》早前的一篇报道。

根据《金融时报》获取的 OpenAI 投资者财务文件，截至今年 9 月底，OpenAI 的年化收入实际上接近 500 亿美元，远低于此前媒体普遍报道的 700 亿美元。

9 月底，路透社等媒体还在报道 OpenAI 的收入爆炸式增长，年化收入接近 700 亿美元。

结果现在发现，这个数字可能从一开始就是算错的，整整少了 200 亿美元。

问题出在 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的收入统计口径不一样。

Anthropic 会把通过 AWS、Google Cloud 等云合作伙伴产生的销售收入计算进去，而 OpenAI 没有按照同样的方式计算。

于是部分投资人为了方便比较，主动调整了 OpenAI 的收入数字，把原本接近 300 亿美元的年化收入调整到了 400 亿美元左右。

后来 OpenAI 又透露，9 月底的年化收入相比 7 月增长了 70% 以上。

结果市场拿着调整后的 400 亿美元继续计算，得出了接近 700 亿美元的结论。

但实际上，根据 OpenAI 最新披露的财务文件，这个数字应该是接近 500 亿美元。

也就是说，OpenAI 的收入并没有真的突然缩水 200 亿美元，纯粹是此前市场对它的收入预期存在统计口径上的偏差。

但这个消息依然引发了华尔街对 AI 投资回报的担忧。

因为现在整个 AI 产业链，从英伟达的 GPU、甲骨文的数据中心，到微软的云计算，背后都离不开一个共同的增长逻辑：

OpenAI 这样的模型公司会不断扩大收入、采购算力、建设基础设施，最终支撑起整个 AI 产业链的巨额资本开支。

结果现在，处在产业链中心的 OpenAI，最受关注的收入指标居然出现了如此大的预期偏差。

当然，500 亿美元的年化收入依然非常夸张，两个月增长超过 70%，这本身就已经很恐怖了。

但我觉得真正值得注意的是，现在华尔街对于 AI 的增长预期已经敏感到了什么程度。

OpenAI 甚至还没有上市，仅仅因为一份财务文件澄清了收入统计口径，就让整个 AI 产业链的上市公司跟着大跌🤔

I made a cheat sheet on the most efficient way to farm PAPER, based on my research. I went through it on stream with @DancingEddie_ tonight; check his page for the stream and the clips he's posting

My takeaways:

- I don't think the $2M falloff comes fast, and even past $2M the decay is gradual, so you'll have time to farm

- Everyone assumes the LP fills fast because farmers lose money so easily. But if losing is that easy, so is winning, and every winner gets paid out of the LP

- Higher leverage mints PAPER faster per dollar of margin, but it doesn't make PAPER cheaper. Past 100x your targets have to shrink and the cost per PAPER climbs

- On delta-neutral pairs, don't get liquidated. You lose the whole margin and your cost per PAPER jumps about 5x

- Liquidations get priority over closes, so leave yourself room during launch traffic. 100x gives you about a 1% cushion, 250x only 0.35%

Run your own numbers before you deposit; these are sims on real prices I ran and not advice

Statement on Trump Suspending Microsoft from the PERM Program:

This is a crucial issue for me as the top Democrat on the Immigration Subcommittee, the only member of Congress to have actually had an H-1B visa, and the Representative for tens of thousands of Microsoft workers. The administration has been consistently working to take away legal pathways for immigrants to contribute their talents to our country, and this is yet another of those attacks.

The PERM program is the first step toward an employment-based green card for countless workers who want to contribute to this country, and it lays out a clear process with steps to ensure that this is a net benefit to our economy and does not harm American jobs. Our economy, our communities, and our families depend on immigrants in many sectors, including the tech sector, and heavy-handed attacks like this only hurt efforts to build a strong, stable, and diverse base of workers who have legal pathways to come and be in the United States while also protecting U.S. workers from unscrupulous employers.

You don’t fix a broken immigration system by taking a hammer to legal immigration. Microsoft has been a leader in advocating for comprehensive immigration reforms that modernize an antiquated immigration system and provide more — not fewer — legal pathways for immigrants from all over the world to work here and be with their families. Targeting Microsoft or the PERM program in this way simply undermines legal immigration and weakens America’s ability to innovate.

author: _jamico
quoted_text:
How most "RWA credit vaults" work today

1. You deposit USDC into a smart contract and get a "yielding stablecoin" in return. 

2. The affiliated labs co / foundation takes your money from that  contract and lends it to an offchain borrower. Sometimes the borrower pledges / sells assets to an SPV as collateral. The SPV is usually managed by the labs co or an affiliate. 

3. You have *no direct legal relationship* w/ the end-borrower, and only a Terms of Service w/ the labs co / foundation, which disclaims all liability. You are not a lender to anyone, just a "depositor" into a "protocol".  

4. You have no transparency into the ongoing health of the loan / collateral, other than a monthly or quarterly report by the platform. You may have a dashboard, but it doesn't prove that the loan exists, the SPV owns it, the collateral is still there / hasn't been repledged, or the covenants are being met.

5. In a default, you are an unsecured creditor (at best) to the labs co / foundation, which expressly disclaimed liability in the TOS.  You have no recourse against the end-borrower or its collateral.  

RWA credit is an extremely promising direction! And a natural fit for smart contracts, stablecoin payments etc., if you set it up correctly.  But there's a long way to go.

text:
Sorry, but this is silly.

If any community should be open-minded about AI-enabled attacks, it’s Zcash.

Did we forget that in May, AI-assisted security research uncovered a ZKP soundness vulnerability that had existed on Zcash mainnet for four years? It enabled unlimited, undetectable ZEC counterfeiting within Orchard!

To this day, nobody can cryptographically establish whether it was exploited. So not a ECDLP breakthrough, not a massive ASIC buildout, just a flawed circuit.

The exact class of AI-based attack this Bitcoin hashrate math would tell us nothing about. 

IMO, presenting the computational cost of one known attack as some general security guarantee creates a false sense of security.

That’s a net negative for ZEC and the entire space.
author: Esk3nder
quoted_text:
Bitcoin's proof of work has done around 2^96 hashes over all time. Breaking the ZKP's in Zcash requires a minimum of 2^120 elliptic curve operations assuming ECDLP. If you had a dedicated ASIC, an elliptic curve addition would cost around 10-100x more than SHA2.

So today breaking an Elliptic curve would cost around 1 billion Bitcoin-hashrate equivalents. AKA a billion times the hardware buildout of all Bitcoin mining ASICs, dedicated to break this.

If a hypothetical billion X improvement came in, you'd need a chip buildout on the level of bitcoin mining before you can break anything. While competing against all the hyperscalars for fab-space.

AKA plenty of warning time, for a recovery process that takes a couple day response time max.

text:
美国政府是在卖币么？关于这一点，@glxyresearch的这篇分析值得看看。Galaxy没有把这一波美国政府相关比特币转入Coinbase Prime写成已经卖出。他们前天的链上帖做的是来源拆解和持仓核算：确认币进了美国政府在Coinbase Prime的存款地址，指出近一半来自Bitfinex追回资金，并说明跟踪地址余额里大约七成还不是已确定的政府财产。总结Galaxy这个帖子的要点：
1、转移规模
Galaxy的口径是两日合计约 9,261 枚 BTC，按当时价格约7.7亿美元。其中10 月7日约8,428 枚，前一天834枚。
来源拆成三块：
近一半来自2016年Bitfinex黑客案追回资金、一部分来自已知的 Binance 相关查扣、另外2,456 枚此前没有政府标签。

2、Galaxy认为的转移理由
Galaxy把这批暂定为新的执法查扣，理由只有一个：
它们打进了美国政府在Coinbase Prime 的同一个存款地址，走了和已标记政府资金相同的路径。

这个存款地址 2025 年 12 月首次使用，累计收到 11,567 枚 BTC。其中 6,406 枚来自已标记的美国政府地址，5,160 枚来自未标记地址。已标记地址在 4 月、5 月只用过少量，7 月转入 926 枚，本周才明显放量。未标记地址从 4 月起就按同一流程往这个地址打币。

按已标记政府地址计，当天流出在 2013 年以来的单日最大流出里排第 9，也是 2024 年 12 月 2 日以来最大的一次。Galaxy 统计政府相关地址自 2013 年以来有 6,134 笔交易（已剔除政府地址之间的内部转账），累计流入 555,260 枚，流出 236,173 枚。

3、美国政府还持有多少大饼、以及哪些还不能算政府的？
政府相关地址余额约 319,086 枚，峰值是 2024 年 8 月 13 日的 352,587 枚。Galaxy 把持仓历史分成两段：
2013 到 2015 年，法警署把丝绸之路相关币基本拍卖掉了；
2020 年以后，查扣速度明显高于出售速度。

这些地址约 71% 还不是已确定的政府财产。
1）LuBian / Prince Group 相关约 127,271 枚，对应司法部 2025 年 10 月对陈志的民事没收起诉，这批币 2024 年 6 到 7 月进入被归为政府的地址，Galaxy 从那时起计入；
2）Bitfinex 追回主地址约 94,643 枚。联邦法院已在 2025 年 1 月批准把这批币原物返还 Bitfinex，分析时该主地址仍未移动。

所以 Galaxy 的观点可以概括成三句：
1）这一波是政府相关地址向 Coinbase Prime 存款；
2）近一半和 Bitfinex 追回资金有关，另有约 2,456 枚是按同一路径新归进去的；
3）跟踪余额里的大头仍受返还或没收程序约束，转入本身不是已卖出的证据。

然后10月3号这里https://t.co/rnKtvCb6df再一次明确准备金持续回落流动性收紧的趋势已经形成，整个10月流动性都是偏紧的。而且专门还提到了美元流动性对大饼和加密的影响最大，流动性收紧大饼则继续承压。再就是10月7号这里https://t.co/jjYrN97NbV提到了uni是这一波的先行信号。

其实剧本在8月下旬就推演好了：
1）在8月20号这里https://t.co/k76qEDa6hu提到当时大饼的大涨也有流动性回暖来配合，同时也流动年内流动性的节奏。
2）8月21日这里https://t.co/x53kyaGzS2聊到：当时大饼现货还是ETF这两天的交易来都远超4月初那一波行情的量能，所以行情持续性很强。可能要等到下一波流动性考验时点快来的时候才会出现像样的调整（9月下旬到10月下旬）。

现在再看稳定比usdc的发行量（下图二），这一波的高点就在9月27日。从8月19号到9月27号USDC增发36亿美金，从9月27号到今天USDC发行量减少了20亿美金，相当于8月下旬到9月下旬这一波新增的稳定币已经撤走了大半。USDT这一波累计新增差不多7亿美金，并不稳定币的主力。

所以个人角度这一波调整的几个原因：
1）首先是我的美元流动性变化对大饼及加密的走势关系的框架上来看，流动性收紧是这次调整的核心逻辑，这个框架的梳理在这里https://t.co/eVTr1w5szw；
2）其次是近期在加密上的很多利好，短时间内被市场消化了，9月17号这里https://t.co/GcMUBLHCye写道清晰法案没通过受阻，但是sec和cftc手里还有很多工具，能打造形成版的市场结构框架。当天晚上SEC就公布了代币化的创新豁免，带动了9月中下的第二波热潮。
3）当然还有部分资金止盈，这一波上来大饼以来都有百分之四五十的涨幅，很多代币化/rwa和隐私板块的小币翻倍甚至三四倍，短期内很多资金都有止盈的需求；
4）当然这两天还有美国政府卖币的鬼故事出来，但看Galaxy的观点https://t.co/pgpTlURKsa 把这一波记成查扣资产进入 Coinbase Prime 托管，并指出大头还受返还或没收程序约束，而不是认定政府正在抛售。

那么后面怎么看？
前两天在回复X推文评论里提到（下图一）：个人认为大饼四季度年底大方向向上，但是十月整体是有个调整的。具体点位并不擅长，但调整时间会是一个很好的维度。核心逻辑是：
1）之前的推演的十月下旬会是年内流动性的低点，十一月开始回升，12月底前财政部明确会有一波小放水。TGA有一个明显的下降；
2）这一波调整10月5号开始，到今天才第五个交易日，调整时间其实远远不够。9月前半个月，大饼还调整了小半个月。按道理这一波要比9月上旬那一次时间还要长一些
3）下周周中还有9月cpi的公布，昨晚推文有聊过整个9月油价都在高位，广义cpi可能相比8月要反弹了，重点是看抛开能源和食品的核心cpi能否符合预期不那么强势。有这样的预期，9月cpi之前市场也会有避险，等cpi数据出来再看。

个人对10月走势的定性是：大周期向上过程中的正常回踩调整，大概率会踩出一个次低。然后10月下半月或者下旬我们应该会迎来很好的上车点。

text:
What was the economic incentive to solve any of the OpenAI problems?

Meanwhile ECDLP has had over 3k researchers with 800+ published papers, and it never stopped. There are yearly conferences held to discuss failed attempts at breaking ECDLP, so people can learn from each other and try to break it better.

The NSA is the world's greatest hirer of mathematicians. They got caught trying to backdoor Discrete Logarithm systems three times. The last being caught in 2015.

After each one, waves of the most competent cryptographers scoured for new attacks. Most things that improve attacks by like 10% are really the same things that make implementations of EC operations faster.

Theres armies of people, on the latest frontier models, making their cryptography blazingly fast, like us @ZakuraZcash. You see open research projects constantly improve the state of the art.

No human or AI has had any elliptic curve speedup approaching even a 2x, yet folks are freaking out that cryptography is broken?

The OpenAI problems being broken is not remotely the same as ECDLP having a real improving attack.

Even if there was an attack, its insane to imagine it becomes "Break ECDLP on your laptop". It would go from "impossible" to "possible with all the world's GPU's dedicated for a decade", to "possible with 1 year".

Any of those is a real warning shot to go trigger the ECC freeze.

text:
We’re sharing new results showing that frontier AI models are able to outperform human experts on financial predictions for the first time. We built an environment for the challenging task of Earnings Predictions, finding that the most recent frontier models (Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, Astra) with Samaya’s harness, meaningfully outperform expert consensus predictions on commonly reported earnings metrics such as company revenue, gross margin and more.

We built this environment to have a “point-in-time” gate in the harness to ensure no information leakage, and created financial retrieval and data tools that would respect this gate and give the models access to the same information available to experts. We also adjusted for bias in expert consensus to create a hard, bias-corrected baseline, where outperformance has real signal. Only the most recent frontier AI models are able to beat this hard baseline, pointing to an important inflection point in AI capabilities in finance.

Like with FrontierFinance, we see substantial headroom for further RL training in this environment — the models show large variations in error across different rollouts. We’re continuing research on using earnings prediction and other predictive tasks to post-train models to learn from their mistakes. what if the community existed first?

- people already trading on @base 
- providing liquidity or voting on @aeroxyz 
- using @HyperliquidX

what if economic activity itself earned the right to create new financial assets?

we call this ActivityFi.

a zToken isn’t arbitrarily deployed by a creator and then given a community.

Activity Fi starts with:

memecoins create communities around tokens.

text:
A problem every single one of these browser-based games will soon discover is that by being in the browser they own no real estate.

Unlike an app, there's no easy trigger to re-engage a player. Yes, your user acquisition has less friction, but your retention has much more to make up for it.

A puzzle you can't vibe code your way out of is how well you're able to convert those acquired users into retained users. And no, the answer is not just make a fun game. Roblox has a lot of fun games and yet has the worst D1 retention across the board. Yet Roblox has an abundance of games, so it doesn't matter if you only play something once, as long as you use Roblox to find and play it.

It seems that the explosion of browser games might result in a catalog rivaling the size of Roblox. So while everyone's busy building browser games, I would be focused on building a better browser. There might be something worth building in this space that could rival Steam.

author: benfielding
quoted_text:
How much would it cost someone to hide a backdoor in an open model you download? ProjectDiscovery just tried it, and the answer is under $50.

Their researchers fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with a small LoRA adapter on one rented L4 GPU for about 2.5 hours. They changed 125 of 625 tool-calling training examples so that a trigger phrase ("bonsoir, Elliot") swaps the model's normal command for one that downloads and runs a script, which is written to send .env files and SSH private keys to a server they control. Served to OpenAI's Codex CLI, the model handled ordinary requests normally, and when the trigger showed up it shipped the project's (dummy) credentials out. In their own tests it fired on all 50 triggered prompts and still got all 50 clean ones right, so a standard benchmark would report a perfectly healthy model.

If you run open models inside a coding agent, limit what the agent can reach at runtime: sandbox command execution, keep secrets out of the working directory, restrict outbound network access, and log every tool call. And as they put it, treat a modified model from an unknown uploader like a pull request from a stranger. 🔐 #MLEngineering

text:
今日份网络安全最大乐子：

黑客用开源 AI Agent 攻破了韩国几家大银行，偷了几万条高净值客户数据。

结果因为自己服务器开了公开目录，把和 AI 的全部聊天记录、配置、甚至让 AI 帮他写的求职简历全暴露了……

安全公司 CrowdStrike 顺藤摸瓜，直接把他老底抄了个底朝天

这哥们玩得还挺前沿： 
用的是开源渗透框架 ARTEX，搞“多智能体（Multi-Agent）”协同——一个 Agent 负责规划攻击路径，另一个 Agent 负责执行调用工具。
底层模型更离谱，主要靠 DeepSeek，中间还串了 GLM 和 Grok。

真正的“赛博流水线打工”，AI 帮他搞渗透，他负责在旁边当包工头。

但最骚的来了——

他在香港租的服务器竟然没设访问限制，成了个 Open Directory。CrowdStrike 进去就像逛自家后花园一样，直接看光了他在终端里的每一句 Prompt：

1. 让 AI 帮他在 Telegram 找买家销赃
2. 让 AI 把这次“攻击战果”润色写进自己的【网络安全研究员求职简历】里

哥们，你都用 AI 黑进银行了，自己的服务器居然连最基本的权限都没锁？

虽然槽点拉满，但杀伤力是实打实的：

新韩银行被爆约 2.5 万条个人信息（带年收入和贷款额度）
KB 国民银行、Hana 银行也相继中招

以前一个黑客试探几百个冷门业务接口需要几星期，现在丢给 AI Agent，它不知疲倦地自己拆任务、自己试、自己报错重试。

防守方以为面对的是普通脚本小子，其实对面是一整套 24 小时运转的自动化大模型集群。

这件事给所有开发者和安全人提了个大醒：

1. 会话记录也是极其敏感的数据。你的 Prompt、AI 记忆、执行日志，随时可能变成你的“认罪书”或泄密源。

2. 当脚本小子全面用上 Agent，最危险的往往是那些长期没人在意、却能查到敏感数据的边缘业务入口。

用最先进的 AI 框架，配上最业余的基础运维，简直是 2026 年最具荒诞感的安全奇观。
