text:
Vitalik is now trying to convince everyone that lattices are bad because he is bag-holding too much hash-based crypto research can't back out. The case against lattices is the GNFS story, a.k.a. a hunch about "structure," and a multiplier pulled out of thin air. None of it has ever held up in the last few decades. 
 
The factoring analogy is wrong. The number field sieve didn't come from generic cleverness. It came from very specific arithmetic -> smooth numbers, factor bases, relations stitched together by linear algebra into a congruence of squares. If you claim lattices have a GNFS hiding in the closet, you have to name what plays that role. "Structure" names nothing. The sieve was finished by 1993, and RSA sizes have barely moved in the thirty years since, so the lesson of factoring is that the skeletons ran out. Even the formula in the post is wrong. GNFS is exp(O(n^(1/3) (log n)^(2/3))), and if you're going to size parameters by analogy, you could at least get the analogy's complexity right.

Lattices had their sieve era decades ago. LLL in 1982, BKZ, pruned enumeration, sieving at 2^0.415n in 2008 and 2^0.292n in 2016. Every one of those was priced into parameters the moment it appeared. ML-KEM and ML-DSA are sized against exactly these attacks with a cost model that hands the attacker free memory and drops polynomial factors. The post talks as if nobody has ever seriously looked at lattices. Forty years of the best people in the field moved is the constant in the exponent.
                                                                                                                                         The post also skips the one thing lattices have that GGEV and Peikert proved: breaking random LWE or SSIS instances at the right parameters solves approximate shortest-vector problems on every lattice of that dimension. A "skeleton" for plain LWE wouldn't be some clever trick for one family. It's a theorem for one of the most attacked problems in computer science. SHA-256 has no theorem like that. Its security is that nobody has broken it yet, which is exactly the standard the post refuses
to extend to lattices.

If you actually want to worry about structure in lattices, then look at the algebra of rings and ideal lattices. Cramer, Ducas, Peikert, and Regev (2016) and Cramer, Ducas, and Wesolowski (2017) gave quantum attacks on Ideal-SVP in cyclotomic fields. Albrecht, Bai, Ducas, and Kirchretched NTRU. Those results killed real schemes, and none of them touch ML-KEM or ML-DSA, which are module schemes with small moduli. Ducas, Plançon, and Wesolowski showed the quantum ideal attack does worse than plain BKZ at every dimension, applied the structure, measured how far the attacks reach, standardized outside their range, kept FrodoKEM with no ring at all, and added HQC in 2025 so KEMs don't rest on lattices alone. Vitalik is either unaware of this or hash-crypto bagholding is causing citation amnesia.

Then there's the claim that hashes are "intended" to have no structure, as if intent were a security proof. Differential cryptanalysis destroyed both MD5 and SHA-1 by attacking their round functions, with no help from P = NP. Of every family he lists, hashes are the only one whose deployed primitives have actually been broken. And the hash-only roadmap he's defending runs on Poseidon and Poseidon2, low-degree polynomial maps over small prime fields, built specifically to be easy to express algebraically. They are the most algebraically structured hashes anyone has ever put into production. Gröbner-basis and interpolation attacks are an active research area, and the Ethereum Foundation even funded a cryptanalysis bounty on Poseidon because of it. If AI is going to eat structure, Poseidon gets eaten long before Module-LWE. 

The proof systems are no better. FRI, STIR, and WHIR at aggressive parameters rest on Reed-Solomon proximity-gap conjectures nobody has proven, and Fiat-Shamir is argued in the random oracle model. That's what "hash-only" actually means in practice. And "we'd pad the round count first" gives the game away, because extra rounds only defend against structure. He's admitting the structure is there.

The theory gets mangled too. Impagliazzo and Rudich is a black-box separation about proof techniques. It is not a theorem that public-key encryption "needs structure," and Merkle's puzzles already give hash-only key agreement with a quadratic gap, which Barak and Mahmoody showed is optimal in that model. "P ≠ NP so hashes are safe" is wrong as well, because P ≠ NP doesn't imply one-way functions exist, let alone that SHA-256 is one. That gap is the entire subject of Impagliazzo's five worlds. And the claim that an object with zero known structures is safer than one with exactly three is a probability claim with no underlying probability model for generic prime-field elliptic curves; the record runs the other way: every subexponential ECDLP attack since 1985 needed a special curve; everyone identified and excluded it, and Shoup's generic-group bound says precisely what a new attack would have to exploit. Nobody has found one in forty years.

"Multiply key sizes by ten" is numerology. Lattice attack cost goes like 2^(c·β). A better constant means you scale dimension by c/c', so a 20 percent improvement costs you about 25 percent more dimension, not 10x. A subexponential break means no multiplier saves you, because 10^n is still subexponential. Neither case gives you ten. Bytes aren't even a security parameter, since raising the modulus at fixed noise can make LWE easier. Parameter selection is a complexity formula set against a security target, and this post contains no formula.

"AI will deliver fifty years of math in two years" isn't a threat model. It names no algorithm or cost, and it can never be falsified, because every year without a break is just "not yet." It also cuts against hashes at least as hard as against lattices, and the post never explains why it shouldn't. 

The field already has a working process for extraordinary claims. In 2024, a preprint claimed a quantum polynomial-time algorithm for LWE, and the bug was found in about ten days. Rainbow and SIKE fell on laptops during the NIST process, under the same public scrutiny that let the lattice schemes survive. An AI-found attack follows the same process: check it, run it through the estimators, and reparameterize. Abandoning the most studied post-quantum family before an attack exists is panic.

And the advice is actively dangerous outside of crypto Twitter. He concedes public-key encryption can't be avoided, then tells TLS, Tor, VPN, and messaging operators to get "much more paranoid" about the only post-quantum KEM that is actually deployed. Harvest-now-decrypt-later is happening right now, and hybrid ML-KEM, already shipping in browsers and messengers, is the defense. Spreading doubt about it, or bloating it tenfold until handshakes break, keeps traffic on classical crypto longer, which is the outcome he says he's worried about. "Send encrypted notes offchain through a third party" fixes nothing, because delivering to someone you'venever spoken to still needs public-key encryption, and now you've added a trusted party that sees your metadata and can drop your messages. Lumping ML-DSA and FHE into one bucket shows a weak grasp of both, since they live in completely different parameter regimes with different attacks.

Use hash-based signatures where they fit; the IETF has worked on XMSS for years, and there have been many great advancements. They are an algebraic dead end, however. You can't easily do the things we treasure in the elliptic-curve world. 

Security engineering means naming the attack, costing it, and sizing the fix within the context of broader business and technological objectives. Vitalik never does this. He writes these damn posts that convince lots of engineers to abandon incredibly important research, and then we have to stumble back to it after years of false starts: Plasma, Ethereum 2.0, Casper, Accounts, etc etc etc. Now we are going to attack Lattices.
author: veH0rny
quoted_text:
I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today. But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously, and minimize our exposure to not just quantum-vulnerable cryptography, but also potentially AI-vulnerable cryptography.

The core new area of risk from this viewpoint is, unfortunately, ML-DSA / FHE / lattices.

(and it's also another reason, along with quantum, why ECDSA might fall even faster than expected, hence the "fresh address" recommendation)

So far most people have been in the mode of thinking "elliptic curves broken, hashes safe, lattices safe". But there is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math.

The basic threat model is: factoring is something that naively takes 2^(n/2) time, but over decades smart people have found and optimized number field sieves, and degraded that to 2^O(n^(1/3)), which is why RSA keys and signatures need to be ~400 bytes (and not 64 bytes). What if there are skeletons in the closet like that, both for elliptic curves and lattices, that we are simply not smart enough to discover - but bots soon will be?

This is a major part of the reason why for the past year ethereum's lean roadmap has been going in the "hash-only" direction: no lattices, no ML-DSA, no Falcon, no lattice-based commitments inside ZK proofs, etc. Signatures in lean ethereum are all hash-based, either WOTS or SPHINCS-.

For signatures and proofs, we already know how to go hash-only. The bigger challenge is for *public-key encryption* - and this goes far beyond blockchains. Secure communication, anonymizing protocols, lots of things need public-key encryption.

And unfortunately there are long-standing mathematical theorems showing why public-key encryption cannot be done with hashes alone. You have to have some kind of trapdoor object that has at least one form of usable "structure" - either group theory (incl. isogenies) or lattices or code-based or potentially in the future even more newfangled and spooky things (local mixing?). But for anything that has structure, you should assume that AI will make at least some progress in breaking that structure. Here, one reasonable inference is that if you want to make something plausibly long-term secure, multiply the key sizes by 10.

To me that's a very plausible world and something not at all extreme to predict. If AI will bring us 50 years of math in 2 years, then that 50 years of math may very plausibly include a "naive factoring -> GNFS" level of improvement to our ability to break lattices. In that world, lattices will still exist, but they will have to be significantly bigger to guarantee the same level of safety.

And at those new larger sizes, hash-based constructions will beat lattice-based constructions on concrete efficiency in every use case where hash-based constructions are possible at all.

Theoretically, of course it's possible that hashes are broken too (eg. P = NP would imply that). But I think P = NP is very unlikely. And intuitively, it's much more likely that a mathematical object has exactly no exploitable structure (like hashes are intended to), than that a mathematical object has exactly ~3 forms of exploitable structure (for elliptic curves: associativity, Schoof, pairings) and not some secret fourth form of structure we have not yet discovered that greatly degrades its security (for elliptic curves, ECDLP and pairing security). Similar for LWE, SVP, RLWE and the zoo of lattice problems.

For this reason, we do not yet see any reason to worry and start padding the byte size of hashes (if we start to worry more, we would pad the round count first before doing anything to the byte size).

Concrete TLDR, my own personal views:

* Hash-based > lattice-based, in those situations where hash-based is possible at all
* For anything lattice-based, be much more paranoid on param sizes. Remember that blockchains are only a small portion of the cryptography story; this point goes far beyond blockchains and applies to eg. access to websites, secure messaging, Tor / VPNs ...
* For privacy protocols, strongly favor NOT putting encrypted notes onchain. Instead, send them offchain through some third-party mechanism.
* If it's not difficult for you, keeping your funds in addresses which have not yet been used to make a transaction is a good idea. If it's easy for you, do it. **But be careful about migrations; I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined**.
* For multisig wallets, doing confirmations offchain is better than onchain, because this way the signatures of signer wallets do not get exposed to the public, so if ECDSA falls to AI much faster than expected, at least the multisig "gracefully degrades" to a 1-of-1 where the 1 is whoever was gathering the signatures - a much better place to be than "anyone can take the money"

特朗普给六位科技公司掌门人颁发美国国家奖章

美国总统特朗普 10 月 8 日在白宫颁发了两项国家奖章。Google 联合创始人 Sergey Brin、英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋、SpaceX 和特斯拉 CEO 马斯克、AMD CEO 苏姿丰获得国家科学奖章；戴尔创始人 Michael Dell、微软 CEO Satya Nadella 获得国家技术与创新奖章。

这两项奖章是美国政府给科技界的最高荣誉，由总统亲自颁发。国家科学奖章 1959 年设立，过去获奖的大多是大学和研究机构里的科学家；国家技术与创新奖章表彰把技术做成产品和产业的人。这是特朗普两届任期里第一次颁发这两项奖章。

颁奖词给出了每个人的理由。

Brin 获奖是因为开发了信息检索和数据处理的基础算法，也就是 Google 搜索背后的那套方法，改变了人们获取信息的方式。

黄仁勋获奖是因为把 GPU 从画图形的芯片变成了通用计算平台，让大规模并行计算成为可能。今天训练大模型用的就是这套东西。

马斯克获奖是因为在航天、智能系统和通信上的工程成就，以及推动美国制造业回流。

苏姿丰获奖是因为处理器架构和芯粒技术（把一颗大芯片拆成几块小芯片拼起来，成本更低、性能更容易往上堆），这套技术撑起了全球第一台百亿亿次超级计算机，也就是每秒能算一百亿亿次的机器。

Dell 获奖是因为建立了一家全球性的科技公司，并资助培养年轻的科学家和工程师。

Nadella 获奖是因为带着微软转型云计算重新焕发活力，并建起超大规模数据中心，颁奖词的说法是这些数据中心让“美国超级智能”得以训练和在全球部署。

这份名单基本就是你每天用的 AI 背后的那条产业链：搜索和模型、训练芯片、服务器、云算力。颁奖词里两次出现“超级智能”，白宫把 AI 算力当成了国家实力来表彰。

特朗普在颁奖时称马斯克是“当代爱迪生”。两人去年公开闹翻，美国媒体把这次授奖看作两人和解的信号。

quoted_text:
So not to go all Yudkowsky Monocause Theory.  But a lot of AI company talk that *sounds smart* did come from me, or me via Bostrom or other diffusion modes.  High-powered ideas like "recursive self-improvement" and "AGI" are ideas they did not invent themselves, but got off higher-quality outside thinkers.  There's a big intellectual history behind me in turn, but the AI companies did not study this history independently; they got it downstream of my writing it up.

I naturally spent some time trying to figure out what the positive vision for AGI and ASI would look like, back in the mid-2000s.

But I considered it a lower priority to write up.

And AI company executives are not at the intellectual level where they can invent coherent answers to questions like that, if they don't have my answer sheet to copy from.

They can't tell you what the positive vision for AGI or ASI looks like, because I didn't prioritize writing up that part of my earlier thoughts.  They can't copy it off from the same answer sheet they used to produce smart-sounding conversation like "general intelligence" or "recursive self-improvement" or "extinction risk" or "AI alignment problem".

If they're not reading off my answer sheet, AI company executives are pretty ordinary as intellectuals.  Being able to spend billions on GPUs does not make you a genius inventor, even if we're used to amazing inventions coming from genius rather than black-box optimization.  AI company executives are not going to give you better answers about "what's the positive vision" than any other random intellectual challenged with a question beyond their wits.

If you start hearing good-sounding answers from Anthropic or OpenAI, it means that Mythos or HPIM advanced to the point of learning how to sound convincing about utopia to humans.

I did do an *abstract* writeup on constraints and requirements over positive ASI scenarios (see eg "31 Laws of Fun"); but that does AI companies no good, because they would need to be able to sketch a concrete AGI scenario from those abstract ideas.  That again is beyond them if I have not done their homework.

It is of course not in humanity's interest that I try to do this homework for the AI companies now.  It would only be a lie.  They have no utopia to offer.

Nick Bostrom explains why pausing AI could accidentally create a secret Manhattan Project for superintelligence:

"I'm sympathetic to this idea of pacing the frontier. I think that would be net good. I am a little less excited about the rhetoric of stopping AI or pausing AI."

"There's nothing more permanent than a temporary government program. If you set up this apparatus to control AI, to get this to happen in the first place, you have to really create huge antagonism against AI. You could imagine things getting locked in."

"This is all before we've actually seen anything bad happening, right? Before there's any big labor market impact, before any catastrophe has happened."

"One natural way would be to stop it in the civilian sector and then push ahead hard in a sort of secret government program. It concentrates more power in fewer stakeholders, makes it less transparent."

"I don't think I have a fixed conviction for this is the way things should go from now to superintelligence. We need to feel our way through, one oar stroke at a time."

text:
Solana 上的 Hook 叙事，不是 Uniswap v4 那套池子回调，而是把规则写进代币转账本身。主线是 Token-2022 的 transfer hook，再叠一层发射台，让 meme 发射时自带防狙击、销毁、持币分红，而不是毕业后靠网站或机器人继续执行。

和以太坊 Hook 的差别
以太坊 v4 的 hook 挂在池子上。创建时写进 PoolKey，在 swap、加减流动性前后插入逻辑，可以改费率甚至改定价。Solana 原生对应物是 Token-2022 transfer hook：mint 指定一个程序，每一笔转账（买入、卖出、钱包互转）都会调用它。转账违反规则就直接失败。规则在链上，不依赖发射台网站一直在线。

这带来一个硬限制。标准 transfer hook 基本只能说 yes 或 no，不能从这笔交易里切一块出来销毁或打给持币人。钱包互转和池子交易在转账层看起来一样，所以「只对买卖收费、互转不收费」做不干净。Solana 上现在的叙事，就是在补这个缺口。

现在实际在讲的三层
1. 协议层：Token-2022 transfer hook

这是底料，不是新发明。Hooked 的文档写得很直白：发射时选定规则，例如单钱包持仓不超过 1%、或只允许钱包互转；Solana 在转账内部执行；发射方和平台事后都不能关掉。毕业（graduation）才是少数能拿掉 hook 的路径，而且只对会毕业的曲线生效。少数类型标明可改：创建者可编辑、持币人 DAO 投票、或交给 AI agent。

2. 发射层：把 hook 产品化

这是 2026 年 9 月底到 10 月才热起来的交易叙事，项目都还很小。

Hooked（@Hoookedpad，https://t.co/UcUdZ4VN0O）在 Meteora bonding curve 上发币。预设包括持仓上限、水下回血（每 5 分钟把手续费锅按浮亏比例打给还没回本的持币人）。10 月 8 日他们又推了「Hooked standard」：自建 token program、DEX 和发射台，声称 hook 不再只返回 yes/no，而是返回金额，从而在每笔交易上给持币人打 SOL、销毁一部分、或付给创建者，并且毕业后规则仍在。同时上了 AI 写 hook，编译器检查后再发射。平台币 HOOKED 的 Meteora 池大约只有数万美元流动性，属于早期盘，不是基础设施龙头。
Hooker（@hookerdotfun）走另一条分发：在 https://t.co/ZJG4fAamwc 和 Pons 上给发射加规则，并做 Meteora 到 https://t.co/ZJG4fAamwc 的毕业上限自定义，也可以选择一直留在 Meteora、hook 不摘。关注度更低。
周边还有 Ember 这类前端在喊「先上 Meteora，下一步上 hooks」，本质仍是发射分发，不是新 AMM。
3. 流动性层：Meteora，不是 hook 本身

Solana 发射的钱大多流过 Meteora 的 DBC（动态 bonding curve）、DLMM 和 DAMM v2。10 月 6 日 Meteora 发布 DLMM Pro：费率随市场成熟递减、LP 仓位 NFT 化、发射参数可配，目前还在 waitlist。这是「可定制 AMM」，和 transfer hook 相邻，但不是同一个机制。Meteora 才是这条链上有真实费用的资产；hook 发射台还在抢叙事。

作为对照，DexPaprika 10 月 9 日口径下 Meteora 三套程序 24 小时成交约 6.9 亿美元，其中 DAMM v2 约 4.67 亿美元。Hooked 自己的池子是万美元级。

叙事在卖什么
卖点就一句：https://t.co/qTudXY3cf9 式发射规则太单一，毕业后税率、销毁、持仓上限全靠项目方自觉；hook 让规则在转账时强制执行，毕业后仍在。玩法模板已经在抄以太坊那套：防狙击费、持有越久卖出税越低、越跌销毁越多、单日卖出上限、持币人 SOL 分红、水下补贴。

和 v4 的关键差异是价值捕获位置。以太坊 hook 吃的是池子手续费和自定义曲线；Solana 这波吃的是发射注意力和代币自带的转账税。平台币能不能分到这些税，要逐个合约看，不能默认「有 hook 就有平台税」。10 月 1 日还有一份针对 Hooked 的指控复核：约 2080 SOL 来自 HOOKED 自己曲线和毕业后流动性仓位的创建者手续费，不是从发射台 flywheel 里转走的。说明这个赛道已经开始打费用归属战。

怎么看
Solana 的 Hook 是 meme 发射规则层，不是 Uniswap v4 的池子可编程层。能对标的是「Token-2022 + 发射台」，不是「自定义 AMM」。Meteora 是流动性底座，Hooked / Hooker 是在上面贴规则的前端和代币标准实验。

跟踪时只看三件事：规则是不是毕业后仍由 token program 执行，而不是网站开关；hook 能不能改金额，还是只能拒绝转账；手续费进的是平台金库、创建者钱包，还是持币人。AI 写 hook 会把恶意或写错的规则规模化，以太坊上 hook 合约大量不安全的问题，在这里会换成「转账直接失败或税被抽走」。

👉 继续这个手动循环

text:
很多人说太空 AI 算力集群没必要，但谷歌告诉你，其实很有必要。
谷歌一年花 2000 亿美元在地面建算力集群，但是在 美国时间10 月 1 日，搭载 SpaceX 猎鹰 9 号的Transporter-18运载任务，发射了 AI 算力实验卫星。之所以要做这个实验，就是在为未来搭建太空 AI 算力集群做准备。
逻辑很简单，就问两个问题，人类对 AI 算力的需求，是地面 AI 算力集群足够满足的吗？在地面上建 AI 算力集群，是越来越容易，还是越来越难？
我的观点是，在太空里建 AI 算力集群就是个早晚的事。
谷歌做过测算，如果太空运载成本达到 一公斤200 美元，太空算力集群就有机会跑通。目前全地球所有航天公司最低的运载成本超过 一公斤1500 美元。只有 Starship，有机会做到一公斤 80 美元。可以说，SpaceX 卡住了太空 AI 算力集群的咽喉，一旦这个领域火起来，SpaceX必然是最大的受益者之一。
对于谷歌这次发射的 AI 实验卫星，以及 SpaceX在太空 AI 算力集群里的位置，我做了一期视频详细做了分析，感兴趣的朋友们欢迎观看。

"逢会必跌"在币圈快成玄学了。

最主要的还是买预期、卖事实。
会前几周,政策表态、机构进场这些故事已经被交易进价格,等台上真讲出来,只要没超出预期,手里有利润的人就顺手走了。台上说的多半是大家早知道的东西,"没惊喜"本身就够当卖出理由。

杠杆负责放大。
会前追涨的多头不少开了杠杆,第一波回落点着强平线,连环爆仓把普通回调砸成大阴线。会期里交易员都在现场社交,盘口变薄,同样的卖单冲击也更大。

但开会本身其实没那么大能量。
还有被忽略的一点：
跌了的会大家都记得,平平无奇的会没人提,"必跌"里有不少是记忆筛出来的。

我现在把大会当成一个偏空的波动窗口:会前涨得多、资金费率偏高、宏观在收紧。

真有超预期的东西落地,照样能涨。

text:
如果说 SWIFT 共享账本的推出只是一次支付系统升级，那么它的重要性将仅限于技术层面。然而，从数字金融发展趋势来看，这项实验真正值得关注之处，在于它重新定义了未来机构级数字资产流通的基础设施竞争。随着 Token 化存款、共享账本及可编程结算逐步进入现实应用，传统金融机构开始将自身长期积累的银行信用、监管体系及全球清算网络引入 Web3 生态。这意味着，未来数字金融竞争的核心将不再只是“谁能够发行一种新的数字货币”，而是“谁能够成为机构资金流动、资产流转以及全球金融互操作性的底层基础设施”。

因此，SWIFT 共享账本的影响远不止于提升跨境支付效率，它正在改变传统银行、Web3 基础设施提供商以及 Web3 原生支付网络之间的竞争关系。过去几年，原生 Web3 项目依靠开放网络率先建立起数字资产流通体系；而如今，以 SWIFT 为代表的传统金融基础设施开始借助 Token 化技术进入同一赛道，双方的竞争也从应用层逐渐下沉到金融基础设施层。

SWIFT 共享账本的落地，意味着传统金融机构并未在 Web3 时代放弃自身长期占据的支付与清算优势，而是开始围绕 Token 化存款重新争夺未来数字货币体系中的核心入口。过去几年，稳定币的发展一度让市场认为，未来跨境支付可能逐渐脱离商业银行体系，转而建立在由私人机构发行的链上数字货币网络之上。然而，随着 JPMorgan、花旗银行、汇丰银行等大型金融机构相继推出 Token 化存款及相关基础设施，传统银行正在尝试证明：未来机构级数字支付并不一定需要脱离商业银行，而可以建立在商业银行负债本身的 Token 化之上。

例如，摩根大通（JPMorgan）推出了 JPM Coin，并依托其 Onyx（现已更名为 Kinexys）平台，为机构客户提供基于区块链的账户管理及 Token 化存款服务；花旗银行（Citi）、汇丰银行（HSBC）等国际银行也分别围绕 Token 化存款、数字现金以及可编程支付展开持续测试。这些实践表明，传统银行并非被动应对 Web3，而是在主动争夺下一代数字金融体系中最重要的资产发行权和清算入口。

以上内容摘自外捕研究（Web3Caff Research）《SWIFT 共享账本专项研报（下篇）：传统金融启动最大 Web3 基础设施实验，全球金融体系将迎来怎样的变革？全景式拆解其发展背景、运行机制、终极愿景、潜在挑战及未来展望》

text:
彼得·蒂尔嫌硅谷造 AI 的人没信仰。可教皇真的出来谈 AI 伦理，他又嫌人家管得太宽。

10 月 8 日，《Nashville Scene》披露了 Thiel 在纳什维尔第二场「敌基督」演讲的更多录音内容。

其中有句话很有意思：

「硅谷制造 AI 的人，几乎没有其他信仰，能够帮助他们在讨论技术时找到立足点，或者保持必要的距离。」

Thiel 似乎认为，硅谷的问题在于太相信技术了。工程师每天讨论模型能力、Scaling、超级智能，却缺乏一套能够超越技术本身的价值体系，来判断自己究竟在创造什么。

但有趣的是，同一天 Politico 披露的另一批演讲内容中，他又猛烈抨击教皇利奥十四世，指责教皇借助公众对 AI 的恐惧获取政治支持。他还将以 AI 安全为理由建立的全球性监管权威，与自己所担忧的「敌基督」联系起来。

而就在最近，Anthropic 正在邀请神父、拉比和其他宗教思想家讨论 Claude 的意识与道德地位，试图从古老的宗教传统中寻找训练 AI 的伦理依据。

这几件事放在一起看，非常有意思。

硅谷正在重新发现宗教的价值，但围绕宗教的分歧也越来越明显。

Anthropic 希望将宗教智慧引入模型的价值判断，教皇希望通过公共规则约束 AI 企业，而 Thiel 一面强调信仰的重要性，一面又极度警惕以道德和安全之名形成的集中权力。

他们都在谈论技术与道德，真正发生冲突的地方，是谁有资格定义道德，以及谁有权将道德变成规则。

我越来越觉得，Thiel 这套神学政治最值得怀疑的地方就在这里。

他要求硅谷建立超越技术的价值参照，但如果这套价值体系最终要求硅谷放慢 AI 的开发速度，甚至牺牲一部分商业利益，他是否还愿意接受？

倘若信仰只能用来批评工程师的精神贫乏，却不能真正约束技术公司的权力，那么这样的信仰，究竟在保护什么？

The internet’s business model was built around people: attention, ads, subscriptions and checkout. AI agents are changing that. They can retrieve and use content without sending a human reader back to the publisher.

That raises a real question for creators, publishers and developers: how can they get paid when an agent uses their work, sometimes for a fraction of a cent?

Our new Coinbase Institute @CoinbaseCBI paper, "Machine-to-machine payments in the AiFi era," examines why existing payment rails often struggle with high-velocity microtransactions—and why stablecoins on low-cost networks are a strong fit today.

The policy goal should be an open, interoperable payment layer, with safeguards that match the risks—not closed marketplaces that decide who can participate.

text:
"The 8 hours" is a trap.

A 2024 study in the journal Sleep tracked over 38,000 people and landed on something simple: sleep regularity predicts mortality better than sleep duration. Eight hours at irregular times carries more risk than six hours at consistent times.

@sleepagotchi is built around that. It tracks two repair windows separately, 11pm to 3am and 3am to 6am. So it's not asking whether you slept. It's asking whether your recovery windows were covered.

Most sleep apps track duration. You slept this many hours, here's your score, close the app. But duration is the outcome. Regularity is the cause. You can't control when your body naturally wakes. You can control when you put the phone down.

Kenny Wood said it plainly in an interview: sleep is the root of almost every health issue. Which is why Sleepagotchi didn't stop at sleep. Four AI agents run on the phone. Sleep Coach reads the night. Wellness Coach checks mood and diet through the day. Meal Planner turns it into food. Shopping Agent acts on it.

All of it runs locally. Biometrics never leave the handset, not to the cloud, not to a chain. They planned an on-chain data marketplace and killed it because wearable TOS and the legal reality made it unworkable.

500k+ registered users. Around 80k daily actives. Token moved from $SLEEP to $CHI. Marketplace and credit sinks still aren't live.

So right now there's one working agent. But it's tracking the thing that actually sits upstream of duration.

Tonight I'm not setting a wake-up alarm. Just a bedtime reminder.

Immutable, permissionless and with the core protocol running onchain, anon.wei is a strong new addition to the privacy toolset.

Main differences vs. popular tools:

Tornado Cash:
- Arbitrary amounts
- Reusable balances
- Private internal transfers

Privacy Pools:
- No ASP / compliance check
- Fewer protocol-level dependencies

FluidKey/Cloaked:
- No central operator seeing the flow

The main downside of being new: the anonymity set is still small.

The UI is a bit loaded but still clear.

It helps grow the anonymity set, and I’m sure you’ll find some interesting use cases for it.

大家好，我是 ZK，OpenETF 的 Co-founder。

我很少在 X 上讲自己，今天讲讲我的故事，以及为什么建设 https://t.co/2mDA9D1fl5。

这是个老故事，但今天有新内容。刚好 10 年前，2016 年的国庆节，ofo 做了一个历史性的决定：要不要在国庆假期结束后，把仅在校园运营的共享单车放在城市街头提供服务。

后面的故事大家都知道了，那个国庆节的决定让 ofo 登上历史舞台。

国庆节结束，我作为 day 1 参与 ofo 的创立成员、PKU 校友，以及团队中为数不多有工作经验（两年）的人，接手了 ofo 的 GTM 重任，负责增长营销、品牌战略、品牌传播、公关。

作为两年奥美广告、本科学生物的新手，边学边干，学增长，学营销方法，学独角兽公司打仗。摸索着从 0 到 1 构建了共享单车新客增长模型。

当时竞争格局是熟悉的剧本，老大老二一决雌雄目标并购对方，顺便干掉老三及其他，因此共享单车的新客增长模型可以抽象为——「货架上两种可乐二选一的决策场景」，用户先选红色可乐，还是先选蓝色的；城市街头就是货架，同样两款车，新客先选黄色单车，还是先选其他颜色。

一个内核是快消品的共享单车增长模型诞生了：
- research（定性洞察、定量统计，分析用户心理和决策模型）
- 定位战略（特劳特：一个符号占据用户心智）
- brand mkt/marcomm（认知、兴趣、偏好、品牌忠诚度）
- 包装（车身改装、车身图案、挂件配件定制）
- 陈列（线下运营调度，成为离用户最近的那辆车，局部的竞争优势）
- 场景提示（货架附近的场景营销，车身挂签、地铁、公交、写字楼楼宇广告）
- 促销策略（抓手）
- APP 环节的转化漏斗优化（与快消品模型的不同之处）

好的战略+优秀的执行，一套连招下来，不赢都难。

结果是一年花了 1 亿美金，搞了 2 亿用户，份额第一名，ofo 的营销案例被写入商学院的教科书。

增长模型的部分商学院没写，因为我没对外分享过。

那年我 26 岁，觉得自己牛逼得要死。

后来我做 founder 才意识到，创业要比当高管难 100 倍。要学的实在太多了，这一学就是十年。

第一课。

「产品不够完美，你愿不愿意带着这些问题先走到用户面前？」

广告人有个毛病，对审美、调性、taste 有要求，对「作品」有执念，再叠加做题家身份，自我要求和期待直接拉满。很多时间都花在优化上。

作为 founder 早晚都要面对一个现实，“打磨”有时候时候是一种推辞，完美主义、高期待、贬损同行竞品都是同理。就是怕面对真实用户，怕解决真实问题，怕被评判，怕被比较，怕当草台，本质上是害怕直面失败，这是很多创始人最大的心魔。

回看十年前的黄色自行车，民用自行车架结构脆弱，充气轮胎漏气就不能骑，四位数机械密码锁、没有定位，记住密码约等于车归你了...对于复杂的城市路况和社会环境，每一项都是草台配置。

十年前能做出进城市的决定，准备直面无数挑战和问题，而不是闭门优化，这是顶级魄力。

今天看来，勇气只是副产品，共享单车真实地解决最后一公里出行问题。

「满足真需求」是创业的第一性原理。而满足真需求的产品也会帮助创始人抵抗恐惧。

战略上胜利，才不必在战术上卖力。

另外，我还是相信好的 taste 一定会给我回报，sooner or later。

第二课是，太早学会了烧钱。

这烧钱我不得不学。ofo GTM 前后我去股东机构经纬创投开会，合伙人给我讲滴滴 Uber 打仗、讲美团点评合并、讲外卖大战、讲老大如何兼并老二。他对我说，如果我学不会烧钱，就提议戴老板换掉我。

故事的结局全国人民都知道了，虽然烧出几亿用户、烧出一家独角兽、烧出第一名，但还是遗憾落幕。

那时候书生气重，责任心重。之后好几年团队还一直反思，是不是对资本、对钱缺乏敬畏。

当然现在想明白了，成功合并就是史诗，是新四大发明。合并失败就是浪费。这是游戏规则，是 playbook。另一方面宏观环境确实变了，有增量的时候要激进增长，存量博弈的时候必须精细化运营、收敛扩张。这些 learnings 可能等 https://t.co/2mDA9D1fl5 到独角兽的时候才用的上，先 mark 住。

自己创业完全是另一回事，缺钱才是创业的常态。缺钱怎么做增长这课正在恶补，不过好在学习能力还可以，好在有很多好老师好榜样。

这第三课是突破自我的思想束缚。

第一份工作是广告公关，第一次创业做的也是增长营销的工作，可以说是干传播起家的，但我很少营销和展示自己。

除了包袱重、面子薄、骄傲，也喜欢低调谦逊，想靠产品靠作品，觉得酒香不怕巷子深，可能也想装个大的。

另一方面作为一名理科生，确实发自内心欣赏搞数学的韦东奕、搞物理的 @chameleon_jeff 、搞代码的 @cz_binance 、搞工程物理的 @elonmusk 这帮理工男的低调+有点 nerd 的 vibe。

不过当我看到 CZ 都开始脱衣服了，我的学长 @justinsuntron 百无禁忌大开大合，我还装什么呢。

得入局。

第四课是创业方向，为什么是 OpenETF on Hyperliquid

年轻时经历过惊艳的人和事确实是一种诅咒。我对不够颠覆、不够创新的东西不再分泌多巴胺了。

所以会对电子烟、人造培育钻石、Backpack、Hyperliquid 这种东西上头。

你被什么感召，什么就是你的命。「创业选方向」这种叙述本身就是错的，因为真正创新、颠覆性的方向根本就不是选出来的，你是被召唤的。

其次是找到真需求、真痛点。回顾过去十年的创业和职业经历，正反馈最强的业务是 2023 年下半年做的一支私募基金：买到了 $28,000 的 BTC、$60 的 SOL、$5 的 HYPE。

最强的正反馈，也伴随着最强的痛点：

- 做一支基金的门槛太高
- 好的策略没能被更多人看到
- 人与人之间的信任成本太高
- 募资规模受限

在传统金融里，基金是一种特权。牌照、人员资质、运营、审计，每一项都是准入门槛，很重，也很贵。

无论是否合规，投资人只要把资金交给基金管理人，就必然有信任成本，资金和数据的状态都要打上问号：跑路、挪用、超出风险边界的交易、对敲、老鼠仓、虚报净值……

投资人看到的往往只是 PPT 上的收益曲线。尤其是通过 API 接入的量化策略，验证历史业绩的成本很高；反过来，量化团队也只能依赖投资人守信、按约支付费用。

归结起来是两个痛点：门槛成本高，信任成本高。

再总结为一个字，就是「贵」。

带着这些痛点，直到遇见另一个惊艳的项目 Hyperliquid，我意识到这些痛点终于可以用前所未有的方式解决。

HyperCore（链上订单簿）和 HyperEVM（智能合约层）共享同一套 HyperBFT 共识，两者之间没有跨链桥，以全链上、去信任的方式原生互通：合约可以持有资产、读取 HyperCore 状态，并直接向 HyperCore 发出交易指令。

这让一种新的基金形态第一次成为可能，OpenETF 把它实现出来：

- 同一个 Vault 合约，在 HyperEVM 上是 ETF 的金库，负责募资、发行份额、付款；
- 在 HyperCore 上是基金的交易账户，持有整个投资组合。从申购、交易到赎回付款，资金全程不下链；
- 每一次申赎的定价都在同一笔交易里直接读取链上状态，不依赖任何外部价格源或平台报价。

在这个底座之上，OpenETF 把发行、投资和管理一支基金需要的东西做成了一套产品：

1. 任何基金管理人（个人、机构、agent）都可以把 HyperCore 交易组合和 HyperEVM DeFi 组合打包成一支 ETF。

现货篮子、多空策略、中性套利、观点表达（L Hype/S ETH）、杠杆代币、DeFi+订单簿+outcome 复合投资组合...everything。

2. 投资人通过持有 ETF 的份额，持有这支 ETF 的整个投资组合。

3. ETF 份额是 ERC-20 代币，有自己的 ticker，投资人按 NAV 申购、赎回，份额可以在钱包之间自由转让；有流动性时可以在二级市场买卖，未来还可以抵押借贷。

4. 基金资产由 Vault 合约持有，管理人只能指挥交易，没有提币权限，跑路和挪用在结构上不可能发生。

5. OpenETF 提供申赎、会计、基金生命周期管理、交易执行和风控组件，降低管理人的管理成本和投资人的信任成本。

基金的形态会发生根本性的转变：从一种带有特权属性的金融工具，变成链上金融原语。

开放、可组合，任何人都可以参与，任何人都可以发行，任何人都可以验证。

任何 trader 都可以无缝成为 ETF manager，各种 ETF 会在所有地方保持流动。

这就是 OpenETF，only possible on Hyperliquid。

这就是我，在 build 的东西定义了我。

——

感谢有机会向老师们介绍我和在做的事情，期待跟大家有更深入的熟悉和交流！

期待 OpenETF 可以满足 trader、agent、机构等基金管理人以及投资人的真需求，欢迎讨论！

text:
我们是不是高估了 Harness 对 Coding Agent「能力」的提升？

这篇论文中把模型固定，只替换 Claude Code、mini-SWE-agent 和 OpenCode，在 SWE-bench Verified 上重新测试。

结果很有意思。

在 447 个任务上，最重的 Claude Code 和最轻的 mini-SWE-agent，成绩差异落在 5 个百分点以内。

在 45 个高难任务、5 个模型上，换 Harness 会让 13% 的任务结果发生变化；但什么都不改，只把同一个配置再跑一遍，同样有 13% 的任务会翻转。

也就是说，很多看起来像 Harness 带来的提升，可能还没有明显超过运行本身的随机波动。

真正拉开差距的反而是成本。

同一个模型、同一批任务，不同 Harness 的单任务成本最高能差 3 倍。主要原因很简单：系统 Prompt 和工具 schema 会在每一步重复进入上下文，初始开销再被执行步数不断放大。

论文还提醒了一个容易被忽略的问题：

45 个任务连 13 个百分点的差距都只有约一半概率能检出；即使做到 447 个任务，分辨率也大约只有 5 个百分点。

所以我们得把 Harness 的价值拆开看了。

它当然会影响 Agent 怎么工作，但很多时候，最稳定、最容易测出来的差异，可能先体现在 token、成本和执行效率上。

这次回调，我最关注的不是跌了多少，而是：

为什么只跌了这么多。
最近宏观面的利空其实不少。

30年美债收益率接近5.7，10年期在5.3附近；年内再加一次息的预期强化；油价、通胀压力重新起来；俄罗斯疑似鼠疫事件也带来了一些恐慌情绪。
放在过去，这里面很多消息单独出现，都足够BTC跌一波。
现在是几个利空一起出来，BTC也只回调了5%左右。
所以我一直觉得：
消息是表象，价格对消息的反应才是信息。
多数人做交易，其实都是被情绪主导。
涨的时候看到的全是利好，跌的时候看到的全是利空。
但只有少部分人，能从众多表象里面，把真正有用的信息找出来。

凡所有相，皆是虚妄。

当利空越来越多，价格却越来越跌不动的时候，本身就在说明一些事情。

这一点和5.8万那一次有点像，但又不完全一样。

5.8万的时候，是极度悲观以后，市场开始出现卖不动的迹象。

现在则是强趋势里面，宏观不断施压，但价格依然没有被真正打坏。

所以目前我不认为这里会直接跌到7.8，更不认为会到7.4。

但是交易不需要证明自己永远正确。

跌破7.9，我开始减仓。

日线收破7.8，剩下的多单全部离场。

没有跌破，就继续持有。
